deduped_items.summary: Le chef de la diplomatie française, Jean-Noël Barrot, est arrivé samedi 3 octobre dans la province orientale de l'Ituri (en République démocratique du Congo), l'épicentre de la plus grave épidémie d'Ebola de l'histoire de ce pays, a constaté l'AFP. deduped_items.title: "Affaires sensibles" : le combat d’un fils pour l’honneur du juge Renaud, dit "le Shérif", assassiné en 1975
deduped_items.summary: "C'est l'honneur de mon père, c'est devenu mon combat." Plus de cinquante ans après qu'on l'a trouvé sans vie devant leur domicile, le fils du juge Renaud n'a pas renoncé à obtenir la vérité : celui qui était surnommé "le Shérif" pour ses méthodes d'enquête musclées a-t-il été assassiné parce qu'il dérangeait le pouvoir de l'époque ?

deduped_items.title: Pakistan summons Indian envoy over killing of 2 civilians by border troops

deduped_items.body_text:
Pakistan summoned the Indian chargé d’affaires to lodge a strong protest over the killing of two Pakistani civilians by Indian Border Security Force (BSF) personnel in the Bedian sector along the international border, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Saturday.
Two unarmed Pakistani civilians were martyred and another was injured in firing by India’s BSF near the border in Kasur on Friday.
“The BSF personnel resorted to unprovoked and lethal force against unarmed civilians. Such use of force was wholly unjustified and grossly disproportionate, resulting in the tragic loss of two precious lives,” the FO said.
Pakistan categorically rejects any attempt to mischaracterise the deceased as “infiltrators”, it added.
The FO said the incident constituted a serious violation of fundamental human rights, including the right to life, and raised concerns over the protection of civilian life under international law.
It called on the Indian side to “conduct an immediate, transparent and credible investigation”, take appropriate disciplinary and legal action against those responsible, and formally communicate the findings and action taken to the government of Pakistan.
India was further urged to “respect fundamental human rights and international law, strictly observe relevant bilateral arrangements and established border procedures, exercise maximum restraint in such situations, and take effective measures to prevent similar incidents in the future”, the FO said.
The three civilians were residents of Ladhar village and had moved a few steps ahead of a border pillar when the BSF opened fire on them without warning. All three were unarmed.
The deceased were identified as Azmat Rasool and Mohsin Jutt, both residents of Jattan Wali Haveli, Ladhar. The injured civilian was taken for medical treatment.
According to security sources, none of the three men had attempted to cross the border fence, with the incident described as a violation of the border agreement and standard operating procedures governing the international border.
The development comes a day after Inter-Services Public Relations Director General Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry lampooned India’s claims of “neutralising” a “terrorist” allegedly linked to the Pakistani military, presenting the individual during a press conference.
Asked whether the recent allegations could trigger another armed conflict between the neighbours during the press briefing, he affirmed that Pakistan’s armed forces were always ready for any such move and warned of “very harsh” retribution.

deduped_items.body_text:
Allegations that the son of the Libyan warlord Khalifa Haftar oversaw a “terror cell” that launched drone attacks on fuel storage facilities and power stations in western Libya have upended plans for the Tripoli-based government of national unity (GNU) to continue cooperating with Haftar on a plan to unify the country.
Saddam Haftar, the deputy commander of the so-called Libyan National Army (LNA), has increasingly been seen by the US as an important figure in its plans to unify Libyan security, judicial and political institutions.
But a round of drone attacks in August worsened electricity blackouts in the west of the country, putting intense popular pressure on the GNU led by the prime minister, Abdul Hamid Dbeibah.
Libya has been split between the east, dominated by Haftar, and the west, governed by the GNU, since the fall of Col Muammar Gaddafi in 2011, leaving the oil-rich country at the mercy of corruption, militia, migrant traffickers and myriad external actors.
Donald Trump’s Africa adviser, Massad Boulos, has hatched a plan to unify the two Libyan governments in which Haftar from the east would take on the role of president and a member of the Dbeibah family from the west would become prime minister.
Boulos has insisted he is not trying a quick fix that entrenches family elites in Libya. “It’s not about families or names,” Boulos said when asked about the reported Haftar-Dbeibah deal, before adding: “At the end of the day, those are individuals that have to be in one position or the other.”
But the drone strikes, it is claimed, were prompted by Haftar’s anger at Dbeibah apparently stalling on the Boulos merger plan and by Tripoli allegedly encouraging tribes in southern Libya to attack and kill his forces.
Over more than five days in August, drones attacked the Zawiya oil station and fuel storage facilities in western Libya. The drone strikes hit the gasoline-storage tank at the Zawiya oil complex, west of Tripoli, causing a large fire and the tank’s collapse. The tank held approximately 4.5m litres of fuel when it was struck, according to Libya’s National Oil Corporation.
On 5 September, three Libyans and one Spanish citizen were arrested in southern Tripoli by the GNU for their alleged role in a plot that was intended to include an attack on Tripoli airport. It was thought the whole group involved five Spaniards and four Libyans. The three arrested Libyans were allegedly affiliated with the Tareq ben Ziyad brigade, an LNA formation. Information that has emerged from interviews about the plot, and Saddam Haftar’s alleged role, not just in Libya, has been described as a goldmine, capable of weakening Khalifa Haftar.
Sources in the GNU said the alleged plotters were working for Saddam Haftar. “No formal decision has been made, but in light of what has been discovered it is impossible to work with Saddam,” the sources said.
The claims not only damage Saddam Haftar’s role in the Boulos plan but also the parallel UN sponsored 4+4 talks involving the main four political institutions in Libya that led to an August agreement to stage elections within two years. The deal endorsed by the UN security council overcomes previous obstacles to elections, and had been backed by the main actors capable of delivering the change.
Walid Ellafi, minister for state for political affairs in the UN-backed Libyan GNU and an enthusiast for elections, said: “Our support for the 4+4 process is rooted in its role as a UN sponsored framework offering a new approach to achieving practical results that pave the way for elections and institutions whose political legitimacy derives from the will of the people – not as a political settlement that overlooks violations or sets aside the rights of those affected.”

deduped_items.body_text:
Michigan won the game on a Hail Mary and got dropped out of the AP Top 25 anyway. Why?
Michigan won the game against Western Michigan but lost most of its support in The Associated Press Top 25 college football poll.
Just like many viewers Saturday night, Top 25 voters were confused when one second was put back on the clock after it appeared time had run out at Michigan Stadium. And they were dazed when JJ Buchanan came down with Bryce Underwood’s second Hail Mary pass to turn the four-touchdown-underdog Broncos’ 12-7 upset into a 13-12 loss.
The Mid-American Conference submitted appeals to the NCAA and the College Football Playoff administration asking for the result to be overturned to let the record show the Broncos actually won the game for purposes of rankings, evaluations and selection deliberations. The NCAA said its rules don’t allow a move like that and the CFP won’t release its first rankings until November.
Top 25 voters have weighed in, though.
The Wolverines dropped from No. 16 in the preseason poll to out of the Top 25 altogether in the first regular-season poll. It was the biggest fall from ranked to unranked after a win since at least 2008.
Michigan had appeared on all 69 preseason ballots and was listed as high as No. 10 on one. The Wolverines were on just 22 ballots Tuesday.
Bob Asmussen of the Champaign (Illinois) News-Gazette, in his 16th year as a voter, put Michigan No. 12 on his preseason ballot and said he knew that was a mistake as he watched Michigan’s offense sputter after scoring on its first possession. Voters sometimes hesitate to penalize a team that wins, but Michigan was going to drop off Asmussen’s ballot regardless. Forty-six other voters agreed with him.
“I saw them lose in my mind, but they didn’t technically lose,” Asmussen said. “It was so easy to drop them because of how horrible they were.”
Kirk Bohls of the Houston Chronicle, in his fourth decade as a voter, had Michigan No. 20 on his preseason ballot but said the Wolverines looked nothing like a Top 25 team. Bohls said he was disturbed by the way the end of the game played out, and the Big Ten’s statement about why 1 second was put on the clock after it showed zeroes didn’t convince him.
“We were all watching and the Big Ten told us don’t believe what you just saw with your eyes, and it’s kind of hard to unsee that,” Bohls said.
Bohls said he’ll be curious as to how the CFP selection committee will look at the game if Michigan ends up under consideration for an at-large playoff bid.
“Some people probably on the selection committee might view it as a loss or at the very least a tainted victory,” he said. “It could ultimately be a tie-breaker that goes against Michigan.”
Lots of choices for No. 1
Ohio State is No. 1 by a wide margin going into its showdown at No. 4 Texas this weekend but there is far from universal agreement on which team is best in the land.

deduped_items.body_text:
In North Carolina, a race is on to restore critical peatland before it dries up or is destroyed
Scientists and investors are restoring a 23-square-mile (60-square-kilometer) tract of peatland in North Carolina to help curb climate-warming emissions and restore native habitat. (AP Video: Joshua A. Bickel)
BELHAVEN, N.C. (AP) — The birds are up with the sunrise — warblers, flycatchers, sparrows and towhees calling across the treetops. Deer browse on tender buds emerging from dense shrubs. Black bears scrounge for roots, insects and other edibles.
It’s an idyllic setting in North Carolina’s Inner Banks, where fields of cotton, soybeans and corn stretch for miles, country roads wend through stands of pines and thousands of bird watchers converge to witness the spring migration.
But it’s what’s underground that has drawn scientists and investors to this 23-square-mile (60-square-kilometer) tract: spongy, dense peat up to 15 feet (5 meters) deep.
They’re here to save it.
Fifty miles (80 kilometers) of ditches dug decades ago for an abandoned farming venture drained much of the water from thousands of years of accumulated peat, leaving the site vulnerable to drought and wildfires, altering its native habitats — and allowing it to emit 130,000 tons of climate-warming carbon dioxide a year.
“Our goal is for perpetuity to conserve these lands so they can’t become oil and gas fields, so they’re not mined for phosphorus or turned into parking lots and shopping centers,” said Tripp Wall, CEO of Colorado-based company Pantheon Regeneration. “They’re just these incredible systems that I feel are underappreciated here in the U.S. (that) for 10,000 to 15,000 years have been climatologically resilient until we screwed them up.”
Peatlands are a climate paradox. Though they account for just 3% of global land surface, they store one-third of the Earth’s carbon dioxide, more than all forests combined. But when degraded — primarily when farmers lower the water table to grow crops — destroyed or burned, they become part of the problem, releasing huge volumes of greenhouse gases, now about 6% of the annual global total from all sources.
And the type of peatlands found in North Carolina, and for hundreds of miles along the Eastern Seaboard, are among the most threatened in the world.
Pantheon plans to reverse the damage by blocking off ditches to control the water table and significantly reduce carbon dioxide emissions. Then it will cull invasive species and replant native grasses, flowers and other plants.
The restoration is modeled after other projects by nonprofits and government agencies, including at the adjacent 175-square-mile (453-square-kilometer) Pocosin Lakes National Wildlife Refuge — one of the largest peatland restoration projects in the U.S. — which provides habitat for threatened and endangered species such as red wolves, yellow pitcher plants and Atlantic white cedar, and has become an important stopover for migrating birds such as Tundra swans.
But what sets apart Pantheon’s project is a plan to sell carbon credits to tech companies and other corporations that want to compensate for their own greenhouse gas emissions, then use the money to restore and preserve a million acres (1,562 square miles, or 4,047 square kilometers) of peatland from Virginia to northern Florida over the next decade.
Each property will be permanently conserved and rewilded — “big corridors, big birding habitats, big biodiversity hotspots that have an outsized impact on climate,” said Wall.
Ancient ecosystems under threat
Neal Flanagan pushes a metal tube through roots and around buried logs until it sinks about a meter (3 feet). When he pulls it out, it’s packed with black soil.
Near the surface, it’s dry and full of dead fibers from plants like wood fern, blueberry and Lyonia. The middle is crumbly, moist and odorless, with bits of charcoal from long-ago fires. But the saturated bottom, 50% carbon, is the consistency of axle grease.

Bob Asmussen of the Champaign (Illinois) News-Gazette, in his 16th year as a voter, put Michigan No. 12 on his preseason ballot and said he knew that was a mistake as he watched Michigan’s offense sputter after scoring on its first possession. Voters sometimes hesitate to penalize a team that wins, but Michigan was going to drop off Asmussen’s ballot regardless. Forty-six other voters agreed with him.
“I saw them lose in my mind, but they didn’t technically lose,” Asmussen said. “It was so easy to drop them because of how horrible they were.”
Kirk Bohls of the Houston Chronicle, in his fourth decade as a voter, had Michigan No. 20 on his preseason ballot but said the Wolverines looked nothing like a Top 25 team. Bohls said he was disturbed by the way the end of the game played out, and the Big Ten’s statement about why 1 second was put on the clock after it showed zeroes didn’t convince him.
“We were all watching and the Big Ten told us don’t believe what you just saw with your eyes, and it’s kind of hard to unsee that,” Bohls said.
Bohls said he’ll be curious as to how the CFP selection committee will look at the game if Michigan ends up under consideration for an at-large playoff bid.
“Some people probably on the selection committee might view it as a loss or at the very least a tainted victory,” he said. “It could ultimately be a tie-breaker that goes against Michigan.”
Lots of choices for No. 1
Ohio State is No. 1 by a wide margin going into its showdown at No. 4 Texas this weekend but there is far from universal agreement on which team is best in the land.
Seven teams received first-place votes, the most since the same number got first-place votes in the 2016 preseason poll. It’s the most in a regular-season poll since seven teams got first-place votes Sept. 2, 2014.
No. 8 LSU’s five first-place votes made the Tigers the lowest-ranked team to get at least one since ninth-ranked Texas A&M on Oct. 11, 2015. LSU hammered Clemson 51-10 in Lane Kiffin’s first game as coach.
SEC flex
The Southeastern Conference occupies seven of the top 12 spots in the poll with No. 2 Georgia, No. 4 Texas, No. 8 LSU, No. 9 Mississippi, No. 10 Texas A&M, No. 11 Oklahoma and No. 12 Alabama. The SEC has a total of nine ranked teams with No. 18 Tennessee and No. 23 Missouri.
The SEC is the only conference to ever have seven teams in the top 12. The SEC also had that many in the top 12 the week of Oct. 5, 2025.

deduped_items.summary: In 1998, Michael Jordan laced up a pair of his iconic black and red Air Jordan 13s to bring home a Bulls victory during Game 2 of his final NBA championship — and now they are the most expensive sneakers ever to sell at auction. deduped_items.title: Flydubai Hijacker Was Barred by Oman, Flagged ‘Security Risk’ — Intended to Crash Jet in Israel
deduped_items.summary: The Omani co-pilot accused of trying to crash a Flydubai passenger jet carrying more than 170 people, nearly all of them Israeli, had previously been barred from flying over concerns about extremist views and identified as a security risk — and has indicated to investigators that he intended to crash the aircraft in Israel, according to reports Friday. The post Flydubai Hijacker Was Barred by Oman, Flagged ‘Security Risk’ — Intended to Crash Jet in Israel appeared first on Breitbart.
deduped_items.body_text:
The Omani co-pilot accused of trying to crash a Flydubai passenger jet carrying more than 170 people, nearly all of them Israeli, had previously been barred from flying over concerns about extremist views and identified as a security risk — and has indicated to investigators that he intended to crash the aircraft in Israel, according to reports Friday.
The Wall Street Journal reported Friday, citing people familiar with the matter, that Oman had barred the co-pilot from flying over concerns that he had adopted radical ideological views. deduped_items.summary: The Omani co-pilot accused of trying to crash a Flydubai passenger jet carrying more than 170 people, nearly all of them Israeli, had previously been barred from flying over concerns about extremist views and identified as a security risk — and has indicated to investigators that he intended to crash the aircraft in Israel, according to reports Friday. The post Flydubai Hijacker Was Barred by Oman, Flagged ‘Security Risk’ — Intended to Crash Jet in Israel appeared first on Breitbart.
deduped_items.body_text:
The Omani co-pilot accused of trying to crash a Flydubai passenger jet carrying more than 170 people, nearly all of them Israeli, had previously been barred from flying over concerns about extremist views and identified as a security risk — and has indicated to investigators that he intended to crash the aircraft in Israel, according to reports Friday.
The Wall Street Journal reported Friday, citing people familiar with the matter, that Oman had barred the co-pilot from flying over concerns that he had adopted radical ideological views. Despite the ban, the Omani national was later hired by Flydubai and allowed to serve as first officer on the sensitive route connecting the United Arab Emirates and Israel.
ABC News provided further details about the earlier warning signs, reporting that the co-pilot had been identified as a security risk while working as a trainee for Oman Air in 2024 after extremist materials were discovered in his possession, according to senior intelligence and law enforcement officials.
He was subsequently removed from flying but allowed to continue working for Oman Air in an administrative role, according to the report. Investigators are now trying to determine how he was later permitted to fly for Flydubai and ultimately became first officer aboard Wednesday’s flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv.
Now in UAE custody, the suspect is cooperating with authorities and “has indicated that his intent was to crash the aircraft in Israel,” ABC reported, citing sources briefed on the investigation. He was transferred to the UAE from Saudi Arabia on Thursday.
The reports raise new questions about how a pilot who had already been deemed a security risk and removed from flying in Oman was subsequently able to enter the cockpit of a Flydubai passenger jet bound for Israel.
Al Arabiya English, meanwhile, reported Friday that the co-pilot spent most of his time outside Oman, particularly in Syria. Citing sources, the outlet said he had been influenced by extremist ideas during a previous stay in Syria before traveling to the UAE, and that he left Oman after authorities barred him from flying over concerns about his extremist views.
It remains unclear whether Oman shared its concerns about the co-pilot with other countries or airlines, the Journal reported, adding that the precise nature of his reported radicalization could not be determined.
A UAE spokesperson declined to address the co-pilot’s reported history in Oman, saying that doing so could “prejudge the outcome of the investigation or interfere with its course.” Flydubai and the Omani government did not respond to the Journal’s requests for comment.
The reports follow Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s assertion Thursday that the attacker had undergone “Islamist radical indoctrination,” while Israeli investigators continue examining whether he acted alone or on behalf of another party.
“As time passes, the picture becomes clearer,” Netanyahu said Friday. “The attacker underwent Islamist radicalization. He came to crash the plane along with its passengers.”
“We are clarifying right now if he was sent,” he added. “And whoever sent him will pay a heavy price.”
The UAE investigation is examining whether Wednesday’s attack was connected to terrorist activity or purpose, or involved prior planning or direction. Anwar Gargash, a senior diplomatic adviser to UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed, on Friday became the first senior Emirati official to publicly characterize the incident as terrorism, describing it as a “dangerous terrorist act.”
The investigation follows the near-catastrophe aboard Flydubai Flight FZ1073 on Wednesday, when the co-pilot attacked Indian captain Smit Machchhar as the Boeing 737 traveled from Dubai to Tel Aviv.
The aircraft plunged more than 16,000 feet in just over 30 seconds, according to Flightradar24 data, before the badly wounded Machchhar managed to open the cockpit door. Israeli passengers rushed forward and subdued the attacker, while off

deduped_items.body_text:
The Omani co-pilot accused of trying to crash a Flydubai passenger jet carrying more than 170 people, nearly all of them Israeli, had previously been barred from flying over concerns about extremist views and identified as a security risk — and has indicated to investigators that he intended to crash the aircraft in Israel, according to reports Friday.
The Wall Street Journal reported Friday, citing people familiar with the matter, that Oman had barred the co-pilot from flying over concerns that he had adopted radical ideological views. Despite the ban, the Omani national was later hired by Flydubai and allowed to serve as first officer on the sensitive route connecting the United Arab Emirates and Israel.
ABC News provided further details about the earlier warning signs, reporting that the co-pilot had been identified as a security risk while working as a trainee for Oman Air in 2024 after extremist materials were discovered in his possession, according to senior intelligence and law enforcement officials.
He was subsequently removed from flying but allowed to continue working for Oman Air in an administrative role, according to the report. Investigators are now trying to determine how he was later permitted to fly for Flydubai and ultimately became first officer aboard Wednesday’s flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv.
Now in UAE custody, the suspect is cooperating with authorities and “has indicated that his intent was to crash the aircraft in Israel,” ABC reported, citing sources briefed on the investigation. He was transferred to the UAE from Saudi Arabia on Thursday.
The reports raise new questions about how a pilot who had already been deemed a security risk and removed from flying in Oman was subsequently able to enter the cockpit of a Flydubai passenger jet bound for Israel.
Al Arabiya English, meanwhile, reported Friday that the co-pilot spent most of his time outside Oman, particularly in Syria. Citing sources, the outlet said he had been influenced by extremist ideas during a previous stay in Syria before traveling to the UAE, and that he left Oman after authorities barred him from flying over concerns about his extremist views.
It remains unclear whether Oman shared its concerns about the co-pilot with other countries or airlines, the Journal reported, adding that the precise nature of his reported radicalization could not be determined.
A UAE spokesperson declined to address the co-pilot’s reported history in Oman, saying that doing so could “prejudge the outcome of the investigation or interfere with its course.” Flydubai and the Omani government did not respond to the Journal’s requests for comment.
The reports follow Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s assertion Thursday that the attacker had undergone “Islamist radical indoctrination,” while Israeli investigators continue examining whether he acted alone or on behalf of another party.
“As time passes, the picture becomes clearer,” Netanyahu said Friday. “The attacker underwent Islamist radicalization. He came to crash the plane along with its passengers.”
“We are clarifying right now if he was sent,” he added. “And whoever sent him will pay a heavy price.”
The UAE investigation is examining whether Wednesday’s attack was connected to terrorist activity or purpose, or involved prior planning or direction. Anwar Gargash, a senior diplomatic adviser to UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed, on Friday became the first senior Emirati official to publicly characterize the incident as terrorism, describing it as a “dangerous terrorist act.”

deduped_items.body_text:
This story was originally published by Inside Climate News and is reproduced here as part of the Climate Desk collaboration.
During the Sand Creek Fire, which has burned since the start of August in southwestern Montana, difficult terrain and fire-weakened trees posed hazards to crews searching for areas still smoldering on steep slopes after the blaze passed. So instead of relying only on firefighters to find hidden embers, fire managers used unmanned aircraft to seek out heat sources.
The operation is part of a broader technological shift underway in wildfire response. The US Forest Service is evaluating firefighting robots on the ground, and researchers are exploring how artificial intelligence could help predict where wildfires will ignite and how quickly fires will spread. Federal agencies already use drones to map fires, detect hotspots and ignite prescribed burns, and are testing their capability to drop firefighting foam and water on blazes.
“Drones are now a critical tool in federal wildfire response, providing real-time infrared imagery to map fire perimeters, detect hotspots, and monitor dangerous or inaccessible terrain, which helps firefighters make safer, faster tactical decisions,” said Meredith Hollowell, a Forest Service press officer, in a statement to Inside Climate News.
The Federal Aviation Administration said drones provide real-time situational awareness by detecting hotspots, mapping fire perimeters and aiding firefighter efforts in dangerous environments.
But drones are no longer being used just to watch fires from above.
During aerial ignition operations in which fire managers intentionally burn vegetation to expand control lines or remove fuels before the main fire reaches them, unmanned aircraft can reduce the exposure of pilots or firefighters to some high-risk conditions, Hollowell said.
The technology has become established enough that federal agencies now have specific positions for UAS pilots, managers, module leaders and data specialists, as well as procedures for ordering drone resources for wildfire incidents.
The Forest Service is also testing autonomous ground vehicles that could carry equipment and supplies into areas where conventional vehicles or manual transport may be difficult or unsafe. In June, the agency and its partners tested robotic vehicles on rough terrain in Georgia that was designed to replicate conditions encountered during wildfire operations.
The vehicles were expected to carry payloads of up to 800 pounds, including firehose packs, heavy hand tools, water containers, and medical supplies. Evaluators tested their ability to navigate rocky roads, uneven ground, and slopes while carrying operational loads.
While the technology is not yet ready for routine wildfire operations, Charlie Gray, a Forest Service district fire management officer, said it shows promise for reducing firefighters’ exposure to risk while getting equipment and supplies to the fireline.
Hollowell said the Forest Service expects advances in AI-enabled unmanned aerial systems, combined with improved fire-behavior models and data from satellites, cameras and weather models to revolutionize wildfire detection and tracking, suppression efficiency and firefighter safety.
Researchers are already examining the potential advantages of combining drones with artificial intelligence.
Phinehas Lampman, a researcher at the University of Idaho, developed a system using thermal-infrared images collected by drones and machine-learning models to analyze fire behavior and predict a fire’s rate of spread. Lampman spent seven years working on engine and hotshot crews for the Clearwater-Potlatch Timber Protective Association and the Forest Service before turning to research, according to his University of Idaho bio.

During the Sand Creek Fire, which has burned since the start of August in southwestern Montana, difficult terrain and fire-weakened trees posed hazards to crews searching for areas still smoldering on steep slopes after the blaze passed. So instead of relying only on firefighters to find hidden embers, fire managers used unmanned aircraft to seek out heat sources.
The operation is part of a broader technological shift underway in wildfire response. The US Forest Service is evaluating firefighting robots on the ground, and researchers are exploring how artificial intelligence could help predict where wildfires will ignite and how quickly fires will spread. Federal agencies already use drones to map fires, detect hotspots and ignite prescribed burns, and are testing their capability to drop firefighting foam and water on blazes.
“Drones are now a critical tool in federal wildfire response, providing real-time infrared imagery to map fire perimeters, detect hotspots, and monitor dangerous or inaccessible terrain, which helps firefighters make safer, faster tactical decisions,” said Meredith Hollowell, a Forest Service press officer, in a statement to Inside Climate News.
The Federal Aviation Administration said drones provide real-time situational awareness by detecting hotspots, mapping fire perimeters and aiding firefighter efforts in dangerous environments.
But drones are no longer being used just to watch fires from above.
During aerial ignition operations in which fire managers intentionally burn vegetation to expand control lines or remove fuels before the main fire reaches them, unmanned aircraft can reduce the exposure of pilots or firefighters to some high-risk conditions, Hollowell said.
The technology has become established enough that federal agencies now have specific positions for UAS pilots, managers, module leaders and data specialists, as well as procedures for ordering drone resources for wildfire incidents.
The Forest Service is also testing autonomous ground vehicles that could carry equipment and supplies into areas where conventional vehicles or manual transport may be difficult or unsafe. In June, the agency and its partners tested robotic vehicles on rough terrain in Georgia that was designed to replicate conditions encountered during wildfire operations.
The vehicles were expected to carry payloads of up to 800 pounds, including firehose packs, heavy hand tools, water containers, and medical supplies. Evaluators tested their ability to navigate rocky roads, uneven ground, and slopes while carrying operational loads.

deduped_items.body_text:
go beyond the headlines.
Join War on the Rocks and gain access to content trusted by policymakers, military leaders, and strategic thinkers worldwide.
October 2, 2026
                            Kurt Sanger                        
A cyber operator can spend a shift tracking an adversary halfway around the world, walk to the parking lot, and be home in time for dinner. There is no flight home, no demobilization, and no transition from an operational mission back to ordinary life. The war zone is a commute away. That arrangement looks like one of the advantages of cyber warfare. It is also becoming one of its human costs.
Bloomberg reported in August that as many as five people working at or alongside U.S. Cyber Command took their own lives in a five-week period in June and July this year, enough for defense officials to label it a suicide cluster. Officials have not established that the deaths are connected, and suicide rarely has a single cause, but Congress has taken notice. Legislative proposals include more counselors and shorter waits for care.
These proposals treat the harm, but do not prevent it. The underlying condition is neither mysterious nor new. The 2024 National Defense Authorization Act directed the Pentagon to study the occupational resiliency of the Cyber Mission Force, the command’s operational arm. The study found the resources and programs available to these operators were inadequate and a risk to long-term personnel readiness. It called for a framework to develop, manage, and assess prevention and treatment programs. The implementation plan Congress required was never delivered.
No prevention and treatment program would be enough on its own. The problem is structural.
I deployed overseas in 2009, then served at Cyber Command from 2014 to 2022 as a judge advocate, reviewing operations and keeping roughly the same hours as the teams running them. In 2021, Michael Kimmage wrote, “Belarus and the Ukraine Trap,” where he argued the United States should adopt a realistic diplomatic relationship with Belarus that takes into account its strategic partnership with Russia and learns from overpromises made to Ukraine. Five years later, we asked Michael to revisit his arguments. Image: President of BelarusIn your 2021 article, you named Belarus as one of the most likely places for a war to break out between Russia and the West. Belarus became a staging ground for Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, yet a direct confrontation with NATO has not occurred. What factors explain why that war didn’t happen, and do you think the risk has passed or simply shiftedBelarus remains an exceptionally dangerous potential flashpoint between Russia and the West. The reason why conflict has not arisen over Belarus in the past five years is that Alexander Lukashenko, the dictator who has long ruled the country, remains in power. He has tried to maintain some distance from the war in Ukraine, but he has also allowed Russian President Vladimir Putin to do what he wishes on Belarusian territory, where the Russian military is dug in and ubiquitous. If anything, the risk that military tensions or even outright war might follow Lukashenko’s departure from the scene, when that occurs, is greater today than it was in 2021.If Lukashenko or Putin can find a political leader to uphold the ancien régime in Belarus, they will be content. European countries, for their part, will not challenge a Belarus under tacit Russian control, since that is already the status quo. October 2, 2026
                            Kurt Sanger                        
A cyber operator can spend a shift tracking an adversary halfway around the world, walk to the parking lot, and be home in time for dinner. There is no flight home, no demobilization, and no transition from an operational mission back to ordinary life. The war zone is a commute away. That arrangement looks like one of the advantages of cyber warfare. It is also becoming one of its human costs.
Bloomberg reported in August that as many as five people working at or alongside U.S. Cyber Command took their own lives in a five-week period in June and July this year, enough for defense officials to label it a suicide cluster. Officials have not established that the deaths are connected, and suicide rarely has a single cause, but Congress has taken notice. Legislative proposals include more counselors and shorter waits for care.
These proposals treat the harm, but do not prevent it. The underlying condition is neither mysterious nor new. The 2024 National Defense Authorization Act directed the Pentagon to study the occupational resiliency of the Cyber Mission Force, the command’s operational arm. The study found the resources and programs available to these operators were inadequate and a risk to long-term personnel readiness. It called for a framework to develop, manage, and assess prevention and treatment programs. The implementation plan Congress required was never delivered.
No prevention and treatment program would be enough on its own. The problem is structural.
I deployed overseas in 2009, then served at Cyber Command from 2014 to 2022 as a judge advocate, reviewing operations and keeping roughly the same hours as the teams running them. I did not have the same operational experience, but much of the day was the same: short-notice recalls, inverted shifts, and the rule that nothing about work goes home.
People assume deployment was harder. Sure, deployment was hard, but it was also simple. Everyone was there for the same reason and could focus on the mission, giving the days a singular purpose. Ordinary responsibilities largely disappeared or at least moved into the distant background: There was no caring for an aging loved one, managing family medical needs, making household decisions, or being available to all the people in your “normal life.” The deployed environment was built to support you to do your job. In some ways, that was liberating, although that might seem counterintuitive to most.
Deployment meant creating boundaries in life. Everyone knew you were away. Everyone around you was away as well.
Cyber operators do not have this separation. They work long and odd hours against adversaries, all while Cyber operators do not have this separation. At Cyber Command, they work long and odd hours against adversaries across the globe while living their ordinary lives and returning home between missions. The movement between these worlds happens every day, sometimes more than once, with no physical distance marking the transition between the mission and a rush-hour commute back to ordinary life. A recall can pull an operator back into the mission hours later, while classification rules foreclose the ordinary form of decompression: describing the day to the people they love.
The effects are not limited to the operators. A child cannot understand why a parent missed the game for a war fought from a building minutes away. A parent who is home but often unavailable, in one form or another, does a quieter kind of damage.

deduped_items.title: Libyan unity talks upended as warlord’s son linked to drone attacks on fuel facilities
deduped_items.summary: Western Libya’s GNU say working with Saddam Haftar ‘impossible’ as US-backed merger plan breaks downAllegations that the son of the Libyan warlord Khalifa Haftar oversaw a “terror cell” that launched drone attacks on fuel storage facilities and power stations in western Libya have upended plans for the Tripoli-based government of national unity (GNU) to continue cooperating with Haftar on a plan to unify the country.Saddam Haftar, the deputy commander of the so-called Libyan National Army (LNA),
deduped_items.body_text:
Allegations that the son of the Libyan warlord Khalifa Haftar oversaw a “terror cell” that launched drone attacks on fuel storage facilities and power stations in western Libya have upended plans for the Tripoli-based government of national unity (GNU) to continue cooperating with Haftar on a plan to unify the country.
Saddam Haftar, the deputy commander of the so-called Libyan National Army (LNA), has increasingly been seen by the US as an important figure in its plans to unify Libyan security, judicial and political institutions.
But a round of drone attacks in August worsened electricity blackouts in the west of the country, putting intense popular pressure on the GNU led by the prime minister, Abdul Hamid Dbeibah.
Libya has been split between the east, dominated by Haftar, and the west, governed by the GNU, since the fall of Col Muammar Gaddafi in 2011, leaving the oil-rich country at the mercy of corruption, militia, migrant traffickers and myriad external actors.
Donald Trump’s Africa adviser, Massad Boulos, has hatched a plan to unify the two Libyan governments in which Haftar from the east would take on the role of president and a member of the Dbeibah family from the west would become prime minister.
Boulos has insisted he is not trying a quick fix that entrenches family elites in Libya. “It’s not about families or names,” Boulos said when asked about the reported Haftar-Dbeibah deal, before adding: “At the end of the day, those are individuals that have to be in one position or the other.”
But the drone strikes, it is claimed, were prompted by Haftar’s anger at Dbeibah apparently stalling on the Boulos merger plan and by Tripoli allegedly encouraging tribes in southern Libya to attack and kill his forces.
Over more than five days in August, drones attacked the Zawiya oil station and fuel storage facilities in western Libya. The drone strikes hit the gasoline-storage tank at the Zawiya oil complex, west of Tripoli, causing a large fire and the tank’s collapse. The tank held approximately 4.5m litres of fuel when it was struck, according to Libya’s National Oil Corporation.
On 5 September, three Libyans and one Spanish citizen were arrested in southern Tripoli by the GNU for their alleged role in a plot that was intended to include an attack on Tripoli airport. It was thought the whole group involved five Spaniards and four Libyans. The three arrested Libyans were allegedly affiliated with the Tareq ben Ziyad brigade, an LNA formation. Information that has emerged from interviews about the plot, and Saddam Haftar’s alleged role, not just in Libya, has been described as a goldmine, capable of weakening Khalifa Haftar.
Sources in the GNU said the alleged plotters were working for Saddam Haftar. “No formal decision has been made, but in light of what has been discovered it is impossible to work with Saddam,” the sources said.
The claims not only damage Saddam Haftar’s role in the Boulos plan but also the parallel UN sponsored 4+4 talks involving the main four political institutions in Libya that led to an August agreement to stage elections within two years. The deal endorsed by the UN security council overcomes previous obstacles to elections, and had been backed by the main actors capable of delivering the change.
Walid Ellafi, minister for state for political affairs in the UN-backed Libyan GNU and an enthusiast for elections, said: “Our support for the 4+4 process is rooted in its role as a UN sponsored framework offering a new approach to achieving practical results that pave the way for elections and institutions whose political legitimacy derives from the will of the people – not as a political settlement that overlooks violations or sets aside the rights of those affected.”
He opposes an elite east-west political deal that brushes aside longstanding grievances such as the displacement of 9,000 families in Benghazi during the 2014 war.

deduped_items.title: Row erupts over Cairo mural depicting Tutankhamun and Nefertiti with dark skin
deduped_items.summary: Artwork created in Tahrir Square for Chinese president’s state visit to Egypt is painted over amid allegations it revived Afrocentric claims about pharaohs’ originsOn the eve of the Chinese president Xi Jinping’s state visit to Cairo last month, the city authorities were busy removing a 66-metre-long mural from the esteemed guest’s line of sight.Depicting the Pharaoh Tutankhamun and Queen Nefertiti, the painting was among 40 murals commissioned to beautify the city for Xi’s arrival and was paint
deduped_items.body_text:
On the eve of the Chinese president Xi Jinping’s state visit to Cairo last month, the city authorities were busy removing a 66-metre-long mural from the esteemed guest’s line of sight.
Depicting the Pharaoh Tutankhamun and Queen Nefertiti, the painting was among 40 murals commissioned to beautify the city for Xi’s arrival and was painted by a group of young volunteers, Rasmet Basma, in Tahrir Square.
But it drew a furious reaction for depicting the two historical figures with dark skin – angering those Egyptians who saw it as reviving Afrocentric claims about the 14th-century BCE pharaoh’s origins. The artwork vanished under fresh paint just hours before Xi landed.
Now, Ahmed Moussa, the 22-year-old founder of Rasmet Basma, has admitted it was asked by the Cairo governorate to paint over its work, which had been prepared in just five days in late August.
The team used the AI programme ChatGPT to generate the designs, which volunteers then painted on to the wall.
Moussa said Cairo’s deputy governor and the head of the district had visited the site throughout the process and were impressed by the murals – until controversy began to build on social media.
“We used a golden-bronze tone that cast a kind of shadow on the faces at night, so they appeared dark-skinned,” Moussa said.
“We acknowledge our mistake in not consulting specialists in archaeology and art.”
Afrocentrism is a political movement asserting that ancient Egyptian civilisation was black African in origin and population.
One user asked whether anyone involved had “even seen what Nefertiti actually looked like”, while others accused Afrocentric groups of appropriating the images to claim Egyptians endorsed their theories.
Zahi Hawass, Egypt’s former antiquities minister, said the volunteers should not have been allowed to paint a city site as significant as Tahrir Square without expert oversight, and that the public outrage was justified.
“Claims linking ancient Egyptian civilisation to sub-Saharan Africa are nonsense,” Hawass said.
“Temple carvings from the late period show Egyptian kings depicted alongside captives from parts of Africa, Libya, Syria and Palestine, with the king himself not shown as dark-skinned,” he said.
This is just the latest episode in a long-running debate over the complexion of ancient Egyptians. In 2023, a Netflix documentary provoked discussion after casting a dark-skinned actor as Cleopatra, and a similar dispute flared in June 2024 after a guide reportedly gave an Afrocentric perspective of Egyptian history in Cairo’s Egyptian Museum.
Monica Hanna, a prominent Egyptologist and assistant professor of archaeology at the American University of Iraq–Baghdad, labelled Afrocentric claims “pseudoscience”. She said Egyptian society had always been ethnically diverse, from Nubian communities in the south to Mediterranean populations in the north.
“Egyptians were never one skin colour,” she said. “We are not snow-white, or the colour of cream.”
Walid Mahmoud, an AI researcher and expert in African anthropology, said AI tools such as ChatGPT reflected whatever information was most widely shared online, rather than what was factually accurate.
They were built by companies in the US and Europe, he said, and the content they generated could shape how those audiences saw themselves.
“That’s why we should never simply accept what it produces, especially when it comes to cultural identity and heritage,” Mahmoud said.
Mostafa Eissa, an art critic, said AI should remain a tool, never a decision-maker in its own right.
“I favour using technology without abandoning the human element within the artist,” he said, warning that letting such tools substitute an artist’s own skill risked emptying a work of its originality.

deduped_items.title: Trump administration diverts human rights funds to push far-right agenda abroad
deduped_items.summary: Support such as for white Afrikaners and anti-communism reveals how US is redefining what qualifies as human rightsWith hours left before the funding expires, the Trump administration is pushing to direct more than $175m of the state department’s flagship human rights fund to a slate of awards that includes a huge $40m grant for an anti-communism fund, support for a group advancing white Afrikaner rights in South Africa, a campaign against Brazil’s supreme court and programs that would reward id
deduped_items.body_text:
With hours left before the funding expires, the Trump administration is pushing to direct more than $175m of the state department’s flagship human rights fund to a slate of awards that includes a huge $40m grant for an anti-communism fund, support for a group advancing white Afrikaner rights in South Africa, a campaign against Brazil’s supreme court and programs that would reward ideological allies in Europe who protect “western civilizational norms”.
On Wednesday, the state department obligated the funds to the grantees hours before the deadline despite congressional concerns and requests not to do so, according to a source familiar with the negotiations. The state department declined to comment on questions from the Guardian specifically on whether it had obligated the funds and had “blown” holds from Congress due to concerns about the money’s use.
Critics have focused on 43 awards of a combined $176.9m that will bolster rightwing and conservative causes around the world while probably angering US allies over interference in internal politics. The Guardian has seen a sample of the controversial grants, which make up most of the $205m in funding that Congress has appropriated for the entire Human Rights and Democracy Fund (HRDF).
Sources with knowledge of the grant process have told the Guardian that the awards were personally lobbied for by members of the Trump administration, and reflect interests that include JD Vance’s warnings of the collapse of traditional western values in Europe and Stephen Miller’s push against immigration and to support white minorities in countries like South Africa.
“The story for me is the high-level – including White House-directed – attention on these programs,” said a person familiar with the discussions over the democracy awards. “These awards have been briefed at the highest levels of the department and have buy-in from the White House.”
The proposed awards represent a significant shift in US support for dissidents, human rights defenders and civil society groups under authoritarian governments. The new slate includes projects in wealthy nations, and those focused on opposition to regulation, Brexit, immigration, anti-communism, Christian protection and opposition to “gender ideology”, offering a window into how the Trump administration is redefining what qualifies as human rights and merits tens of millions of dollars in US foreign assistance.
“Congress appropriated money for the democracy fund on a bipartisan basis to support defenders of human rights, to assist victims of human rights violations and to instead promote the growth of democracy abroad,” said Jeanne Shaheen, the top Democrat on the US Senate committee on foreign relations.
“The Trump administration’s proposals would use taxpayer funds to promote far-right organizations and programs in established democracies. This is a waste of resources and undermines United States values and relations with democratic partners, including allies in Europe.”
A Democratic congressional aide said Shaheen had maintained 10 holds on $22m of awards focusing on Brazil, South Africa, Nigeria, and the promotion of a rightwing ideology in the United Kingdom and in Europe. According to the aide, secretary of state Marco Rubio had personally signed a memo to disregard the holds and obligate the funds.
The largest award, of $40m, was directed to a consortium led by the Victims of Communism Memorial Foundation (VOC), an anti-communist non-profit that has received far smaller grants in the past. A state department vetting document seen by the Guardian records $96,997 in previous contracts in the last five years between the foundation and the department, all in the 2022 fiscal year, and notes that it had been vetted in 2019 in connection with tickets to the foundation’s gala. The vetting document also identifies Andrew Bremberg, a former Trump White House domestic policy adviser and US ambassador to the UN European office, as a “senior leader” of the foundat

deduped_items.summary: Western Libya’s GNU say working with Saddam Haftar ‘impossible’ as US-backed merger plan breaks downAllegations that the son of the Libyan warlord Khalifa Haftar oversaw a “terror cell” that launched drone attacks on fuel storage facilities and power stations in western Libya have upended plans for the Tripoli-based government of national unity (GNU) to continue cooperating with Haftar on a plan to unify the country.Saddam Haftar, the deputy commander of the so-called Libyan National Army (LNA),
deduped_items.body_text:
Allegations that the son of the Libyan warlord Khalifa Haftar oversaw a “terror cell” that launched drone attacks on fuel storage facilities and power stations in western Libya have upended plans for the Tripoli-based government of national unity (GNU) to continue cooperating with Haftar on a plan to unify the country.
Saddam Haftar, the deputy commander of the so-called Libyan National Army (LNA), has increasingly been seen by the US as an important figure in its plans to unify Libyan security, judicial and political institutions.
But a round of drone attacks in August worsened electricity blackouts in the west of the country, putting intense popular pressure on the GNU led by the prime minister, Abdul Hamid Dbeibah.
Libya has been split between the east, dominated by Haftar, and the west, governed by the GNU, since the fall of Col Muammar Gaddafi in 2011, leaving the oil-rich country at the mercy of corruption, militia, migrant traffickers and myriad external actors.
Donald Trump’s Africa adviser, Massad Boulos, has hatched a plan to unify the two Libyan governments in which Haftar from the east would take on the role of president and a member of the Dbeibah family from the west would become prime minister.
Boulos has insisted he is not trying a quick fix that entrenches family elites in Libya. “It’s not about families or names,” Boulos said when asked about the reported Haftar-Dbeibah deal, before adding: “At the end of the day, those are individuals that have to be in one position or the other.”
But the drone strikes, it is claimed, were prompted by Haftar’s anger at Dbeibah apparently stalling on the Boulos merger plan and by Tripoli allegedly encouraging tribes in southern Libya to attack and kill his forces.
Over more than five days in August, drones attacked the Zawiya oil station and fuel storage facilities in western Libya. The drone strikes hit the gasoline-storage tank at the Zawiya oil complex, west of Tripoli, causing a large fire and the tank’s collapse. The tank held approximately 4.5m litres of fuel when it was struck, according to Libya’s National Oil Corporation.
On 5 September, three Libyans and one Spanish citizen were arrested in southern Tripoli by the GNU for their alleged role in a plot that was intended to include an attack on Tripoli airport. It was thought the whole group involved five Spaniards and four Libyans. The three arrested Libyans were allegedly affiliated with the Tareq ben Ziyad brigade, an LNA formation. Information that has emerged from interviews about the plot, and Saddam Haftar’s alleged role, not just in Libya, has been described as a goldmine, capable of weakening Khalifa Haftar.
Sources in the GNU said the alleged plotters were working for Saddam Haftar. “No formal decision has been made, but in light of what has been discovered it is impossible to work with Saddam,” the sources said.
The claims not only damage Saddam Haftar’s role in the Boulos plan but also the parallel UN sponsored 4+4 talks involving the main four political institutions in Libya that led to an August agreement to stage elections within two years. The deal endorsed by the UN security council overcomes previous obstacles to elections, and had been backed by the main actors capable of delivering the change.
Walid Ellafi, minister for state for political affairs in the UN-backed Libyan GNU and an enthusiast for elections, said: “Our support for the 4+4 process is rooted in its role as a UN sponsored framework offering a new approach to achieving practical results that pave the way for elections and institutions whose political legitimacy derives from the will of the people – not as a political settlement that overlooks violations or sets aside the rights of those affected.”
He opposes an elite east-west political deal that brushes aside longstanding grievances such as the displacement of 9,000 families in Benghazi during the 2014 war.

deduped_items.title: Benefits fraudster who sold fake luxury gear through Instagram claimed £158,000 cash found amid baby clothes was her children's life savings
deduped_items.body_text:
Benefits fraudster who sold fake luxury gear through Instagram claimed £158,000 cash found amid baby clothes was her children's life savings
A benefits fraudster who sold fake luxury gear on Instagram has claimed that £158,000 found stashed among baby clothes was her children's life savings.
Megan Carney-Borrowman, 35, flogged the counterfeit goods – purporting to be Chanel, Burberry and Versace – on social media to her thousands of followers.
She built a business empire with accounts linked to the mother showing more than £4million was deposited over a four-year period.
The mother-of-four from Southport, Merseyside, was aided by her husband Jordan Borrowman, 35, and her mother Sandra Carney, 65, who also roped in her long-term business partner Adam Yaffe, 53.
The four defendants were sentenced over two days at Liverpool Crown Court this week with Carney-Borrowman being handed a sentence of four years and three months for conspiracy to commit trademark offences.
Carney-Borrowman and her husband's home was first raided in November 2022 after Chanel tipped off anti-crime units to the illicit activity. Neither of them were home, and when they were later asked they claimed not to have their phones.
Borrowman said his phone was lost and it has never been recovered, although the court heard it was used again following the arrest.
Meanwhile Carney-Borrowman tried to deceive officers by handing over her son's phone in a failed attempt to pass it off as her own. However, her phone was recovered and messages led police to uncover Yaffe's involvement.
Analysis of Carney-Borrowman's accounts following her first arrest found she made significant cash withdrawals and her home was searched again in April 2023. The second raid prompted the discovery of her phone, on top of her curtain rail in the master bedroom.
Megan Carney-Borrowman built a £4million business empire flogging counterfeit goods online
Cash was seized from the fraudster's home in connection with her counterfeit conspiracy
More significantly as James Rae, prosecuting, told the court: 'She also sought to prevent the officers searching her baby's bedroom, although it became apparent that the real reason was that there was £158,000 in cash concealed in there.
'This was seized despite the defendant claiming that it was her children's savings that she had withdrawn.'
The seizure of the phone proved to be significant for the investigation, as it showed a 'very large volume of chats from which it was overwhelmingly evident that she was selling counterfeit goods and using a "drop-shipping" method to import them from the overseas supplier directly to the customer's address'.
Police found Carney-Borrowman had eight business bank accounts as well as 18 personal accounts, some in the name of her young children. The court heard between 2019 and 2023 the business accounts received nearly £4,319,952.73, and £753,419.50 of it was paid into her personal accounts.
Carney-Borrowman was then arrested for benefit fraud in May 2024, with an investigation by the Department for Work and Pensions finding she benefited to the tune of around £68,300 made up of a failure to declare her self-employment income; her purchases of two houses; her residing with Borrowman; and their joint assets.
She was also found to have made a bogus insurance claim after telling Halifax she had lost an expensive Rolex on a night out in Blackpool.
But when North West Regional Organised Crime Unit (NWROCU) officers attended her home, they saw a Rolex on her wrist that matched the same serial number as the apparently missing timepiece.
Footage from the NWROCU shows the moment an officer questions Carney-Borrowman about the Rolex on her wrist. Asked if she was wearing a Rolex, she said: 'It's not real... you're not taking it off me. It was for my 30th birthday.'
After being told to hand it over, she added: 'It's actually my mum and dad who got it for me so I could probably get a receipt.'

Touching moments that show Princess Anne's soft side - from supporting Mike Tindall's 'struggling' father to 'doting' on her grandchildren - after Earl Spencer claimed she made him feel 'small'
By MAANYA SACHDEVA, ASSOCIATE LIFESTYLE EDITOR
Published: | Updated:
She's widely adored for her no-nonsense attitude, quick wit and dedication to The Firm. But Earl Spencer has painted Princess Anne in a very different light in his new memoir.
While King Charles takes the most heat in Swan Song: Diana, My Sister, the Princess Royal also caught some crossfire in his controversial retelling, which was released ahead of the 30th anniversary of Diana's death next year.
'Lord Spencer does like to lob a casual potshot into a story,' royal biographer Robert Hardman noted, reacting to the Earl's claim that Anne shut him down during a formal meal at Buckingham Palace two days before Diana's wedding to Charles.
Earl Spencer wrote he left the dinner feeling incredibly 'small' after Princess Anne dismissed his question about Zara Tindall's christening in 1981. He claims: 'She stopped, looked at me witheringly, and asked, "Tell me, how's a christening supposed to go?".' But royal fans might find this account difficult to digest.
Practical and reserved as she might be, Princess Anne also has a softer side as a doting grandmother, compassionate friend and fun-loving royal with a unique sense of humour.
As Hardman declared, recollections about Princess Anne's demeanour will certainly 'vary' from the Earl's unflattering account – especially where the second-busiest royal has shown just how sweet she can be.
Warmth radiated from the Princess at her daughter Zara's 2011 wedding to Mike Tindall as she comforted the groom's late father, Philip Tindall, who was suffering from Parkinson's disease
Princess Anne kissing her adorable granddaughter Mia Tindall as they watched Zara compete in a charity polo match in 2016
Princess Anne will likely have been a pillar of support for her son-in-law, former England rugby star Mike Tindall, after the death of his father Phil at 80.
Phil lived with Parkinson's for more than 20 years, a condition Mike has called 'brutal'. A poignant photo from Mike and Zara's 2011 wedding shows Anne, in a pleated skirt and embroidered jacket, guiding Phil, then 65, through the venue.
'He was really struggling at our wedding and had an operation on his spine just afterwards,' Mike told The Sunday Times in 2020.
And earlier this year, it was reported that Princess Anne welcomed her newest step-granddaughter, 13-year-old Georgina, into the family 'with open arms' after her son Peter's wedding to NHS nurse Harriet Sperling.
According to a well-placed source, Anne has embraced Georgina's arrival, describing Anne as an 'amazing mother and grandmother' with a natural talent for making people feel at ease, much like her late mother Queen Elizabeth II.
Georgina is stepsister to Peter's daughters Savannah, 15, and Isla, 14, joining a growing brood of grandchildren all part of Anne's close-knit family at Gatcombe Park.
Both Peter and Zara live close to their mother on her 700-acre Gloucestershire estate, meaning Anne can see her grandchildren regularly during the rare gaps in her packed schedule.
Mr Hardman has previously said that Anne's relationship with the younger members of her family is 'very normal' and that she 'dotes' on them.
'It's very normal; there isn't any standing on ceremony, and she's the only one with a title,' the royal author said. 'She's a very good grandmother. She's hands-on, but like all grandchildren, I think they can get away with things. She dotes on them.'
Any suggestion that the Princess Royal is not affectionate was put to bed after an old clip of her and daughter Zara Tindall was recently posted online

'She adores them, and it's touching to see her

deduped_items.summary: New York, IRNA – Iran’s ambassador and chargé d’affaires to the United Nations has emphasized that the Security Council must uphold the UN Charter and international law while refraining from any politicization or abuse of its procedures, warning that the United States and its allies have repeatedly exploited the Council’s procedures and powers to advance short-sighted political agendas.

deduped_items.title: خبرهای کوتاه فارس؛ از هشدار درباره رمال‌ها تا افتتاح ۲ بوم‌گردی
deduped_items.summary: شیراز-ایرنا- هشدار درباره خطرات مراجعه به شیادانی همچون رمال‌ها، افتتاح دو مجموعه بوم‌گردی در آباده، شناسایی ۱۵۷۴ مورد تغییر کاربری غیرمجاز در اراضی، برداشت ۲۷۰ هزار تن سیب پاییزه، برگزاری نشست ستاد مدیریت بحران در جهرم با تاکید بر برنامه‌ریزی پیشگیرانه، تاکید بر ضرورت تقویت نقش اصناف در تصمیم‌سازی‌های اقتصادی، حفاظت از باغ‌های انجیر در فصل برداشت، اهدای لوازم‌التحریر به دانش‌آموزان نیازمند آباده، و درخشش جوان فارسی در جشنواره ملی شیخ بهایی، از مهمترین خبرهای کوتاه فارس در روز شنبه یازدهم مهر ۱۴

deduped_items.summary: شیراز-ایرنا- هشدار درباره خطرات مراجعه به شیادانی همچون رمال‌ها، افتتاح دو مجموعه بوم‌گردی در آباده، شناسایی ۱۵۷۴ مورد تغییر کاربری غیرمجاز در اراضی، برداشت ۲۷۰ هزار تن سیب پاییزه، برگزاری نشست ستاد مدیریت بحران در جهرم با تاکید بر برنامه‌ریزی پیشگیرانه، تاکید بر ضرورت تقویت نقش اصناف در تصمیم‌سازی‌های اقتصادی، حفاظت از باغ‌های انجیر در فصل برداشت، اهدای لوازم‌التحریر به دانش‌آموزان نیازمند آباده، و درخشش جوان فارسی در جشنواره ملی شیخ بهایی، از مهمترین خبرهای کوتاه فارس در روز شنبه یازدهم مهر ۱۴

deduped_items.summary: شیراز-ایرنا- هشدار درباره خطرات مراجعه به شیادانی همچون رمال‌ها، افتتاح دو مجموعه بوم‌گردی در آباده، شناسایی ۱۵۷۴ مورد تغییر کاربری غیرمجاز در اراضی، برداشت ۲۷۰ هزار تن سیب پاییزه، برگزاری نشست ستاد مدیریت بحران در جهرم با تاکید بر برنامه‌ریزی پیشگیرانه، تاکید بر ضرورت تقویت نقش اصناف در تصمیم‌سازی‌های اقتصادی، حفاظت از باغ‌های انجیر در فصل برداشت، اهدای لوازم‌التحریر به دانش‌آموزان نیازمند آباده، و درخشش جوان فارسی در جشنواره ملی شیخ بهایی، از مهمترین خبرهای کوتاه فارس در روز شنبه یازدهم مهر ۱۴

deduped_items.summary: بنیامین نتانیاهو در گفت‌وگو با روزنامه بریتانیایی دیلی‌میل، خطاب به ایرانیان مخالف جمهوری اسلامی گفت این حکومت سقوط خواهد کرد و محاصره آمریکا سپاه پاسداران را تضعیف کرده است. او همچنین بریتانیا را به مماشات با تهران متهم کرد و درباره پرونده پایگاه فرفورد و حادثه فلای‌دبی سخن گفت.

deduped_items.title: الأمطار الغزيرة تعرقل الحركة المرورية في حلب واللاذقية.. والسيول تدخل مخيمات إدلب
deduped_items.summary: أمطار غزيرة هطلت، يومي الخميس والجمعة، على محافظات حلب وإدلب واللاذقية شمال غربي سوريا، وأدت إلى أضرار بالمنازل والمحال التجارية في حلب، وتعطل حركة السير في اللاذقية، وتجمع المياه في مخيمات النازحين في إدلب.
deduped_items.body_text:
الأمطار الغزيرة تعرقل الحركة المرورية في حلب واللاذقية.. والسيول تدخل مخيمات إدلب
عرقلت الهطولات المطرية الغزيرة على محافظات حلب وإدلب واللاذقية، يومي الخميس والجمعة الماضيين، حركة المرور جراء ارتفاع مستوى المياه في الشوارع، فيما تكبد الأهالي وأصحاب المحال التجارية في مدينة حلب خسائر جسيمة جراء دخول المياه إلى الأقبية والمنازل المنخفضة.
وكانت وزارة الطوارئ وإدارة الكوارث السورية حذرت من أمطار غزيرة وعواصف رعدية ورياح هابطة ما بين 2 و5 أكتوبر/تشرين الأول الجاري.
وقالت الوزارة، في بيان لها، يُتوقع أن تشهد المناطق الساحلية والشمالية الغربية والأجزاء الغربية من المناطق الوسطى بالدرجة الأولى هطولات مطرية رعدية غزيرة، تليها أجزاء من ريف دمشق الغربي الشمالي وأجزاء من حمص وحماة وصولا إلى الرقة والحسكة وأجزاء من دير الزور.

من جهته، أعلن محافظ حلب عزام الغريب صيانة ومعالجة "أكثر من 50 نقطة ضمن شبكة الصرف"، مضيفا -في منشور له على منصة إكس أمس الجمعة- بعد الخلل الذي حصل خلال العاصفة المطرية وتجمع المياه في بعض المواقع، "اتخذنا عدة إجراءات إدارية لتلافي التقصير، بالتوازي مع تكثيف العمل الميداني على عدة محاور".
وكان الغريب عبّر، في تصريح سابق، عن أسفه جراء ما حصل في بعض المواقع، مؤكدا الوقوف مع المتضررين من أصحاب المنازل والمحال التجارية في المحافظة.
وقال إن المحاسبة الحاسمة ستكون "مصير من قصر في عمله وكان سببا في الضرر الذي حصل".

وفي اللاذقية، أعاق تجمع المياه والسيول الحركة في الشوارع الرئيسية للمدينة، فيما سجلت أضرار مادية بالممتلكات جراء سقوط أشجار وغمر المياه لبعض الشوارع والساحات العامة.
وقالت محافظة اللاذقية، في بيان، إنه تم "فتح المصارف المطرية، وتسليك شبكات الصرف الصحي، وإزالة الأنقاض والعوائق المتراكمة لضمان انسيابية السير" مؤكدة وضع فرق الطوارئ في حالة "جاهزية تامة على مدار الساعة للتدخل السريع في كافة الأحياء والمناطق حفاظا على السلامة العامة".
بدورها، أعلنت مديرية الطوارئ وإدارة الكوارث في اللاذقية استجابة فرقها لتداعيات الأمطار الغزيرة والرياح خلال 12 ساعة الماضية في 18 موقعا في مدينة اللاذقية ومناطق جبلة والقرداحة جنوبي المحافظة وطريق اللاذقية-طرطوس وطريق اللاذقية-حلب، مضيفة أن الفرق عملت على تصريف المياه وفتح ممرات مائية وإزالة أشجار من الطرقات.

وقالت مديرية الطوارئ وإدارة الكوارث إن فرق الدفاع المدني عملت على "إزالة الحجارة والرواسب التي جرفتها السيول، إضافة إلى فتح مجار لتصريف مياه الأمطار، بما يسهم في إعادة الحركة إلى الطرق وتعزيز سلامة الأهالي".
كما استجابت فرق الدفاع المدني، الخميس، لبلاغات حول تجمع مياه الأمطار في عدد من مخيمات شمال إدلب، ومنها: مخيم الكرامة ومخيم الشيخ صالح ومدرسة مخيم تجمع الكرامة، ومخيم قرية الجنة بالإضافة إلى طريق عقربات-كفرلوسين.
وقالت مديرية الطوارئ إنه تم العمل على شفط المياه المتجمعة، وفتح المصارف لتصريف المياه والحد من آثار تجمعها، بالإضافة إلى إزالة الجدران التي انهارت بسبب الأمطار، وفتح وتسهيل طريق عقربات-كفرلوسين لتسهيل حركة الأهالي والمركبات.

الأمطار الغزيرة تعرقل الحركة المرورية في حلب واللاذقية.. والسيول تدخل مخيمات إدلب
عرقلت الهطولات المطرية الغزيرة على محافظات حلب وإدلب واللاذقية، يومي الخميس والجمعة الماضيين، حركة المرور جراء ارتفاع مستوى المياه في الشوارع، فيما تكبد الأهالي وأصحاب المحال التجارية في مدينة حلب خسائر جسيمة جراء دخول المياه إلى الأقبية والمنازل المنخفضة.
وكانت وزارة الطوارئ وإدارة الكوارث السورية حذرت من أمطار غزيرة وعواصف رعدية ورياح هابطة ما بين 2 و5 أكتوبر/تشرين الأول الجاري.
وقالت الوزارة، في بيان لها، يُتوقع أن تشهد المناطق الساحلية والشمالية الغربية والأجزاء الغربية من المناطق الوسطى بالدرجة الأولى هطولات مطرية رعدية غزيرة، تليها أجزاء من ريف دمشق الغربي الشمالي وأجزاء من حمص وحماة وصولا إلى الرقة والحسكة وأجزاء من دير الزور.
المياه غمرت أقبية في حلب
وفي حلب، غمرت مياه الأمطار أقبية منازل في حي الزبدية، فيما أظهرت مشاهد مصورة ارتفاع منسوب المياه في عدد من الشوارع، ولا سيما في أحياء صلاح الدين وسيف الدولة والفيض وكرم الجزماتي داخل المدينة، إضافة إلى الطريق الممتد باتجاه جسر الحج، ما انعكس على حركة المركبات والمواصلات.
وأعلنت محافظة حلب، في بيان لها، استمرار فرق الطوارئ أعمال تنظيف وتعزيل شبكات الصرف الصحي، وفتح خطوط التصريف وفتح الطرقات وتنظيف الساحات العامة.
من جهته، أعلن محافظ حلب عزام الغريب صيانة ومعالجة "أكثر من 50 نقطة ضمن شبكة الصرف"، مضيفا -في منشور له على منصة إكس أمس الجمعة- بعد الخلل الذي حصل خلال العاصفة المطرية وتجمع المياه في بعض المواقع، "اتخذنا عدة إجراءات إدارية لتلافي التقصير، بالتوازي مع تكثيف العمل الميداني على عدة محاور".
وكان الغريب عبّر، في تصريح سابق، عن أسفه جراء ما حصل في بعض المواقع، مؤكدا الوقوف مع المتضررين من أصحاب المنازل والمحال التجارية في المحافظة.
وقال إن المحاسبة الحاسمة ستكون "مصير من قصر في عمله وكان سببا في الضرر الذي حصل".
فتح طرق في اللاذقية
وفي اللاذقية، أعاق تجمع المياه والسيول الحركة في الشوارع الرئيسية للمدينة، فيما سجلت أضرار مادية بالممتلكات جراء سقوط أشجار وغمر المياه لبعض الشوارع والساحات العامة.
وقالت محافظة اللاذقية، في بيان، إنه تم "فتح المصارف المطرية، وتسليك شبكات الصرف الصحي، وإزالة الأنقاض والعوائق المتراكمة لضمان انسيابية السير" مؤكدة وضع فرق الطوارئ في حالة "جاهزية تامة على مدار الساعة للتدخل السريع في كافة الأحياء والمناطق حفاظا على السلامة العامة".
بدورها، أعلنت مديرية الطوارئ وإدارة الكوارث في اللاذقية استجابة فرقها لتداعيات الأمطار الغزيرة والرياح خلال 12 ساعة الماضية في 18 موقعا في مدينة اللاذقية ومناطق جبلة والقرداحة جنوبي المحافظة وطريق اللاذقية-طرطوس وطريق اللاذقية-حلب، مضيفة أن الفرق عملت على تصريف المياه وفتح ممرات مائية وإزالة أشجار من الطرقات.
وأضافت أنه تم شفط المياه من مبنيين حكوميين في مدينة جبلة، ومنزل في منطقة سقوبين، إلى جانب عدد من المواقع على طريق اللاذقية والكورنيش الجنوبي وأمام حديقة البطرنة، كما أزالت شجرة سقطت على طريق بورسعيد في مدينة اللاذقية.
مخيمات إدلب
وفي إدلب، تضررت بعض المخيمات جراء وصول مياه الأمطار إلى داخل مساكن الأهالي، كما أظهرت مشاهد فيديو تضرر منازل داخل مخيم الكرامة، فيما عملت فرق الدفاع المدني، أمس الجمعة، على فتح مجاري المياه وإزالة الحجارة والرواسب التي جرفتها السيول، لتسهيل حركة الأهالي وضمان سلامتهم في مدينة إدلب وبلدة سلقين وقرية مصيبين.
وقالت مديرية الطوارئ وإدارة الكوارث إن فرق الدفاع المدني عملت على "إزالة الحجارة والرواسب التي جرفتها السيول، إضافة إلى فتح مجار لتصريف مياه الأمطار، بما يسهم في إعادة الحركة إلى الطرق وتعزيز سلامة الأهالي".
كما استجابت فرق الدفاع المدني، الخميس، لبلاغات حول تجمع مياه الأمطار في عدد من مخيمات شمال إدلب، ومنها: مخيم الكرامة ومخيم الشيخ صالح ومدرسة مخيم تجمع الكرامة، ومخيم قرية الجنة بالإضافة إلى طريق عقربات-كفرلوسين.
وقالت مديرية الطوارئ إنه تم العمل على شفط المياه المتجمعة، وفتح المصارف لتصريف المياه والحد من آثار تجمعها، بالإضافة إلى إزالة الجدران التي انهارت بسبب الأمطار، وفتح وتسهيل طريق عقربات-كفرلوسين لتسهيل حركة الأهالي والمركبات.

وكانت وزارة الطوارئ وإدارة الكوارث السورية حذرت من أمطار غزيرة وعواصف رعدية ورياح هابطة ما بين 2 و5 أكتوبر/تشرين الأول الجاري.

المياه غمرت أقبية في حلب
وفي حلب، غمرت مياه الأمطار أقبية منازل في حي الزبدية، فيما أظهرت مشاهد مصورة ارتفاع منسوب المياه في عدد من الشوارع، ولا سيما في أحياء صلاح الدين وسيف الدولة والفيض وكرم الجزماتي داخل المدينة، إضافة إلى الطريق الممتد باتجاه جسر الحج، ما انعكس على حركة المركبات والمواصلات.
وأعلنت محافظة حلب، في بيان لها، استمرار فرق الطوارئ أعمال تنظيف وتعزيل شبكات الصرف الصحي، وفتح خطوط التصريف وفتح الطرقات وتنظيف الساحات العامة.
من جهته، أعلن محافظ حلب عزام الغريب صيانة ومعالجة "أكثر من 50 نقطة ضمن شبكة الصرف"، مضيفا -في منشور له على منصة إكس أمس الجمعة- بعد الخلل الذي حصل خلال العاصفة المطرية وتجمع المياه في بعض المواقع، "اتخذنا عدة إجراءات إدارية لتلافي التقصير، بالتوازي مع تكثيف العمل الميداني على عدة محاور".
وكان الغريب عبّر، في تصريح سابق، عن أسفه جراء ما حصل في بعض المواقع، مؤكدا الوقوف مع المتضررين من أصحاب المنازل والمحال التجارية في المحافظة.

وقال إن المحاسبة الحاسمة ستكون "مصير من قصر في عمله وكان سببا في الضرر الذي حصل".

وفي اللاذقية، أعاق تجمع المياه والسيول الحركة في الشوارع الرئيسية للمدينة، فيما سجلت أضرار مادية بالممتلكات جراء سقوط أشجار وغمر المياه لبعض الشوارع والساحات العامة.

بدورها، أعلنت مديرية الطوارئ وإدارة الكوارث في اللاذقية استجابة فرقها لتداعيات الأمطار الغزيرة والرياح خلال 12 ساعة الماضية في 18 موقعا في مدينة اللاذقية ومناطق جبلة والقرداحة جنوبي المحافظة وطريق اللاذقية-طرطوس وطريق اللاذقية-حلب، مضيفة أن الفرق عملت على تصريف المياه وفتح ممرات مائية وإزالة أشجار من الطرقات.

كما استجابت فرق الدفاع المدني، الخميس، لبلاغات حول تجمع مياه الأمطار في عدد من مخيمات شمال إدلب، ومنها: مخيم الكرامة ومخيم الشيخ صالح ومدرسة مخيم تجمع الكرامة، ومخيم قرية الجنة بالإضافة إلى طريق عقربات-كفرلوسين.
وقالت مديرية الطوارئ إنه تم العمل على شفط المياه المتجمعة، وفتح المصارف لتصريف المياه والحد من آثار تجمعها، بالإضافة إلى إزالة الجدران التي انهارت بسبب الأمطار، وفتح وتسهيل طريق عقربات-كفرلوسين لتسهيل حركة الأهالي والمركبات.
