deduped_items.title: Депутат Рады попросил США раскрыть обсуждаемые условия завершения конфликта
deduped_items.body_text:
Краткий пересказ от РИА ИИ
- Алексей Гончаренко* направил письмо госсекретарю США Марко Рубио и американским переговорщикам Стиву Уиткоффу и Джареду Кушнеру с просьбой опубликовать условия завершения конфликта на Украине.
- По словам депутата, украинские власти скрывают от народа имеющиеся предложения сторон.
МОСКВА, 3 окт - РИА Новости. Депутат Верховной рады Алексей Гончаренко* заявил, что отправил письмо госсекретарю США Марко Рубио и американским переговорщикам Стиву Уиткоффу и Джареду Кушнеру с просьбой опубликовать условия завершения конфликта на Украине, которые обсуждаются сторонами на данный момент. 
По словам депутата, украинские власти скрывают от народа имеющиеся предложения сторон и утрируют позицию России, выдавая возможное мирное соглашение за капитуляцию Украины. 
Ранее президент России Владимир Путин заявил, что Москве хотелось бы как можно быстрее прекратить боевые действия на Украине с помощью мирных переговоров. 
США в сентябре активизировали посреднические усилия по украинскому урегулированию. Уиткофф и Кушнер посетили Москву и Киев, где провели переговоры о возможных путях завершения конфликта. Американская сторона также выступила за возобновление трехсторонних переговоров России, США и Украины.
*внесен в РФ в перечень террористов и экстремистов

deduped_items.title: В Киеве прогремели взрывы
deduped_items.body_text:
Краткий пересказ от РИА ИИ
- В Киеве прогремели взрывы.
- В Киеве и Киевской области звучит сигнал воздушной тревоги.
МОСКВА, 3 окт - РИА Новости. Взрывы прогремели в Киеве на фоне воздушной тревоги, сообщает украинский "24 канал". 
Ранее утром украинские СМИ сообщали о взрывах в украинской столице. 
«
"В Киеве слышны взрывы", - говорится в сообщении в Telegram-канале "24 канала". 
По данным онлайн-карты украинского министерства цифровой трансформации, в Киеве и Киевской области звучит сигнал воздушной тревоги.
Интерактивная карта спецоперации Вооруженных сил России на Украине 22 июня 2022, 17:18

deduped_items.title: "Что вы сделали?" К депутатам Рады обратились с жестким заявлением
deduped_items.body_text:
Краткий пересказ от РИА ИИ
- Артем Дмитрук заявил, что депутаты Верховной Рады не сделали ничего, что могло бы приблизить Украину к миру с Россией.
МОСКВА, 3 окт — РИА Новости. Депутаты Верховной Рады не сделали ровным счетом ничего, что могло бы приблизить Украину к миру с Россией, заявил парламентарий Артем Дмитрук.
"Сейчас хочу конкретно спросить у своих коллег, которые пишут, что необходимо объединяться всем, кто "за мир". Вы сегодня сидите в парламенте с реальными полномочиями и влиянием. <…> Вы создали новую переговорную группу для поездки в Минск или Москву? Нет. Вы встали на защиту хоть одного храма нашей Церкви? Нет. Вы потребовали освободить священников из тюрьмы? Нет. Вы, в конце концов, защитили хоть одного человека от ТЦК? Нет. <…> Что вы, люди с сильной властью, сделали для достижения мира?" — написал он в Telegram-канале.
По мнению Дмитрука, все, что сейчас происходит в Раде, является "игрой на жизнях людей" и попыткой депутатов сохранить власть.
В пятницу депутат Верховной рады Алексей Гончаренко* призвал заключить с Россией мир на фоне поражения Киева в конфликте.
Президент Владимир Путин на пленарной сессии XXIII ежегодного заседания международного дискуссионного клуба "Валдай" заявил, что Россия не видит желания со стороны Украины проводить переговоры, подчеркнув, что Москва готова начать переговоры по урегулированию и завершить их как можно быстрее, но на приемлемых для российского народа условиях.
* Внесен в перечень террористов и экстремистов в России

deduped_items.title: Depression: Autoritäre Erziehung macht Kinder krank
deduped_items.summary: Ob Depressionen oder Verhaltensstörungen - psychische Probleme von Kindern hängen oft mit der Erziehung zusammen. Eltern können nicht alles richtig machen, aber es gibt ein paar Dinge, die sie wirklich nicht tun sollten.
deduped_items.body_text:
Wie autoritäre Erziehung Kinder psychisch krank macht
3. Oktober 2026
Ob Depressionen oder Verhaltensstörungen - psychische Probleme von Kindern hängen oft mit der Erziehung zusammen. Eltern können nicht alles richtig machen, aber es gibt ein paar Dinge, die sie wirklich nicht tun sollten.
Alle Eltern kennen das: das Kind bekommt eine Aufgabe und lässt sich davon ungefähr so beeindrucken, als hätte man mit dem Toaster gesprochen. Irgendwann ist der elterliche Puls bei 180 und es gibt Geschrei. Ist nicht schön, passiert aber.
Problematisch wird es dann, wenn der Erziehungsstil hauptsächlich von derart negativen Interaktionen geprägt ist. Eine aktuelle Studie aus China kommt zu dem Schluss, dass harte, autoritäre Erziehung das Risiko für depressive Symptome und aggressives Verhalten bei Kindern erhöht. Damit bestätigen die Forschenden etwas, das andere Experten und Expertinnen ebenfalls beobachten.
Eine harte, autoritäre Erziehung ist mehr als einzelne Ausraster. Vielmehr gehe es hier "um unterschiedliche Formen von Gewalt, Disziplin und Kontrolle", sagt Psychiater und Psychologe Stephan Bender.
Gewaltvolle Erziehung erhöht das Risiko für Depressionen
Schläge oder körperlicher Zwang seien dabei nur eine Form der Gewalt. Die andere ist psychischer Natur: verletzende Kritik, aggressive Sprache, Manipulation oder Liebesentzug. Gut möglich, dass Kinder dann zwar auf der Stelle gehorchen, aber dieser angstgetriebene Gehorsam hat einen Preis. "Eine gewaltvolle Erziehung fördert Ohnmachtssituationen und die sind ein wichtiger Risikofaktor für Depressionen", sagt Bender im DW-Gespräch. "Eine chronisch zu harsche Erziehung ist durchaus eine chronische Traumatisierung."
Kinder, die immer wieder die Erfahrung machten, dass sie als Person mit ihren Gefühlen nicht berücksichtigt würden, könnten ihre Emotionen schlechter wahrnehmen und regulieren, sagt Bender. Wer mit Gewalt und ohne Freiheiten erzogen werde, erlebe sich auch nicht als selbstwirksam. Selbstwirksamkeit meint die Überzeugung, durch eigene Fähigkeiten Herausforderungen zu überwinden und Ziele zu erreichen.
Damit diese Überzeugung ausgebildet werden kann, müssen Kinder lernen, dass sie Probleme eigenständig und erfolgreich bewältigen können. Selbstwirksamkeit ist wichtig, um mit Emotionen umgehen und das eigene Verhalten steuern zu lernen, und um Selbstvertrauen zu entwickeln. Eine Erziehung, die auf Gewalt und Zwang beruht, verhindere das, sagt Bender, der die Klinik und Poliklinik für Psychiatrie, Psychosomatik und Psychotherapie des Kindes und Jugendalters am Universitätsklinikum in Köln leitet.
Mit ganz unterschiedlichen Folgen für die Kinder. In seinem Klinikalltag sieht Stephan Bender, dass Jungen eher zur sogenannten Externalisierung neigen: Das empfundene Leid wird nach außen getragen und äußert sich häufiger in einem gestörten Sozialverhalten bis hin zu kriminellem Verhalten.
Mädchen dagegen würden eher internalisieren, sagt der Psychiater und Psychologe Bender: "Das heißt, die bekommen emotionale Probleme, Depression, Angststörungen oder auch Essstörungen, vor allem ab der Pubertät."
Hinweise auf epigenetische Veränderungen durch autoritäre Erziehung
Evelien van Assche ist Psychiaterin und leitende Oberärztin der Klinik für Psychische Gesundheit am Universitätsklinikum in Münster. Sie hat Hinweise darauf gefunden, dass sich eine autoritäre Erziehung in der DNA verankert und so das Risiko für eine spätere Depression erhöhen könnte.
Die Psychiaterin untersuchte im Rahmen ihrer Promotion, ob sich eine autoritäre Erziehung in der Epigenetik der jugendlichen Probanden widerspiegelt. Die Epigenetik beschäftigt sich mit der Verbindung von Umwelteinflüssen auf die DNA: Sie bestimmt mit, wann welche Gene an- oder ausgeschaltet werden. Dies geschieht unter anderem durch die sogenannte Methylierung der Gene. Dabei handelt es sich um eine Genregulation, die Einfluss darauf, welche körperlichen oder psychischen Merkmale ausgeprägt werden.
Grundlage für van Assches Studie waren voran

Problematisch wird es dann, wenn der Erziehungsstil hauptsächlich von derart negativen Interaktionen geprägt ist. Eine aktuelle Studie aus China kommt zu dem Schluss, dass harte, autoritäre Erziehung das Risiko für depressive Symptome und aggressives Verhalten bei Kindern erhöht. Damit bestätigen die Forschenden etwas, das andere Experten und Expertinnen ebenfalls beobachten.
Eine harte, autoritäre Erziehung ist mehr als einzelne Ausraster. Vielmehr gehe es hier "um unterschiedliche Formen von Gewalt, Disziplin und Kontrolle", sagt Psychiater und Psychologe Stephan Bender.
Gewaltvolle Erziehung erhöht das Risiko für Depressionen
Schläge oder körperlicher Zwang seien dabei nur eine Form der Gewalt. Die andere ist psychischer Natur: verletzende Kritik, aggressive Sprache, Manipulation oder Liebesentzug. Gut möglich, dass Kinder dann zwar auf der Stelle gehorchen, aber dieser angstgetriebene Gehorsam hat einen Preis. "Eine gewaltvolle Erziehung fördert Ohnmachtssituationen und die sind ein wichtiger Risikofaktor für Depressionen", sagt Bender im DW-Gespräch. "Eine chronisch zu harsche Erziehung ist durchaus eine chronische Traumatisierung."
Kinder, die immer wieder die Erfahrung machten, dass sie als Person mit ihren Gefühlen nicht berücksichtigt würden, könnten ihre Emotionen schlechter wahrnehmen und regulieren, sagt Bender. Wer mit Gewalt und ohne Freiheiten erzogen werde, erlebe sich auch nicht als selbstwirksam. Selbstwirksamkeit meint die Überzeugung, durch eigene Fähigkeiten Herausforderungen zu überwinden und Ziele zu erreichen.
Damit diese Überzeugung ausgebildet werden kann, müssen Kinder lernen, dass sie Probleme eigenständig und erfolgreich bewältigen können. Selbstwirksamkeit ist wichtig, um mit Emotionen umgehen und das eigene Verhalten steuern zu lernen, und um Selbstvertrauen zu entwickeln. Eine Erziehung, die auf Gewalt und Zwang beruht, verhindere das, sagt Bender, der die Klinik und Poliklinik für Psychiatrie, Psychosomatik und Psychotherapie des Kindes und Jugendalters am Universitätsklinikum in Köln leitet.
Mit ganz unterschiedlichen Folgen für die Kinder. In seinem Klinikalltag sieht Stephan Bender, dass Jungen eher zur sogenannten Externalisierung neigen: Das empfundene Leid wird nach außen getragen und äußert sich häufiger in einem gestörten Sozialverhalten bis hin zu kriminellem Verhalten.
Mädchen dagegen würden eher internalisieren, sagt der Psychiater und Psychologe Bender: "Das heißt, die bekommen emotionale Probleme, Depression, Angststörungen oder auch Essstörungen, vor allem ab der Pubertät."
Hinweise auf epigenetische Veränderungen durch autoritäre Erziehung
Evelien van Assche ist Psychiaterin und leitende Oberärztin der Klinik für Psychische Gesundheit am Universitätsklinikum in Münster. Sie hat Hinweise darauf gefunden, dass sich eine autoritäre Erziehung in der DNA verankert und so das Risiko für eine spätere Depression erhöhen könnte.
Die Psychiaterin untersuchte im Rahmen ihrer Promotion, ob sich eine autoritäre Erziehung in der Epigenetik der jugendlichen Probanden widerspiegelt. Die Epigenetik beschäftigt sich mit der Verbindung von Umwelteinflüssen auf die DNA: Sie bestimmt mit, wann welche Gene an- oder ausgeschaltet werden. Dies geschieht unter anderem durch die sogenannte Methylierung der Gene. Dabei handelt es sich um eine Genregulation, die Einfluss darauf, welche körperlichen oder psychischen Merkmale ausgeprägt werden.

deduped_items.title: Gescheiterte Hinrichtung in Tennessee: „Dies ist im Namen von uns allen geschehen“
deduped_items.summary: Christa Pike hat ihre eigene Exekution überlebt. Aber in welchem Zustand? Und wie geht diese fürchterliche Geschichte jetzt weiter? Das Schicksal der 50-Jährigen aus Tennessee hat in den USA die Debatte über die Todesstrafe wieder entfacht.
deduped_items.body_text:
Seit 30 Jahren saß eine Frau in einer amerikanischen Zelle und wartete auf diesen Tag. Auf den Moment, umgebracht zu werden. Gemeinsam mit ihrem Freund hatte Christa Pike 1995 in Knoxville, Tennessee, die 19-jährige Mitschülerin Colleen Slemmer im Wald gefoltert und ermordet, eine Freundin stand Wache. Mit einem Teppichmesser ritzten die Teenager ihrem Opfer ein Pentagramm in die Brust und schnitten ein Stück aus ihrem Schädel.
Gescheiterte Hinrichtung in Tennessee„Dies ist im Namen von uns allen geschehen“
Lesezeit: 6 Min.
Christa Pike hat ihre eigene Exekution überlebt. Aber in welchem Zustand? Und wie geht diese fürchterliche Geschichte jetzt weiter? Das Schicksal der 50-Jährigen aus Tennessee hat in den USA die Debatte über die Todesstrafe wieder entfacht.
Von Peter Burghardt, Washington
Cornell University:Aufsatz schreiben als Strafe nach einer mutmaßlichen Vergewaltigung

deduped_items.title: Cabinet OKs Public Finance Planning Document, budget deviation for energy, defence
deduped_items.summary: The government will seek a 0.3% deviation for energy and 0.3% for defence in 2027 and 2028
deduped_items.body_text:
Premier Giorgia Meloni's cabinet on
Friday greenlit the Public Finance Planning Document (DPFP), the
government's economic blueprint, with a major budget deviation
for energy and defence.
                                    
According to reports, the flexibility requested by the
government amounts to approximately €14 billion for 2027 and €14
billion for 2028.
                                    
This represents 0.3% of GDP for defence and 0.3% for energy
annually.

deduped_items.summary: The government will seek a 0.3% deviation for energy and 0.3% for defence in 2027 and 2028
deduped_items.body_text:
Premier Giorgia Meloni's cabinet on
Friday greenlit the Public Finance Planning Document (DPFP), the
government's economic blueprint, with a major budget deviation
for energy and defence.
                                    
According to reports, the flexibility requested by the
government amounts to approximately €14 billion for 2027 and €14
billion for 2028.
                                    
This represents 0.3% of GDP for defence and 0.3% for energy
annually.

deduped_items.title: Kiev sotto assedio: Mosca intensifica attacchi a ponti e centrali energetiche in vista dell’inverno
deduped_items.summary: La paralisi del traffico di Kiev è l’ennesima prova imposta alla capitale ucraina dagli attacchi dei russi, che negli ultimi giorni hanno oltrepassato una nuova linea rossa accanendosi sul Pivdennyi,...
deduped_items.body_text:
Kiev sotto assedio: Mosca intensifica attacchi a ponti e centrali energetiche in vista dell’inverno
Secondo un documento citato dal New York Times, l’obiettivo è causare il crollo del sistema energetico di Kiev. Intanto Zelensky denuncia: Putin ha ordinato ai generali di non obbedire più ad alcuna regola di guerra
3' di lettura
I punti chiave
3' di lettura
La paralisi del traffico di Kiev è l’ennesima prova imposta alla capitale ucraina dagli attacchi dei russi, che negli ultimi giorni hanno oltrepassato una nuova linea rossa accanendosi sul Pivdennyi, il Ponte Sud, nella parte meridionale della città: un’infrastruttura cruciale per i collegamenti automobilistici tra le due rive del Dnipro e per la metro, costretta a chiudere in entrambe le direzioni dopo che i bombardamenti della notte di venerdì si sono aggiunti ai danni registrati giovedì, quando il ponte - utilizzato da decine di migliaia di pendolari - è stato ripetutamente colpito in pieno giorno. Le restrizioni al traffico decise per gli altri due ponti vicini, Paton e Metro, hanno contribuito a spaccare in due la città: strutture di questo tipo finora erano state generalmente risparmiate.
Chiedilo al Sole
La guerra senza regole di Putin
Ma ormai per Vladimir Putin ogni regola è saltata, ha detto ieri Volodymyr Zelensky parlando al Financial Times dal rifugio di una scuola raggiunta da un drone russo il giorno precedente: riferendo informazioni ricevute dall’intelligence ucraina, anche attraverso intercettazioni di alti funzionari del Cremlino, Zelensky ha spiegato che in settembre il presidente russo avrebbe ordinato ai propri generali di non obbedire più ad alcuna regola di guerra. L’obiettivo è intensificare tutto quanto serve a isolare e piegare la resistenza della popolazione, con il contributo dell’inverno. Scuole, ospedali, centri dati, telecomunicazioni, centrali elettriche, ora ferrovie e ponti.
L’allarme nasce anche da un documento intercettato che il ministro dell’Energia ucraino, Denys Shmyhal, ha condiviso nei giorni scorsi con i colleghi europei: ne parla il New York Times, che ne ha ottenuto una copia. Si tratta di un piano russo mirante a provocare il crollo del sistema energetico nazionale con l’impiego di mille tra missili, droni e bombe diretti contro centraline elettriche e idroelettriche e centrali termiche, stazioni di pompaggio e impianti di depurazione dell’acqua. L’allarme maggiore però riguarda le sotto-stazioni che forniscono elettricità alle centrali nucleari (a meno di un km dai reattori), per staccarle dalla rete e costringere l’Ucraina a chiudere le tre centrali rimaste operative. Il documento fa delle cifre: l’obiettivo è privare Kiev, Kharkiv e Odessa del 90% delle forniture di elettricità e di riscaldamento, e far saltare il sistema fognario.
Il caos che vuole il Cremlino
Al quotidiano spagnolo El Paìs Zelensky ha detto che oltre a danneggiare le infrastrutture civili, Putin si propone di costringere gli abitanti della capitale a fuggire, alimentando nuovi flussi di profughi e creando ulteriori motivi di attrito con i Paesi europei confinanti.
Durante una riunione del Consiglio di Difesa ripresa sul canale Telegram, il sindaco di Kiev Vitaly Klitschko ha denunciato ieri «la situazione estremamente drammatica» in cui si trova la capitale: «Non è più possibile far finta di poter vivere come in tempo di pace! – ha detto -. Il nemico sta devastando Kiev. Le infrastrutture critiche, la logistica, gli alloggi, i servizi sociali. L’aggressore si è anche rimesso a distruggere il settore energetico». Ai vari servizi municipali il sindaco ha chiesto di coordinare i propri interventi e di «parlare onestamente» ai residenti della situazione, perché l’unità tra abitanti e autorità sarà l’unico modo per resistere agli attacchi e permettere a Kiev di rialzarsi.

deduped_items.title: Nuovo appello di Mosca a diplomatici e stranieri, 'lasciate Kiev'
deduped_items.summary: Kiev avrà bisogno fino a 70 miliardi extra nel 2027 per la guerra. Drone viola lo spazio aereo lituano, rientrata l'allerta alla popolazione
deduped_items.body_text:
Mosca lancia un nuovo avvertimento a diplomatici e cittadini stranieri che si trovano a Kiev, invitandoli a "lasciare la città". Lo si legge in una dichiarazione del ministero degli Esteri russo.
Intanto il Servizio di crisi del governo lituano ha fatto rientrale l'allarme per la violazione dello spazio aereo del Paese da parte di un drone in arrivo dalla Bielorussia. In conseguenza dell'ingresso del drone, intorno alle 9.40 lituane (le 8.40 in Italia) le autorità di Vilnius avevano invitato i cittadini della Lituania orientale a individuare i rifugi aerei più vicini verso cui dirigersi in caso di bisogno.
Anche l'aeroporto di Vilnius aveva interrotto temporaneamente le sue operazioni, mentre gli aerei della Nato si erano levati in volo per pattugliare cieli del Paese.
Attacchi russi hanno colpito un importante ponte di Kiev, il Ponte Nord, due giorni dopo gli attacchi al Ponte Sud. Lo ha comunicato il sindaco della capitale ucraina, Vitali Klitschko. "Il Ponte Nord è stato colpito. I servizi di emergenza sono in arrivo", ha scritto sul suo profilo Telegram. In precedenza, in città era stato lanciato un allarme droni. Il ponte Sud della capitale è stato già colpito diverse volte ieri e nei giorni scorsi, come riportato sempre dal sindaco Klitschko.
Nella notte la Russia ha lanciato un attacco con droni contro la città di Hostomel, nell'oblast di Kiev, colpendo alcuni magazzini e ferendo, secondo quanto riferito dalle autorità, quattro persone, tra cui una bambina. Lo riporta la testata Kyiv Independent. Il capo dell'amministrazione militare dell'oblast di Kiev, Tymur Tkachenko, ha riferito che due uomini e una donna hanno riportato numerose ferite in seguito all'attentato. Una bambina di 8 anni è stata colpita da una scheggia a un arto inferiore, ha aggiunto Tkachenko. Almeno una delle vittime ferite è stata ricoverata in ospedale.

Mosca lancia un nuovo avvertimento a diplomatici e cittadini stranieri che si trovano a Kiev, invitandoli a "lasciare la città". Lo si legge in una dichiarazione del ministero degli Esteri russo.
Intanto il Servizio di crisi del governo lituano ha fatto rientrale l'allarme per la violazione dello spazio aereo del Paese da parte di un drone in arrivo dalla Bielorussia. In conseguenza dell'ingresso del drone, intorno alle 9.40 lituane (le 8.40 in Italia) le autorità di Vilnius avevano invitato i cittadini della Lituania orientale a individuare i rifugi aerei più vicini verso cui dirigersi in caso di bisogno.
Anche l'aeroporto di Vilnius aveva interrotto temporaneamente le sue operazioni, mentre gli aerei della Nato si erano levati in volo per pattugliare cieli del Paese.
Attacchi russi hanno colpito un importante ponte di Kiev, il Ponte Nord, due giorni dopo gli attacchi al Ponte Sud. Lo ha comunicato il sindaco della capitale ucraina, Vitali Klitschko. "Il Ponte Nord è stato colpito. I servizi di emergenza sono in arrivo", ha scritto sul suo profilo Telegram. In precedenza, in città era stato lanciato un allarme droni. Il ponte Sud della capitale è stato già colpito diverse volte ieri e nei giorni scorsi, come riportato sempre dal sindaco Klitschko.
Nella notte la Russia ha lanciato un attacco con droni contro la città di Hostomel, nell'oblast di Kiev, colpendo alcuni magazzini e ferendo, secondo quanto riferito dalle autorità, quattro persone, tra cui una bambina. Lo riporta la testata Kyiv Independent. Il capo dell'amministrazione militare dell'oblast di Kiev, Tymur Tkachenko, ha riferito che due uomini e una donna hanno riportato numerose ferite in seguito all'attentato. Una bambina di 8 anni è stata colpita da una scheggia a un arto inferiore, ha aggiunto Tkachenko. Almeno una delle vittime ferite è stata ricoverata in ospedale.

Il ponte Sud della capitale è stato già colpito diverse volte ieri e nei giorni scorsi, come riportato sempre dal sindaco Klitschko.
Nella notte la Russia ha lanciato un attacco con droni contro la città di Hostomel, nell'oblast di Kiev, colpendo alcuni magazzini e ferendo, secondo quanto riferito dalle autorità, quattro persone, tra cui una bambina. Una bambina di 8 anni è stata colpita da una scheggia a un arto inferiore, ha aggiunto Tkachenko. Almeno una delle vittime ferite è stata ricoverata in ospedale.

Il capo dell'amministrazione militare dell'oblast di Kiev, Tymur Tkachenko, ha riferito che due uomini e una donna hanno riportato numerose ferite in seguito all'attentato. Una bambina di 8 anni è stata colpita da una scheggia a un arto inferiore, ha aggiunto Tkachenko. Almeno una delle vittime ferite è stata ricoverata in ospedale.

deduped_items.title: Kiev sotto assedio: Mosca intensifica attacchi a ponti e centrali energetiche in vista dell’inverno
deduped_items.summary: La paralisi del traffico di Kiev è l’ennesima prova imposta alla capitale ucraina dagli attacchi dei russi, che negli ultimi giorni hanno oltrepassato una nuova linea rossa accanendosi sul Pivdennyi,...
deduped_items.body_text:
Kiev sotto assedio: Mosca intensifica attacchi a ponti e centrali energetiche in vista dell’inverno
Secondo un documento citato dal New York Times, l’obiettivo è causare il crollo del sistema energetico di Kiev. Intanto Zelensky denuncia: Putin ha ordinato ai generali di non obbedire più ad alcuna regola di guerra
3' di lettura
I punti chiave
3' di lettura
La paralisi del traffico di Kiev è l’ennesima prova imposta alla capitale ucraina dagli attacchi dei russi, che negli ultimi giorni hanno oltrepassato una nuova linea rossa accanendosi sul Pivdennyi, il Ponte Sud, nella parte meridionale della città: un’infrastruttura cruciale per i collegamenti automobilistici tra le due rive del Dnipro e per la metro, costretta a chiudere in entrambe le direzioni dopo che i bombardamenti della notte di venerdì si sono aggiunti ai danni registrati giovedì, quando il ponte - utilizzato da decine di migliaia di pendolari - è stato ripetutamente colpito in pieno giorno. Le restrizioni al traffico decise per gli altri due ponti vicini, Paton e Metro, hanno contribuito a spaccare in due la città: strutture di questo tipo finora erano state generalmente risparmiate.
Chiedilo al Sole
La guerra senza regole di Putin
Ma ormai per Vladimir Putin ogni regola è saltata, ha detto ieri Volodymyr Zelensky parlando al Financial Times dal rifugio di una scuola raggiunta da un drone russo il giorno precedente: riferendo informazioni ricevute dall’intelligence ucraina, anche attraverso intercettazioni di alti funzionari del Cremlino, Zelensky ha spiegato che in settembre il presidente russo avrebbe ordinato ai propri generali di non obbedire più ad alcuna regola di guerra. L’obiettivo è intensificare tutto quanto serve a isolare e piegare la resistenza della popolazione, con il contributo dell’inverno. Scuole, ospedali, centri dati, telecomunicazioni, centrali elettriche, ora ferrovie e ponti.
L’allarme nasce anche da un documento intercettato che il ministro dell’Energia ucraino, Denys Shmyhal, ha condiviso nei giorni scorsi con i colleghi europei: ne parla il New York Times, che ne ha ottenuto una copia. Si tratta di un piano russo mirante a provocare il crollo del sistema energetico nazionale con l’impiego di mille tra missili, droni e bombe diretti contro centraline elettriche e idroelettriche e centrali termiche, stazioni di pompaggio e impianti di depurazione dell’acqua. L’allarme maggiore però riguarda le sotto-stazioni che forniscono elettricità alle centrali nucleari (a meno di un km dai reattori), per staccarle dalla rete e costringere l’Ucraina a chiudere le tre centrali rimaste operative. Il documento fa delle cifre: l’obiettivo è privare Kiev, Kharkiv e Odessa del 90% delle forniture di elettricità e di riscaldamento, e far saltare il sistema fognario.
Il caos che vuole il Cremlino
Al quotidiano spagnolo El Paìs Zelensky ha detto che oltre a danneggiare le infrastrutture civili, Putin si propone di costringere gli abitanti della capitale a fuggire, alimentando nuovi flussi di profughi e creando ulteriori motivi di attrito con i Paesi europei confinanti.
Durante una riunione del Consiglio di Difesa ripresa sul canale Telegram, il sindaco di Kiev Vitaly Klitschko ha denunciato ieri «la situazione estremamente drammatica» in cui si trova la capitale: «Non è più possibile far finta di poter vivere come in tempo di pace! – ha detto -. Il nemico sta devastando Kiev. Le infrastrutture critiche, la logistica, gli alloggi, i servizi sociali. L’aggressore si è anche rimesso a distruggere il settore energetico». Ai vari servizi municipali il sindaco ha chiesto di coordinare i propri interventi e di «parlare onestamente» ai residenti della situazione, perché l’unità tra abitanti e autorità sarà l’unico modo per resistere agli attacchi e permettere a Kiev di rialzarsi.

L’allarme maggiore però riguarda le sotto-stazioni che forniscono elettricità alle centrali nucleari (a meno di un km dai reattori), per staccarle dalla rete e costringere l’Ucraina a chiudere le tre centrali rimaste operative. deduped_items.summary: A la hora de querer bajar de peso, la reacción de la mayoría de la gente suele ser mirar al milímetro lo que pone en el plato o matarse a hacer ejercicio. deduped_items.body_text:
SALUD
Pablo Ojeda, nutricionista: «El estrés engorda. Una persona que come lo mismo y está tranquila, puede adelgazar»
El experto explica por qué los nervios dificultan perder peso y recomienda algunos alimentos para ayudar a relajarse
Sevilla
A la hora de querer bajar de peso, la reacción de la mayoría de la gente suele ser mirar al milímetro lo que pone en el plato o matarse a hacer ejercicio. Sin embargo, muchas veces hay un condicionante detrás que influye de forma directa en el cuerpo y al que no se le suele prestar demasiada atención. Se trata del ritmo de vida y del nivel de tensión acumulado.
El nutricionista sevillano Pablo Ojeda ha hablado recientemente sobre este tema en el programa 'Las Mañanas de Kiss' de KISS FM. Durante la entrevista, el especialista explicó por qué estar angustiado o preocupado de manera continua complica la pérdida de peso, además de recomendar algunas pautas sencillas y alimentos que pueden ayudarte a combatir este problema desde el desayuno.
 @lasmananaskiss 🫨 LOS NERVIOS ENGORDAN + ALIMENTOS PARA EVITARLO ℹ️ @pabloojedaj82 📻 Las Mañanas KISS | De lunes a viernes de 06:00 a 11:00 en KISS FM con Xavi Rodríguez y María Lama #Cortisol #Estrés #Ansiedad #Salud #PerderPeso ♬ sonido original - Las Mañanas KISS 💋 
Por qué los nervios hacen que se acumule más peso
La explicación de por qué cuesta tanto adelgazar cuando se atraviesa una época mala a nivel de estrés no está en la falta de voluntad, sino en cómo reacciona nuestro propio cuerpo ante la presión. Cuando acumulamos tensión por temas de trabajo, de familia o por el ajetreo diario, se eleva la presencia de cortisol, que es la sustancia que libera el organismo cuando siente que algo no va bien.
Según detalla Pablo Ojeda, este cambio le manda una señal muy clara al cerebro. Al notar que estamos en un estado de alerta continuo, el cuerpo se pone en modo ahorro y tiende a quedarse con todo lo que comemos. En la práctica, esto significa que dos personas pueden hacer la misma dieta y moverse exactamente lo mismo, pero la que vive tranquila va a perder peso con más facilidad que la que está pasando por una etapa de mucho estrés.
Alimentos para ayudar al cuerpo a relajarse
Para frenar este proceso y echar una mano al organismo, el nutricionista no habla de dietas raras ni de ingredientes imposibles. Su propuesta pasa por incluir en el menú del día a día opciones muy corrientes que ayudan a rebajar los nervios:
- Pescado azul y grasas buenas: Opciones como el salmón o las sardinas aportan nutrientes esenciales que sientan muy bien al sistema nervioso. Ojeda recalca que no hace falta ponerse a cocinar cosas complicadas ni dejar malos olores en la cocina, ya que abrir una lata de sardinas en conserva soluciona la comida de forma rápida y aporta ese omega 3 tan necesario.
- Fibra, cereales enteros y alimentos cuidados: Comer un buen pan integral por la mañana o alimentos que cuiden las digestiones ayuda a mantener la energía estable a lo largo del día, evitando esos picos de ansiedad que nos llevan a picar entre horas.
- Frutos rojos: Los arándanos o las frambuesas funcionan como un gran aliado para proteger al cuerpo del desgaste que provoca el estar acelerados todo el tiempo.
Un buen desayuno para empezar el día sin estrés
Para aplicar todo esto en la rutina diaria de forma muy práctica, Pablo Ojeda propone una combinación fácil de preparar en casa. Si se nota que la tensión está flojeando a primera hora, una buena medida es pasarse al café descafeinado para no sumar más revoluciones al cuerpo.
A partir de ahí, se puede preparar una buena tostada con pan de pueblo integral, un chorro generoso de aceite de oliva virgen extra, unas láminas de salmón y unos tomates cherry. Acompañar esto con un puñadito de arándanos da como resultado un desayuno completo, rico y pensado para que el cuerpo arranque la jornada con mucha más calma.

deduped_items.body_text:
Tres encapuchados roban dinero y botellas de alcohol de un restaurante en la avenida de Cádiz de Sevilla
Los detenidos intentaron darse a la fuga sin éxito al ser rápidamente interceptados e inmovilizados por la Policía Local
Los agentes del Grupo de Apoyo y Reacción (GAR) de la Policía Local han detenido a tres hombres por un robo con fuerza en un restaurante ubicado en las inmediaciones de la Avenida de Cádiz. Los ladrones intentaron sustraer del establecimiento dinero de la ... caja registradora y botellas de alcohol.
Tal y como comunica Emergencias Sevilla, la Sala de Control y Transmisiones de la Policía Local alertó de madrugada a las patrullas de la presencia de tres encapuchados que intentaban robar en el interior de un restaurante. Los agentes, que llegaron de forma inmediata, sorprendieron a estos individuos que intentaban darse a la fuga. No obstante, fueron rápidamente interceptados e inmovilizados.
En la inspección posterior, los agentes comprobaron que las cajas registradoras del negocio habían sido forzadas y vaciadas. En el momento del arresto y registro, los efectivos policiales intervinieron: un bolso con dinero, botellas de bebidas alcohólicas e instrumental de cerrajería utilizado para la apertura del local, además de prendas para ocultar el rostro y prendas de abrigo empleadas durante el asalto.
En la misma madrugada de este sábado, los tres detenidos fueron trasladados a dependencias policiales quedando a disposición de la autoridad judicial.

deduped_items.body_text:
Galicia sale a la calle por la vivienda con protestas en La Coruña, Vigo, Santiago y Lugo
Las movilizaciones reclaman «soluciones permanentes» y llegan tras el rechazo en el Congreso del decreto con medidas sobre alquileres y desahucios
Santiago
Galicia se suma este sábado a las movilizaciones por la vivienda convocadas en distintos puntos del país, con protestas previstas en La Coruña, Vigo, Santiago de Compostela y Lugo para reclamar «soluciones permanentes» frente a la crisis habitacional. Las marchas llegan apenas un día después ... de que el Congreso rechazase el decreto ley que incluía medidas como la prohibición de los desahucios a personas vulnerables y la prórroga de los contratos de alquiler que vencen este año, tumbado por 178 votos frente a 172.
Las convocatorias se repartirán a lo largo de la jornada. En Santiago, el Sindicato de Vivenda de Compostela ha llamado a concentrarse a las 12.00 horas en la Praza do Obradoiro, donde desde el jueves permanece instalada una 'Acampada pola vivenda' con carácter indefinido. Ya por la tarde, a las 19.00 horas, comenzarán las manifestaciones de Vigo y La Coruña: la primera partirá del cruce de Vía Norte con Urzáiz y finalizará en la Porta do Sol, mientras que la segunda saldrá de la Ronda de Outeiro con Avenida das Conchiñas y llegará hasta la Subdelegación del Gobierno.
A esa misma hora está prevista una concentración frente al Concello de Lugo. Las movilizaciones continuarán además la próxima semana, con una protesta convocada el lunes a las 20.00 horas en la Praza da Peregrina de Pontevedra. Sus promotores presentan la iniciativa como una «respuesta local a la alarmante situación habitacional». En A Coruña, el Sindicato de Vivenda saldrá bajo el lema «Contra el rentismo, por la huelga general» y sostiene que las protestas de los últimos días demuestran que «el poder está en la calle» y que la presión social puede provocar respuestas institucionales.
La portavoz nacional del BNG, Ana Pontón, se ha sumado a las reivindicaciones y ha asegurado que las movilizaciones reflejan el sentir de una sociedad «farta» de que, a su juicio, el derecho a la vivienda se haya convertido en «derecho a la especulación». «Una casa es mucho más que cuatro paredes. Es un lugar donde hacemos nuestros proyectos de vida», ha reclamado. A su entender, en la jornada de este sábado la sociedad dice «basta ya» a la subida de los precios y a la expulsión de población joven de las ciudades.
La dirigente nacionalista ha repartido responsabilidades entre los gobiernos autonómico y central, aunque centrando buena parte de sus críticas en la Xunta. Ha acusado al PP gallego de haber «boicoteado» durante años la política social de vivienda y reprochó la escasa construcción de vivienda pública de alquiler. Al Ejecutivo estatal le ha reclamado también medidas de carácter estructural y ha afirmado que dispone de más de 1.200 viviendas que, según sus datos, podrían ponerse a disposición de los gallegos. Pontón ha criticado además el rechazo parlamentario del decreto de vivienda, que atribuye a PP y otras fuerzas que votaron en contra.
Como alternativas, el BNG plantea fijar límites en los alquileres y en las hipotecas, reforzar la protección de los inquilinos, incrementar la vivienda pública y movilizar inmuebles vacíos. Pontón ha vuelto a defender en particular un plan de compra pública de vivienda ya construida para destinarla al alquiler, una fórmula que considera más rápida que levantar nuevas promociones. «La solución es la política», ha insistido, llamando a mantener la presión en las calles para impulsar un cambio en las políticas de vivienda.

El experto explica por qué los nervios dificultan perder peso y recomienda algunos alimentos para ayudar a relajarse
Sevilla
A la hora de querer bajar de peso, la reacción de la mayoría de la gente suele ser mirar al milímetro lo que pone en el plato o matarse a hacer ejercicio. Sin embargo, muchas veces hay un condicionante detrás que influye de forma directa en el cuerpo y al que no se le suele prestar demasiada atención. Se trata del ritmo de vida y del nivel de tensión acumulado.
El nutricionista sevillano Pablo Ojeda ha hablado recientemente sobre este tema en el programa 'Las Mañanas de Kiss' de KISS FM. Durante la entrevista, el especialista explicó por qué estar angustiado o preocupado de manera continua complica la pérdida de peso, además de recomendar algunas pautas sencillas y alimentos que pueden ayudarte a combatir este problema desde el desayuno.
 @lasmananaskiss 🫨 LOS NERVIOS ENGORDAN + ALIMENTOS PARA EVITARLO ℹ️ @pabloojedaj82 📻 Las Mañanas KISS | De lunes a viernes de 06:00 a 11:00 en KISS FM con Xavi Rodríguez y María Lama #Cortisol #Estrés #Ansiedad #Salud #PerderPeso ♬ sonido original - Las Mañanas KISS 💋 
Por qué los nervios hacen que se acumule más peso
La explicación de por qué cuesta tanto adelgazar cuando se atraviesa una época mala a nivel de estrés no está en la falta de voluntad, sino en cómo reacciona nuestro propio cuerpo ante la presión. Cuando acumulamos tensión por temas de trabajo, de familia o por el ajetreo diario, se eleva la presencia de cortisol, que es la sustancia que libera el organismo cuando siente que algo no va bien.
Según detalla Pablo Ojeda, este cambio le manda una señal muy clara al cerebro. Al notar que estamos en un estado de alerta continuo, el cuerpo se pone en modo ahorro y tiende a quedarse con todo lo que comemos. En la práctica, esto significa que dos personas pueden hacer la misma dieta y moverse exactamente lo mismo, pero la que vive tranquila va a perder peso con más facilidad que la que está pasando por una etapa de mucho estrés.
Alimentos para ayudar al cuerpo a relajarse
Para frenar este proceso y echar una mano al organismo, el nutricionista no habla de dietas raras ni de ingredientes imposibles. Su propuesta pasa por incluir en el menú del día a día opciones muy corrientes que ayudan a rebajar los nervios:
- Pescado azul y grasas buenas: Opciones como el salmón o las sardinas aportan nutrientes esenciales que sientan muy bien al sistema nervioso. Ojeda recalca que no hace falta ponerse a cocinar cosas complicadas ni dejar malos olores en la cocina, ya que abrir una lata de sardinas en conserva soluciona la comida de forma rápida y aporta ese omega 3 tan necesario.
- Fibra, cereales enteros y alimentos cuidados: Comer un buen pan integral por la mañana o alimentos que cuiden las digestiones ayuda a mantener la energía estable a lo largo del día, evitando esos picos de ansiedad que nos llevan a picar entre horas.
- Frutos rojos: Los arándanos o las frambuesas funcionan como un gran aliado para proteger al cuerpo del desgaste que provoca el estar acelerados todo el tiempo.
Un buen desayuno para empezar el día sin estrés
Para aplicar todo esto en la rutina diaria de forma muy práctica, Pablo Ojeda propone una combinación fácil de preparar en casa. Si se nota que la tensión está flojeando a primera hora, una buena medida es pasarse al café descafeinado para no sumar más revoluciones al cuerpo.
A partir de ahí, se puede preparar una buena tostada con pan de pueblo integral, un chorro generoso de aceite de oliva virgen extra, unas láminas de salmón y unos tomates cherry. Acompañar esto con un puñadito de arándanos da como resultado un desayuno completo, rico y pensado para que el cuerpo arranque la jornada con mucha más calma.

deduped_items.title: Moscow Expels Hungarian Diplomats and Warns of Economic Consequences
deduped_items.summary: Diplomatic tensions between the pro-EU TISZA government and Moscow have reached a new high. In a direct response to Hungary’s controversial expulsion of ten Russian diplomats a few weeks ago, the Russian government has in turn imposed personnel-related measures, expelling several Hungarian diplomats from the country. As Hungary Today previously reported, the TISZA government decided […] The post Moscow Expels Hungarian Diplomats and Warns of Economic Consequences appeared first on Hungary Today.
deduped_items.body_text:
A new sanction would impose tariffs of up to 100 percent on U.S. exports to countries that are among the top buyers of Russian oil or gas.Continue reading
Diplomatic tensions between the pro-EU TISZA government and Moscow have reached a new high. In a direct response to Hungary’s controversial expulsion of ten Russian diplomats a few weeks ago, the Russian government has in turn imposed personnel-related measures, expelling several Hungarian diplomats from the country.
As Hungary Today previously reported, the TISZA government decided on September 8 to expel ten Russian diplomats. The decision was announced by Hungarian Foreign Minister Anita Orbán to the silent applause of the European pro-Ukraine lobby. She justified the Hungarian government’s action by saying that those affected had carried out activities on Hungarian territory that were prohibited under the provisions of the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations; in other words, she accused them of carrying out intelligence activities. No evidence was presented in support of these allegations.
The Russian ambassador in Budapest was then asked to arrange for the affected staff members to leave the country.
The specific allegations against the diplomats and the deadline for their departure were not made public. Prime Minister Péter Magyar said at the time on social media that he was determined to protect the country’s sovereignty.
❗️ The statement by Anita Orbán regarding Budapest’s demand that 10 Russian diplomats should leave the Hungarian territory indicates that the new Hungarian authorities have got captured by ideologically driven anti-Russian phobias…
🔗 https://t.co/EST1FCcxUV https://t.co/L7L8F0Oeg1
— Russian Embassy, HU (@RusEmbHungary) September 8, 2026
The announced countermeasure did not take long to materialize. As the Russian news agency Interfax reported, Russia is expelling Hungarian embassy and consular staff.
According to the Russian Foreign Ministry, Hungary’s chargé d’affaires in Moscow, Gábor Gergics, was officially summoned on October 1. The Russian side strongly protested the Hungarian measures of September 8, 2026, which it described as “unjustified” and “extremely unfriendly.” The Hungarian diplomat was informed that
a group of staff members from the Hungarian Embassy in Moscow and the Consulates General in St. Petersburg and Kazan would have to leave Russia within two weeks.
Hungary’s Foreign Ministry responded immediately. Budapest said it took note of the decision and regarded it as a response to its own action, but saw no reason to abandon its security considerations.
An escalation is not in Hungary’s interest, and the diplomatic missions in Russia will remain fully operational,
the ministry said.
Beyond diplomatic personnel, the relationship between the two countries now also faces potential economic repercussions. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov commented on Russian outlet URA on whether the dispute could spill over into trade relations, saying,
Unfortunately, I would not completely rule that out.”
Moscow has so far kept the increasingly strained political relationship separate from economic cooperation. The two countries maintain particularly close ties in the energy sector, as Hungary continues to purchase Russian energy products. According to the Kremlin spokesperson, the current Hungarian leadership’s approach toward Russia differs significantly from that of the previous government under Viktor Orbán; in economic matters, however, Budapest has so far maintained a measured approach.
Although Moscow has not yet announced any specific trade or energy sanctions, Peskov’s warning is being viewed as a clear signal to Hungary. Continuing economic relations may be in both sides’ interest, but in the long term they are unlikely to remain entirely insulated from political tensions.
Via interfax.ru, ura.news; Featured image: Pixabay

deduped_items.body_text:
Petr Pavel to Miss Local Elections After Trip Planning Error
Prague Morning
Czech President Petr Pavel will not vote in next week’s local elections in Černouček, the village in the Litoměřice region where he lives, because he will be abroad on a private trip.
The Presidential Office confirmed on Friday that Pavel had left the Czech Republic and would not be able to participate in the municipal elections. The Castle said the president regrets the planning mistake.
Pavel is expected to return to his official schedule on October 19, when he will receive newly appointed ambassadors. During his absence, he will remain in contact with the Presidential Office in case a situation requiring his attention arises.
A post by Czech rally driver Martin Prokop has linked Pavel to the Rallye du Maroc. Prokop shared a photograph with the president and wrote that Pavel had visited the event.
The rally is taking place in Morocco from September 28 to October 3.
According to Czech media reports, Pavel’s private trip is a motorcycle holiday. The Presidential Office itself has not confirmed the location of the trip.
The timing of the trip is notable because Pavel himself formally set the dates for this year’s elections in June.
Under recently amended electoral rules, local and regional elections are held on the Friday and Saturday of the first full week of October.

deduped_items.body_text:
VIDEO: Hollywood Actress Zendaya Takes Over Prague for New Sportswear Campaign
Prague Morning
Zendaya recently came to Prague to film a promotional campaign for Swiss sportswear and footwear brand On, with several recognizable locations across the city serving as the backdrop.
The actress filmed at the Strahov ventilation towers, the building used by Prague’s Technical Road Administration for tunnel management, and the roof of the National Museum’s New Building.
The two-minute campaign video follows Zendaya as she runs through Prague while being pursued by a group of women. The opening scenes were filmed around the Strahov ventilation towers before the action moves to the brutalist TSK tunnel administration building.
A fight takes place outside the building and continues underneath it, before Zendaya escapes and heads toward the National Museum’s New Building.
The final part of the video was filmed inside the museum building, including its staircase and corridors, and on the roof. The campaign ends with Zendaya jumping from the rooftop.
The video was directed by Pantera, an Argentine directing trio. On selected Prague for the launch of its new collection, using the city as the setting for both still photography and the campaign film.
Zendaya is the latest major international star to film in Prague, which has become an increasingly popular location for international productions.
Several recent projects have used Prague neighborhoods and buildings as filming locations. The horror film Resident Evil was shot at locations including Karlín and Holešovice late last year.
Holešovice has also attracted international television productions.
Apple TV selected a tax office building in Prague 7 as a filming location for Birdwatcher, with production taking place there for two weeks. Wyatt Russell, the son of actors Goldie Hawn and Kurt Russell, is among the series’ lead actors.

deduped_items.body_text:
Prague Passengers Can Now Request Czech or English Speaking Bolt Drivers
Prague Morning
Bolt has introduced two new ride categories in Prague that allow passengers to request drivers who speak either Czech or English.
The new options are available at the same price as a standard Bolt ride.
They are open to drivers of any nationality who can communicate in the relevant language at a level suitable for everyday conversation.
Czech-speaking passengers who are less comfortable communicating in English can request a Czech-speaking driver, while foreign residents, tourists and business travellers can choose a driver who speaks English.
Bolt already provides automatic translation for communication between passengers and drivers within its app. Booking information, addresses and messages can therefore be translated automatically. The new categories are designed to cover situations in which communication takes place outside the app, particularly during the journey itself.
The company said the new options are already available in Prague, where it has enough partner drivers who meet the language requirements.
Drivers can choose whether to participate in the new categories. They may offer rides in Czech, English, both languages or continue driving exclusively in the standard category.
Participation is voluntary.
Passengers will see the two new options directly in the Bolt app. The Czech-speaking category is identified by an icon featuring the Czech flag, while the English-speaking option uses an English flag icon.

Sokhumi, Tskhinvali, Moscow Digest – September 25-October 1, 2026
Below is the weekly digest of key developments and discourses in and around the occupied regions of Abkhazia and Tskhinvali/South Ossetia, as well as those concerning Tbilisi–Moscow relations.
Sokhumi
- Abkhazia’s de facto Foreign Minister Oleg Bartsits Holds Talks with Sergey Lavrov
Abkhazia’s de facto Foreign Minister Oleg Bartsits and Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov held talks in Moscow on economic, humanitarian and security “cooperation”.
Lavrov described Russia-Abkhazia relations as strategic and allied, and highlighted Abkhazia’s support for Russia amid the war in Ukraine. He also noted a 16% increase in bilateral trade in 2025 and a 40% rise in Russian excursion trips to Abkhazia in 2026.
Tourism and infrastructure were key topics. Lavrov said Moscow would support Abkhazia’s plans to increase annual tourist arrivals to five million by 2030. Bartsits highlighted the reopening of Sukhumi airport, saying around 200,000 people had used the airport since its reopening, as well as ongoing railway and maritime cooperation.
The two sides also discussed investment, preferential lending, and cooperation in healthcare, education and culture. Following the bilateral talks, a “trilateral” meeting between Lavrov, Bartsits, and South Ossetia’s de facto Foreign Minister Akhsar Dzhioev was held to discuss regional security.
- Russia and Occupied Abkhazia Agree to Mutual Recognition of ‘Customs Inspection Results‘
Sokhumi and Moscow have agreed to mutually recognize “customs inspection” results, a measure expected to facilitate the movement of goods across the so-called Psou border crossing.
The relevant “protocol” was signed on 25 September by Russia’s Federal Customs Service and the de facto Customs Committee of Abkhazia, following more than four years of negotiations.
According to the document, the two sides will exchange “customs inspection” data electronically. In cases where goods or vehicles have already been inspected by one side, the other side may use the results instead of conducting a duplicate inspection.
The de facto Customs Committee said the new mechanism is intended to reduce processing times and ease congestion at the border, particularly during the tourist and citrus seasons when passenger and cargo flows increase.
Abkhaz de facto officials described “mutual recognition of customs controls” as an established international practice and said the new system would improve the efficiency and capacity of the “border crossing.”
- Russian Tourist Killed in Gagra
A 26-year-old Russian citizen, Amina Bikbova, was killed while on holiday in Gagra in late September. The de facto Interior Ministry detained 25-year-old local resident Edgar Abukhba, who confessed to the killing.
According to the de facto authorities, Bikbova met Abukhba in Gagra on 23 September and later accompanied him to a rented apartment. He initially denied involvement but subsequently confessed to strangling her and showed investigators where he had left her body.
The case has caused widespread outrage because Abukhba had previously been convicted of the rape and violent assault of a Russian tourist in 2019. As he was a minor at the time, his sentence was reduced from nine years, and he was released in February 2024.
De facto Ombudsman Anas Kishmaria attributed the incident to what she described as systemic shortcomings in the penitentiary system, including inadequate rehabilitation and post-release supervision. She called for reforms to penitentiary legislation and greater prevention and awareness efforts concerning sexual violence.
The Gagra district administration covered the cost of transporting Bikbova’s body to Russia and provided assistance to her relatives.
Abukhba has been placed in pre-trial detention for two months. The investigation continues. Read more here.
Tskhinvali

Russian Foreign Minister Sergey

deduped_items.body_text:
Sokhumi, Tskhinvali, Moscow Digest – September 25-October 1, 2026
Below is the weekly digest of key developments and discourses in and around the occupied regions of Abkhazia and Tskhinvali/South Ossetia, as well as those concerning Tbilisi–Moscow relations.
Sokhumi
- Abkhazia’s de facto Foreign Minister Oleg Bartsits Holds Talks with Sergey Lavrov
Abkhazia’s de facto Foreign Minister Oleg Bartsits and Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov held talks in Moscow on economic, humanitarian and security “cooperation”.
Lavrov described Russia-Abkhazia relations as strategic and allied, and highlighted Abkhazia’s support for Russia amid the war in Ukraine. He also noted a 16% increase in bilateral trade in 2025 and a 40% rise in Russian excursion trips to Abkhazia in 2026.
Tourism and infrastructure were key topics. Lavrov said Moscow would support Abkhazia’s plans to increase annual tourist arrivals to five million by 2030. Bartsits highlighted the reopening of Sukhumi airport, saying around 200,000 people had used the airport since its reopening, as well as ongoing railway and maritime cooperation.
The two sides also discussed investment, preferential lending, and cooperation in healthcare, education and culture. Following the bilateral talks, a “trilateral” meeting between Lavrov, Bartsits, and South Ossetia’s de facto Foreign Minister Akhsar Dzhioev was held to discuss regional security.
- Russia and Occupied Abkhazia Agree to Mutual Recognition of ‘Customs Inspection Results‘
Sokhumi and Moscow have agreed to mutually recognize “customs inspection” results, a measure expected to facilitate the movement of goods across the so-called Psou border crossing.
The relevant “protocol” was signed on 25 September by Russia’s Federal Customs Service and the de facto Customs Committee of Abkhazia, following more than four years of negotiations.
According to the document, the two sides will exchange “customs inspection” data electronically. In cases where goods or vehicles have already been inspected by one side, the other side may use the results instead of conducting a duplicate inspection.
The de facto Customs Committee said the new mechanism is intended to reduce processing times and ease congestion at the border, particularly during the tourist and citrus seasons when passenger and cargo flows increase.
Abkhaz de facto officials described “mutual recognition of customs controls” as an established international practice and said the new system would improve the efficiency and capacity of the “border crossing.”
- Russian Tourist Killed in Gagra
A 26-year-old Russian citizen, Amina Bikbova, was killed while on holiday in Gagra in late September. The de facto Interior Ministry detained 25-year-old local resident Edgar Abukhba, who confessed to the killing.
According to the de facto authorities, Bikbova met Abukhba in Gagra on 23 September and later accompanied him to a rented apartment. He initially denied involvement but subsequently confessed to strangling her and showed investigators where he had left her body.
The case has caused widespread outrage because Abukhba had previously been convicted of the rape and violent assault of a Russian tourist in 2019. As he was a minor at the time, his sentence was reduced from nine years, and he was released in February 2024.
De facto Ombudsman Anas Kishmaria attributed the incident to what she described as systemic shortcomings in the penitentiary system, including inadequate rehabilitation and post-release supervision. She called for reforms to penitentiary legislation and greater prevention and awareness efforts concerning sexual violence.
The Gagra district administration covered the cost of transporting Bikbova’s body to Russia and provided assistance to her relatives.
Abukhba has been placed in pre-trial detention for two months. The investigation continues. Read more here.
Tskhinvali
- Lavrov Announces Moscow’s Support for New Leadership of Occupied Tskhinvali
Russian Foreign Minister Sergey

deduped_items.title: Dec. 16 verdict date for Sara Duterte not set by impeachment court — Pangilinan
deduped_items.summary: Sen. Francis "Kiko" Pangilinan said the Senate impeachment court has yet to set a date for the verdict in Vice President Sara Duterte's trial, contradicting an announcement by court spokesperson Reginald Tongol that the proceedings could end on December 16.
deduped_items.body_text:
Dec. 16 verdict date for Sara Duterte not set by impeachment court — Pangilinan
MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Francis "Kiko" Pangilinan said the Senate impeachment court has yet to set a date for the verdict in Vice President Sara Duterte's trial, contradicting an announcement by court spokesperson Reginald Tongol that the proceedings could end on December 16.
Pangilinan, one of the senator-judges, said the impeachment court has yet to formally or informally discuss a timetable for the trial, including the proposed verdict date.
"I have been asked by the media and the public about the schedule of the trial and the verdict date," Pangilinan said in a statement posted on Facebook Saturday.
"The Impeachment Court has yet to formally or informally discuss this and has yet to decide on the timetable/timeline of the trial moreso a verdict date of December 16," he added.
Tongol said Friday that the impeachment court was increasingly confident it could finish the trial before the Senate's holiday recess, with a final verdict targeted for December 16.
He said the trial had moved ahead of its initial calendar after the House prosecution panel dropped several witnesses from its original lineup.
The prosecution could finish presenting its evidence for Article II, which covers alleged ill-gotten wealth, by next week, Tongol said.
The trial will go on recess after October 15 and resume on November 23. Once the prosecution rests, the defense is expected to present its evidence within 30 days.
Pangilinan, however, stressed that Tongol's December 16 announcement should not be treated as a decision of the impeachment court.
"This verdict date is merely the opinion of the spokesperson. As Senator Judge, I do not share the opinion of the spokesperson," Pangilinan said.
"He has no authority to issue his personal opinions on the Court’s behalf," he added.
The impeachment trial involves allegations against Duterte, including accusations of unexplained wealth.
The prosecution is also set to present evidence involving P6.7 billion in transactions linked to the bank accounts of Duterte and her husband, Manases Carpio.
The court recently postponed the testimony of Anti-Money Laundering Council executive director Ronel Buenaventura after the defense sought additional time to review documents submitted by the agency.

deduped_items.title: Sixth arrest, same mystery: UK-Iranian man out on bail over RAF Fairford scare
deduped_items.summary: LONDON, Oct 3 — A UK-Iranian dual national arrested over a mysterious incident near a British military airbase has...
deduped_items.body_text:
LONDON, Oct 3 — A UK-Iranian dual national arrested over a mysterious incident near a British military airbase has been released on bail, counter-terrorism police said on Saturday.
The 25-year-old was arrested in central London on Thursday “on suspicion of preparation of terrorist acts” as part of an investigation into events near RAF Fairford in southwest England on Sunday.
Five other men arrested on suspicion of explosives and terrorism offences near the airbase in Gloucestershire were also released on bail earlier this week.
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said there were “strong indications that Iran played a part” in the incident, a claim Tehran has rejected.
But the source and nature of the threat near the airbase – used by the US military in its war against Iran – have remained shrouded in mystery.
Police were called to the base early on Sunday after reports that “suspicious” white vans were heading towards it, triggering the evacuation of a nearby village and the declaration of a “major incident”.
Days later, police said no explosives had been found at the scene.
Adding to the mystery, British media reported that officers were alerted to the incident by one of the initial suspects, although police have not commented on the reports.
Washington has further muddied the waters by criticising the release of the suspects on bail and declaring hostile state involvement early in the investigation.
“The investigation into the circumstances surrounding events in Gloucestershire is continuing,” UK police said in an update on Saturday. — AFP

deduped_items.title: ‘Unacceptable’: US Muslim group demands action from Trump over American teen held for months without charge in Israel
deduped_items.summary: WASHINGTON, Oct 3 — The Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR) yesterday called on the White House and Congr...
deduped_items.body_text:
WASHINGTON, Oct 3 — The Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR) yesterday called on the White House and Congress to demand the release of Abdalkareem Issa Ahmed Safi, an American teenager held in an Israeli prison for nearly four months without charge, Anadolu Ajansi (AA) reported.
“It should be unacceptable to the White House and Congress for the Israeli government to continue kidnapping Americans and disappearing them into prisons known for torture, all without any criminal charges or other due process,” Nihad Awad, CAIR’s national executive director, said in a statement.
“The Trump administration has a legal and moral obligation to protect American citizens overseas, especially from rogue governments funded by American taxpayer dollars,” he added.
Awad urged Congress “to exercise its oversight authority and demand that the State Department secure Abdalkareem’s swift and safe release.”
CAIR and its chapter in the state of Texas said Safi, a US citizen with roots in Texas, has been “held hostage in an Israeli prison known for torture for almost four months without facing any criminal charges.”
According to a statement from the US-based American Muslims for Palestine, Israeli forces this June raided Safi’s family home in Jalazone, north of the city of Ramallah in the occupied West Bank, in the middle of the night.
The group said Safi is the third Palestinian American citizen detained by Israeli forces without charge or trial, alongside Sama Safi and Adam Karakrah.
According to a report by US-based independent news outlet Zeteo, Israeli authorities issued an administrative detention order against him days later, based on information withheld from his lawyer and family. The practice allows Israel to hold detainees without charge or trial.
Asked about the case, a US State Department spokesman told Anadolu that the department is “aware of reports of an American detained in the West Bank.”
“The Trump Administration takes its commitment to assist Americans abroad seriously, and we are tracking the situation,” the spokesman said.
“When Americans are detained abroad, the Department works on their behalf to obtain access to adequate medical care, proper treatment, and regular consular visits,” the spokesman added.
The spokesman said the administration “has no higher priority than the safety and security of Americans,” but declined to comment further, citing “privacy and other considerations.” — Bernama-Anadolu

deduped_items.title: Flydubai co-pilot tried to carry out ‘terrorist act’, attacked captain with cockpit axe, UAE says
deduped_items.summary: DUBAI, Oct 3 — UAE investigators have said the co-pilot of a flydubai flight to Israel this week was planning a &l...
deduped_items.body_text:
DUBAI, Oct 3 — UAE investigators have said the co-pilot of a flydubai flight to Israel this week was planning a “terrorist act” and used the cockpit’s emergency axe to attack the captain, but they did not reveal his motive.
Initial findings from the UAE’s investigation into the attack also did not confirm his nationality, according to a report today from the country’s state news agency WAM, but a Saudi source has confirmed to AFP that he was Omani.
Media reports have also said he had been barred from flying in his home nation over concerns about extremist views.
The reports came as the first flight carrying Israelis home from the United Arab Emirates landed in Tel Aviv after services were suspended following the attack, according to Israel’s airport authority website.
“The co-pilot had attempted to carry out a terrorist act” and had “attacked the captain in the cockpit with the emergency axe and tried to take control of the aircraft”, WAM quoted UAE Attorney General Hamad Saif Al Shamsi as saying, referring to initial findings of an investigation.
The co-pilot is still in custody in the UAE. Multiple media outlets overnight identified him as Omani national Hamam al-Hammami and said he had been banned from flying in Oman over concerns about his extremist views.
During the flydubai flight, the plane’s Indian captain was assaulted by the co-pilot but the captain managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers and crew to overpower the attacker and force an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.
Passengers described rushing the cockpit and a fight for control after the plane plummeted — losing around 17,000 feet of altitude in the span of a minute, according to the Flightradar24 website.
‘Radical indoctrination’
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said the suspect had undergone “Islamist radical indoctrination” and had attempted to crash the plane.
The Wall Street Journal reported yesterday that Omani authorities had banned the pilot from flying over concerns he had adopted radical ideological views, citing people familiar with the matter.
CNN, citing two sources familiar with the matter, reported the pilot was removed from a job at Oman’s national airline last year over concerns about extremist views.
Al Arabiya, citing an informed source, also reported that Omani authorities determined that the co-pilot held extremist views.
The broadcaster said he had spent time in Syria, raising concerns he may have been influenced by radical groups there.
ABC News, citing senior intelligence and law enforcement officials familiar with the investigation, reported the suspect had allegedly been found in possession of extremist materials while he was a trainee.
US President Donald Trump warned on Thursday that if Iran was found to be linked to the attack the country would be “hit very hard”.
Netanyahu has said Israel would check how he had been cleared to work on flights to the country.
“We have constraints that say that you can’t have pilots from countries that don’t have diplomatic relations with Israel. Obviously he was able to go through that,” Netanyahu told Fox News. — AFP

deduped_items.title: Pakistan summons Indian envoy over killing of 2 civilians by border troops
deduped_items.summary: Pakistan summoned the Indian chargé d’affaires to lodge a strong protest over the killing of two Pakistani civilians by Indian Border Security Force (BSF) personnel in the Bedian sector along the international border, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Saturday. Two unarmed Pakistani civilians were martyred and another was injured in firing by India’s BSF near the border in Kasur on Friday. “The BSF personnel resorted to unprovoked and lethal force against unarmed civilians. Such use of force was w
deduped_items.body_text:
Pakistan summoned the Indian chargé d’affaires to lodge a strong protest over the killing of two Pakistani civilians by Indian Border Security Force (BSF) personnel in the Bedian sector along the international border, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Saturday.
Two unarmed Pakistani civilians were martyred and another was injured in firing by India’s BSF near the border in Kasur on Friday.
“The BSF personnel resorted to unprovoked and lethal force against unarmed civilians. Such use of force was wholly unjustified and grossly disproportionate, resulting in the tragic loss of two precious lives,” the FO said.
Pakistan categorically rejects any attempt to mischaracterise the deceased as “infiltrators”, it added.
The FO said the incident constituted a serious violation of fundamental human rights, including the right to life, and raised concerns over the protection of civilian life under international law.
It called on the Indian side to “conduct an immediate, transparent and credible investigation”, take appropriate disciplinary and legal action against those responsible, and formally communicate the findings and action taken to the government of Pakistan.
India was further urged to “respect fundamental human rights and international law, strictly observe relevant bilateral arrangements and established border procedures, exercise maximum restraint in such situations, and take effective measures to prevent similar incidents in the future”, the FO said.
The three civilians were residents of Ladhar village and had moved a few steps ahead of a border pillar when the BSF opened fire on them without warning. All three were unarmed.
The deceased were identified as Azmat Rasool and Mohsin Jutt, both residents of Jattan Wali Haveli, Ladhar. The injured civilian was taken for medical treatment.
According to security sources, none of the three men had attempted to cross the border fence, with the incident described as a violation of the border agreement and standard operating procedures governing the international border.
The development comes a day after Inter-Services Public Relations Director General Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry lampooned India’s claims of “neutralising” a “terrorist” allegedly linked to the Pakistani military, presenting the individual during a press conference.
Asked whether the recent allegations could trigger another armed conflict between the neighbours during the press briefing, he affirmed that Pakistan’s armed forces were always ready for any such move and warned of “very harsh” retribution.

deduped_items.title: Taiwan receives first 2 F-16V Block 70s
deduped_items.body_text:
- Taiwan receives first 2 F-16V Block 70s WAITING FOR MORE: The delivery comes amid growing concern in Taiwan about the Trump administration’s commitment to arming Taipei, despite US reassurances
  - Staff writer, with agencies
Taiwan yesterday took delivery of the first two of 66 F-16V Block 70 jets purchased from the US after years of delays, helping to strengthen an air force that has to scramble almost daily to shadow China’s military. The aircraft, bearing tail numbers 6727 and 6728, landed at Chihhang Air Base in Taitung County at about noon after departing from Hawaii and making a stop in Guam. The two fighter jets had been expected to arrive in Taiwan by the end of August, but remained in Hawaii without explanation as US President Donald Trump prepared to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping (習近平) late last month. An F-16V Block 70 fighter jet, one of two delivered to Taiwan from an order of 66 aircraft from the US, arrives at the Chihhang Air Base in Taitung County yesterday. Photo: Yu Tai-lang, Taipei Times The delivery comes amid growing concern in Taiwan about the Trump administration’s commitment to arming Taipei, despite Washington saying there has been no change in policy. President William Lai (賴清德) welcomed the arrival of the two aircraft. “This is an important milestone in strengthening Taiwan’s air defense capabilities. It also demonstrates our resolve to bolster self-defense and ensure peace through strength,” Lai wrote in a social media post. Lai said it was his administration’s “unwavering” goal to preserve peace in the Taiwan Strait, and that investing in national defense, which increases the cost of invading Taiwan and lowers the risk of miscalculation, helps further that aim. Air Force Command said in a statement that it would carry out a planned transition training and gradually complete preparations for the new aircraft to ensure that their operational capabilities are brought online in phases. The F-16V Block 70s would be operated by the 7th Tactical Fighter Wing, which was established on Dec. 1, 2023, it said. The wing is being organized into operational squadrons in three phases, with air and maintenance personnel being sent to the US in batches for transition training, it said. Some of the remaining F-16V Block 70s have reached the stage of being ready for delivery, it said, adding that it would continue coordinating with the US program office and managing the delivery and return of the aircraft to Taiwan according to the planned schedule. Earlier in the day, Minister of National Defense Wellington Koo (顧立雄) told reporters at the Legislative Yuan that “there will be more than two jets delivered this year.” The delivery dates of subsequent F-16V Block 70s would be determined in coordination with the US, he said. Asked where the new F-16Vs would be stationed, Koo said that, in line with the military’s strategy, eastern Taiwan would be an important stronghold for preserving combat power. He did not elaborate. The US approved the sale of 66 F-16Vs and related equipment to Taiwan in 2019 for about US$8 billion. Delivery was expected to begin in 2023 and be completed this year, but delays due to technical issues have pushed the timetable back. The arrival of the first two aircraft yesterday also came almost exactly a week after Trump met Xi in Washington. Trump said after meeting Xi in Beijing in May that he was holding a new US$14 billion package for Taiwan in abeyance, although he did approve one worth US$11 billion in December last year. The F-16Vs have advanced avionics, weapons and radar systems to better counter the Chinese air force, including its stealthy J-20 fighters, though Washington has been unwilling to provide Taiwan its most advanced fighters such as the F-22 or F-35. An upgrade program for Taiwan’s existing F-16s was completed in 2023. deduped_items.title: Traffic fines to be fully allocated to road safety
deduped_items.body_text:
- Traffic fines to be fully allocated to road safety
  - By Wu Liang-yi and Jake Chung / Staff reporter, with staff writer
The Ministry of Transportation and Communications (MOTC) yesterday announced amendments to the Regulations Governing the Allocation and Use of Road Traffic Fines (道路交通違規罰鍰收入分配及運用辦法) that would increase the proportion of revenue from traffic fines used to improve traffic safety and enforcement from “at least 12 percent” to 100 percent. For traffic citations issued by special municipalities or city and county governments, 75 percent of the revenue goes to the local government. In the six special municipalities, 99 percent of the fines are deposited into the municipal treasury according to regulations. Department of Public Transportation and Supervision Director-General Hu Ti-chi, front, displays placards at a news conference in Taipei yesterday. Photo: CNA Another 24 percent is allocated to the issuing authority to cover operational costs and law-enforcement-related incentives, while the remaining 1 percent goes to the national treasury. The system has often drawn criticism, with some saying that it creates an incentive for local governments to issue more traffic tickets as it boosts municipal revenue. The issue is particularly pronounced in the six special municipalities, where nearly all traffic fines flow into the city’s coffers, critics said. Department of Public Transportation and Supervision Director-General Hu Ti-chi (胡迪琦) said that with the changes, revenue from traffic violations would hopefully go toward ameliorating roads and financing law enforcement efforts. The changes require city and county governments to issue a public report every six months on how they have used money generated from traffic fines, allowing auditors and the public to scrutinize their use, she said, adding that local governments must budget for and spend the funds in accordance with the Budget Act (預算法). If the funds are not used for their designated purposes, competent authorities should demand local governments rectify the situation within a specified period, Hu said. Official statistics show five of the special municipalities leading in collection of traffic fines: New Taipei City, NT$3.67 billion (US$115.3 million); Taipei, NT$3.15 billion; Taichung, NT$2.89 billion, Taoyuan, NT$2.5 billion; and Kaohsiung, NT$2.48 billion. Citing the NT$20.5 billion in revenue generated by fines last year from all local governments, once the new regulations are implemented, an additional NT$18 billion should be available for traffic improvement and road safety, she said. Local governments would be able to flexibly allocate the funds for infrastructure projects in accident-prone areas in their jurisdictions, including upgrading road signs, markings and traffic signals, renovating pedestrian overpasses and underpasses, and installing additional guardrails and traffic mirrors. The new system would be implemented in line with local governments’ budget cycles, and is expected to take effect in 2028, she said.
