deduped_items.title: Lin wins second straight boxing gold at Asiad
deduped_items.body_text:
- Lin wins second straight boxing gold at Asiad
  - Staff writer, with agencies
Taiwanese Olympic champion Lin Yu-ting (林郁婷) yesterday won her second consecutive Asian Games boxing gold, defeating her Chinese opponent in the women’s 60kg final. Lin beat Yang Chengyu (楊成宇) by a unanimous 5-0 decision at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, adding the 60kg title to her 57kg gold from Hangzhou, China, in 2023. “In this competition, I’m like a newborn calf ... or a little white rabbit that has wandered into a great forest,” Lin said. Gold medalist Lin Yu-ting of Taiwan celebrates on the podium after the women’s 60kg boxing event during the Asian Games at Nishio Gymnasium in Nishio, Japan, yesterday. Photo: Mohd Rasfan, AFP “None of my opponents was ordinary. Every one of them was incredibly strong and powerful,” she said. “I don’t think there was a single one of my four bouts where I didn’t end up on the ground at some point. That shows just how difficult this competition was,” she added. Yang said she struggled to cope with the taller Lin’s style. Taiwanese boxer Lin Yu-ting, in red, punches China’s Yang Chengyu in the women’s 60kg gold medal boxing bout during the Asian Games at Nishio Gymnasium in Nishio, Japan, yesterday. Photo: CNA “She is really tall and, in training, we don’t often face someone of that height, so that distance can feel unfamiliar,” she said. The victory gave Taiwan its fourth gold of this year’s Asian Games and was Lin’s first international title since moving up to the 60kg weight class following her gold-medal triumph at the 2024 Paris Olympics. Lin had taken bronze at April’s Asian Boxing Elite Boxing Championships in Ulan Batar, Mongolia, before winning silver at the World Boxing Cup in Guiyang, China, in June. Taiwan’s Hung Jiun-yi, left, in action during the men’s under-80kg semi-final against Kazakhstan’s Batyrkhan Toleugali at the Asian Games in Japan yesterday. Photo: Andy Chua, Reuters In the event in Guiyang, Lin defeated former world champion Yang by a 4-1 split decision in the semifinals to reach her first World Boxing Cup final in the heavier division. In the final, Lin was edged by Viktoriya Grafeyeva of Kazakhstan 3-2, but she avenged that defeat in the first round of the Asian Games competition with a 3-2 victory over the Kazakh boxer. Lin said before the Asian Games that she had considered retiring after winning gold at the Paris Olympics, but wanted to carry on fighting in part to defy those who questioned her eligibility following a gender row that involved US President Donald Trump, Elon Musk and author J.K. Rowling. Gold medalist Parveen Hooda of India, second left, flanked by silver medalist Chen Nien-chin of Taiwan, left, and bronze medalists Hwang Hyo Sun of North Korea, right, and Li Shu of China, second right, are pictured during the medal ceremony for the women’s 65kg boxing event at the Asian Games in Nishio, Japan, yesterday. Photo: AP She said after her victory in Nagoya that she had been “waiting for that moment when the light breaks through.” “It was really not easy at all,” she said. “It’s rare to finally reach that point where you see the dawn, and I’m just so grateful to myself for making it through,” she added. South Korea and Taiwan compete in the League of Legends e-sports finals at the Aichi Sky Expo at the Asian Games in Tokoname, Japan, yesterday. Photo: AFP Winning at the Asian Games was different from her Olympic victory, Lin said, adding that its “significance is monumental.” “I basically just felt like packing up my things and rushing back home — that was the kind of mindset I had,” she said of her previous experience. “I didn’t hold on to any hope anymore. I am so grateful to the coach for always believing in me and always believing that good things would happen,” she said. deduped_items.title: Hong Kong public universities’ non-local fees jump by up to 26% as quota expands
deduped_items.summary: Hong Kong public universities will raise undergraduate tuition fees for non-local students by up to 26 per cent in the 2027-28 academic year, marking the sharpest increase in recent years as institutions adjust to an expanded quota. Non-local students admitted to the University of Hong Kong’s (HKU) medicine and dentistry programmes will face the steepest jump, with annual tuition rising by 137 per cent to HK$590,000 (US$75,187) to recover the high costs of clinical training. Seven of the eight..
deduped_items.body_text:
Hong Kong public universities’ non-local fees jump by up to 26% as quota expands
HKU medicine, dentistry fees more than double to HK$590,000, with online users on RedNote saying hikes are ‘going too far’
Hong Kong public universities will raise undergraduate tuition fees for non-local students by up to 26 per cent in the 2027-28 academic year, marking the sharpest increase in recent years as institutions adjust to an expanded quota.
Non-local students admitted to the University of Hong Kong’s (HKU) medicine and dentistry programmes will face the steepest jump, with annual tuition rising by 137 per cent to HK$590,000 (US$75,187) to recover the high costs of clinical training.
Seven of the eight public universities have published their 2027-28 non-local tuition fees, with the average increase standing at 17 per cent compared with the current academic year.
The cumulative hike for 2027-28 represents a 41 per cent rise since 2023-24, when the non-local quota stood at 20 per cent of local places.

deduped_items.body_text:
Hong Kong public universities’ non-local fees jump by up to 26% as quota expands
HKU medicine, dentistry fees more than double to HK$590,000, with online users on RedNote saying hikes are ‘going too far’
Hong Kong public universities will raise undergraduate tuition fees for non-local students by up to 26 per cent in the 2027-28 academic year, marking the sharpest increase in recent years as institutions adjust to an expanded quota.
Non-local students admitted to the University of Hong Kong’s (HKU) medicine and dentistry programmes will face the steepest jump, with annual tuition rising by 137 per cent to HK$590,000 (US$75,187) to recover the high costs of clinical training.
Seven of the eight public universities have published their 2027-28 non-local tuition fees, with the average increase standing at 17 per cent compared with the current academic year.
The cumulative hike for 2027-28 represents a 41 per cent rise since 2023-24, when the non-local quota stood at 20 per cent of local places.

Seven of the eight public universities have published their 2027-28 non-local tuition fees, with the average increase standing at 17 per cent compared with the current academic year.
The cumulative hike for 2027-28 represents a 41 per cent rise since 2023-24, when the non-local quota stood at 20 per cent of local places.

deduped_items.title: Foreign language files land three North Korean youth league officials in custody
deduped_items.summary: North Korean authorities have arrested three youth league officials in Pyongyang over unauthorized foreign materials on their computers. The case opens a new front in the regime’s 2026 crackdown on outside information, which now reaches the cadres tasked with policing young people. The three officials worked for the Pyongyang branch of the Socialist Patriotic Youth […]
deduped_items.body_text:
North Korean authorities have arrested three youth league officials in Pyongyang over unauthorized foreign materials on their computers. The case opens a new front in the regime’s 2026 crackdown on outside information, which now reaches the cadres tasked with policing young people.
The three officials worked for the Pyongyang branch of the Socialist Patriotic Youth League, which is the Workers’ Party of Korea’s mass organization for young people between the ages of 14 and 30. The organization oversees the ideological education of North Korean youth and serves as a key pipeline into party membership.
“On Sept. 20, an anti-socialist inspection group carried out a surprise check of computers used by city youth league officials,” a source in Pyongyang told Daily NK on Thursday. “They found many foreign technical documents and books that the state had never approved for use. There were also foreign language study materials that copied South Korean and Chinese writing conventions and expressions. Three officials from the city youth league were arrested as a result.”
Anti-socialist inspection groups are joint task forces drawing on party, police and prosecution personnel. The regime dispatches them to root out what it calls anti-socialist behavior, often with no advance notice.
The inspectors showed up without warning at the officials’ workplace and went straight through their computers, according to the source. They singled out unapproved foreign technical documents and books that the officials had saved as image files.
The computers also held a range of technical standards along with explanatory materials on international law, and some of these files had been encrypted or tucked away in hidden folders on the machines. That effort at concealment made the case look even more serious to the inspectors, the source said.
What alarmed the inspectors most were the language study materials modeled on South Korean and Chinese spelling and phrasing. They labeled the files “anti-socialist cultural material” and claimed that keeping them violated the Reactionary Ideology and Culture Rejection Law.
North Korea enacted that law in December 2020 to stamp out foreign media and culture, particularly from South Korea. Its penalties include long terms in labor camps and, in the most serious cases, the death penalty.
Youth league officials arrested in broad daylight
“The inspection group arrested the three youth league officials on the spot,” the source said. “They tied their hands with rope and led them away in broad daylight. Other officials who watched it happen were shocked, and atmosphere in the whole office became extremely tense.”
Youth league officials are expected to educate young people and set an example for them to follow, which makes the discovery especially damaging for the organization and for those who supervise it.
Concern is now growing that their superiors will face collective responsibility and punishment as well, the source said, adding that many officials also fear that further inspections will soon follow across the league.
The inspection followed a recent directive from the party’s Central Committee on people with prior convictions that ordered tighter monitoring of anyone punished under the Reactionary Ideology and Culture Rejection Law or the Youth Education Guarantee Law.
Pyongyang adopted the youth education law in 2021 to police the speech, dress and thinking of young North Koreans with a view to shield them from foreign influences, especially South Korean culture and slang.
Kim Jong Un’s government appears to see a grave threat in league officials secretly consuming outside information as these are the very people charged with indoctrinating young North Koreans in party ideology. That concern seems to have pushed the authorities to widen the crackdown to include league officials themselves.

deduped_items.title: David Fifita leads Australia in wild mismatch against PNG
deduped_items.summary: Australia and captain David Fifita have routed Papua New Guinea in the annual Prime Minister's XIII game in Port Moresby, while winger Jada Taylor has put her hand up for a World Cup berth after the women's team handed PNG a record loss.
deduped_items.body_text:
Fri, 11 Sept, 7:50 pm, Final score, Rabbitohs 10, Knights 20
Prime Minister's XIIIs thrash PNG in 11- and 12-try victories in Port Moresby
A rag-tag Australian side has outclassed Papua New Guinea 60-10 in the annual Prime Minister's XIII clash in Port Moresby.
The Australians scored 11 tries and exposed the PNG side's defensive frailties almost at will in what was the 20th men's Prime Minister's XIII match.
It was hardly a conventional game at the National Football Stadium on Saturday, with Australia switching on and off as players became accustomed to their makeshift position.
Ezra Mam spent time at fullback. Jock Madden appeared to be playing on an edge. Jamal Fogarty stood in the centres, and Josh Curran kicked a goal.
At one stage they had three regular hookers on the field.
In one piece of consistency, captain David Fifita started and finished the match as a devastating left centre.
Commentator Cooper Cronk mused it was coach Ben Teo's way of keeping the Aussies engaged after a long, hard season.
It was at times chaotic and they dropped the ball a lot, but it was fun. Less so for the PNG side, who were not just outclassed but also ill-disciplined, missing 47 tackles — 28 in the first half alone.
With the PNG Chiefs' arrival in the NRL fast approaching, it is clear the next level of local players are still a long way from that standard.
On a positive note, earlier on Saturday the Junior Kumuls scored a historic first win over the Australian Schoolboys, 18-10.
If Kangaroos coach Kevin Walters hasn't settled on his squad for this month's Rugby League World Cup, several players put their hands up.
Regular back-rower Fifita, who showed his class and power in the centres on Saturday, first appeared in the PM's XIII game seven years ago and looked destined for higher honours that never arrived. Maybe that time is approaching again.
Mam and fellow half Lachlan Galvin showed more than one glimpse of their brilliance, while hulking front-rower Tom Hazelton was one of the best players on the field.
For former NRL and current London Broncos coach Jason Demetriou, who will guide the PNG Kumuls at the World Cup, there was not a lot to love.
Sylvester Namo should be there, while uncapped centre Stanford Talita and fullback Sanny Wabo were dangerous at times and could find their way into Demetriou's squad.
In the women's game, Australia was also successful, dishing out a 66-6 thumping of their hosts.
PNG might have scored for the first time in three years, but Australia was a class above, crossing for 12 tries to one to rack up the biggest winning margin in the fixture's history.
While the standard of PNG's second-tier players has improved alongside the growth of the national women's competition, the Santos Cup, so too has that of the Australians.
Several showed they would not be out of place if called up to coach Jess Skinner's Jillaroos for this month's 2026 Rugby League World Cup.
Jada Taylor scored three tries and was almost impossible to handle at times, showing her versatility by playing on the wing, despite playing her club football at fullback.
Half Kasey Reh, centre Tahlia O'Brien, hooker Taneka Todhunter and back-rower Tayla Preston were others who impressed in what was effectively an audition in front of Skinner for a grander stage.
PNG Orchids coach Craig Sandercock, who this year guided Wests Tigers to their first NRLW finals series, would also have enjoyed the opportunity to see the next generation of PNG players.
There was no doubt they were outclassed, and they struggled for time with the ball, having just 37 per cent possession.
However, they had an 85 per cent completion rate and tried hard in defence, before tiring late in each half.
AAP

deduped_items.title: One Nation vows to abolish First Nations treaty and legalise pepper spray at Victorian campaign launch
deduped_items.summary: Candidate Mark Nicholson said former premiers Daniel Andrews and Jacinta Allan would be ‘in prison by Christmas’ if One Nation won the electionGet our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcastOne Nation has launched its Victorian election campaign, vowing to legalise the personal use of pepper spray, abolish the state’s treaty with Indigenous people, and scrap payroll tax in regional Victoria.A social media post announcing its policy to “make it cheaper and easier to set up new busines
deduped_items.body_text:
One Nation has launched its Victorian election campaign, vowing to legalise the personal use of pepper spray, abolish the state’s treaty with Indigenous people, and scrap payroll tax in regional Victoria.
A social media post announcing its policy to “make it cheaper and easier to set up new businesses in Victoria” featured an AI-generated image of a “taaditional [sic] fish n’chips” shop.
One Nation used its official campaign launch at Crown Casino to unveil candidates for the state’s upper house and all 88 lower house electorates.
These candidates include a former Liberal who has won support from alleged underworld figures, a naturopath who has endorsed Donald Trump’s unfounded claim that paracetamol is linked to autism and a former shire councillor who lost his licence for drink-driving.
The party is understood to have again prevented reporters from certain media outlets from attending the launch. It has previously barred the ABC, Guardian, and the Age from its media events. The Guardian did not attempt to attend Saturday’s launch.
The Herald Sun reported that Northern Metropolitan candidate and creator of the party’s Please Explain Cartoon, Mark Nicholson, vowed at the launch that if One Nation won the election, former premiers Daniel Andrews and Jacinta Allan would be “in prison by Christmas”.
Details of other policies were scant online, but a 63-page document was reportedly circulated at the event that included plans to “gang up on gangs”.
Images of the document show it was described as One Nation’s policy platform and “The Real Deal for Victoria”, with a focus on restoring safety, prosperity and trust.
According to the party’s website on Saturday afternoon, an “update [was] in progress” regarding its crime policy.
The party’s Victorian state president, Warren Pickering, told radio 3AW Melbourne on Friday that crime and bail remained a top priority for One Nation.
“[It] is the key issue in the state right now and people need to feel safe in their homes and places of work once more,” he said.
“You make that happen by taking a pragmatic approach, not an expensive one, to ensuring we get more police on the streets, get our empty stations manned and ensure bail laws and sentences are fitting with the crimes.”
The party claimed in social media posts that more than 1,000 people attended the launch, but other estimates put the crowd at several hundred lower than that. A smaller group of protesters outside were monitored by police.
The party has come under fire for practices that could see it collect as much as $633,000 from people who have nominated for the Victorian election, with some potential candidates questioning whether the party is staging a “cash grab”.
While the party has fashioned itself as representing the working class, its founder Pauline Hanson has faced a series of revelations about her links to billionaire Gina Rinehart, including exclusive use of a private jet, and staying at her multimillion-dollar homes.
– Additional reporting by Australian Associated Press

deduped_items.body_text:
One Nation has launched its Victorian election campaign, vowing to legalise the personal use of pepper spray, abolish the state’s treaty with Indigenous people, and scrap payroll tax in regional Victoria.
A social media post announcing its policy to “make it cheaper and easier to set up new businesses in Victoria” featured an AI-generated image of a “taaditional [sic] fish n’chips” shop.
One Nation used its official campaign launch at Crown Casino to unveil candidates for the state’s upper house and all 88 lower house electorates.
These candidates include a former Liberal who has won support from alleged underworld figures, a naturopath who has endorsed Donald Trump’s unfounded claim that paracetamol is linked to autism and a former shire councillor who lost his licence for drink-driving.
The party is understood to have again prevented reporters from certain media outlets from attending the launch. It has previously barred the ABC, Guardian, and the Age from its media events. The Guardian did not attempt to attend Saturday’s launch.
The Herald Sun reported that Northern Metropolitan candidate and creator of the party’s Please Explain Cartoon, Mark Nicholson, vowed at the launch that if One Nation won the election, former premiers Daniel Andrews and Jacinta Allan would be “in prison by Christmas”.
Details of other policies were scant online, but a 63-page document was reportedly circulated at the event that included plans to “gang up on gangs”.
Images of the document show it was described as One Nation’s policy platform and “The Real Deal for Victoria”, with a focus on restoring safety, prosperity and trust.
According to the party’s website on Saturday afternoon, an “update [was] in progress” regarding its crime policy.
The party’s Victorian state president, Warren Pickering, told radio 3AW Melbourne on Friday that crime and bail remained a top priority for One Nation.
“[It] is the key issue in the state right now and people need to feel safe in their homes and places of work once more,” he said.
“You make that happen by taking a pragmatic approach, not an expensive one, to ensuring we get more police on the streets, get our empty stations manned and ensure bail laws and sentences are fitting with the crimes.”
The party claimed in social media posts that more than 1,000 people attended the launch, but other estimates put the crowd at several hundred lower than that. A smaller group of protesters outside were monitored by police.
The party has come under fire for practices that could see it collect as much as $633,000 from people who have nominated for the Victorian election, with some potential candidates questioning whether the party is staging a “cash grab”.
While the party has fashioned itself as representing the working class, its founder Pauline Hanson has faced a series of revelations about her links to billionaire Gina Rinehart, including exclusive use of a private jet, and staying at her multimillion-dollar homes.
– Additional reporting by Australian Associated Press

deduped_items.summary: Western Libya’s GNU say working with Saddam Haftar ‘impossible’ as US-backed merger plan breaks downAllegations that the son of the Libyan warlord Khalifa Haftar oversaw a “terror cell” that launched drone attacks on fuel storage facilities and power stations in western Libya have upended plans for the Tripoli-based government of national unity (GNU) to continue cooperating with Haftar on a plan to unify the country.Saddam Haftar, the deputy commander of the so-called Libyan National Army (LNA),
deduped_items.body_text:
Allegations that the son of the Libyan warlord Khalifa Haftar oversaw a “terror cell” that launched drone attacks on fuel storage facilities and power stations in western Libya have upended plans for the Tripoli-based government of national unity (GNU) to continue cooperating with Haftar on a plan to unify the country.
Saddam Haftar, the deputy commander of the so-called Libyan National Army (LNA), has increasingly been seen by the US as an important figure in its plans to unify Libyan security, judicial and political institutions.
But a round of drone attacks in August worsened electricity blackouts in the west of the country, putting intense popular pressure on the GNU led by the prime minister, Abdul Hamid Dbeibah.
Libya has been split between the east, dominated by Haftar, and the west, governed by the GNU, since the fall of Col Muammar Gaddafi in 2011, leaving the oil-rich country at the mercy of corruption, militia, migrant traffickers and myriad external actors.
Donald Trump’s Africa adviser, Massad Boulos, has hatched a plan to unify the two Libyan governments in which Haftar from the east would take on the role of president and a member of the Dbeibah family from the west would become prime minister.
Boulos has insisted he is not trying a quick fix that entrenches family elites in Libya. “It’s not about families or names,” Boulos said when asked about the reported Haftar-Dbeibah deal, before adding: “At the end of the day, those are individuals that have to be in one position or the other.”
But the drone strikes, it is claimed, were prompted by Haftar’s anger at Dbeibah apparently stalling on the Boulos merger plan and by Tripoli allegedly encouraging tribes in southern Libya to attack and kill his forces.
Over more than five days in August, drones attacked the Zawiya oil station and fuel storage facilities in western Libya. The drone strikes hit the gasoline-storage tank at the Zawiya oil complex, west of Tripoli, causing a large fire and the tank’s collapse. The tank held approximately 4.5m litres of fuel when it was struck, according to Libya’s National Oil Corporation.
On 5 September, three Libyans and one Spanish citizen were arrested in southern Tripoli by the GNU for their alleged role in a plot that was intended to include an attack on Tripoli airport. It was thought the whole group involved five Spaniards and four Libyans. The three arrested Libyans were allegedly affiliated with the Tareq ben Ziyad brigade, an LNA formation. Information that has emerged from interviews about the plot, and Saddam Haftar’s alleged role, not just in Libya, has been described as a goldmine, capable of weakening Khalifa Haftar.
Sources in the GNU said the alleged plotters were working for Saddam Haftar. “No formal decision has been made, but in light of what has been discovered it is impossible to work with Saddam,” the sources said.
The claims not only damage Saddam Haftar’s role in the Boulos plan but also the parallel UN sponsored 4+4 talks involving the main four political institutions in Libya that led to an August agreement to stage elections within two years. The deal endorsed by the UN security council overcomes previous obstacles to elections, and had been backed by the main actors capable of delivering the change.
Walid Ellafi, minister for state for political affairs in the UN-backed Libyan GNU and an enthusiast for elections, said: “Our support for the 4+4 process is rooted in its role as a UN sponsored framework offering a new approach to achieving practical results that pave the way for elections and institutions whose political legitimacy derives from the will of the people – not as a political settlement that overlooks violations or sets aside the rights of those affected.”
He opposes an elite east-west political deal that brushes aside longstanding grievances such as the displacement of 9,000 families in Benghazi during the 2014 war.

They can also have a big impact on Americans' personal finances and on the broader economy. The bond market can dictate how much ordinary people have to pay on their mortgages and car loans, as well as how much they earn from their savings accounts and 401(k) plans.

deduped_items.summary: Admiramos a quienes se juegan a fondo y ponen el cuerpo ante lo que deben hacer, por más difícil que resulte. Aunque no estamos preparados para trances así, de pronto la vida, sin que lo busquemos, nos pone ante encrucijadas que no hay forma de esquivar y que no admiten grises ni términos medios. De un modo u otro, a todos nos llega el desafío, esa hora de la verdad que suele cifrarse en una decisión o en un acto trascendental que reclama una valentía que nos supera. Pero el ser humano es paradó

deduped_items.title: Venezuelans Won’t Get Liberty Until We “Get” Liberty
deduped_items.summary: Long-awaited freedom won’t be realized if we fail to address the power inequalities that plagued us long before chavismo
deduped_items.body_text:
Venezuelans Won’t Get Liberty Until We “Get” Liberty
Long-awaited freedom won’t be realized if we fail to address the power inequalities that plagued us long before chavismo
When Maduro was taken and arrested on January 3rd, many Venezuelans brought out the good stuff. The old bottle of rum or whiskey they’d been saving for a special occasion, believing the incursion would inevitably lead to the return of liberty in Venezuela. Nine months later, the “transition” has not been what most Venezuelans wanted. Hundreds of political prisoners were released, but that is not enough. A few laws are being reformed, but not the institutions that carry them out. Delcy remains in power despite no lawful statute allowing it nor any sort of popular mandate for her to be the head of the Venezuelan State.
Many who brought out the good whiskey have soured on the transition, or at the very least lost their shiny optimism. But the mistake was not just to believe in a future that now seems a bit naive, but to yearn for the return of a past which was the precursor to our current tragic state.
The quest for a more liberal society
Yes, we were better off before the 2000s, but we’ve never had a truly free society without clientelism or corruption. Chavismo may have perfected the art of corruption in Venezuela, but they certainly did not invent it. Venezuela, since its inception, has not been able to ameliorate the very Latin American issue of inequalities of power. We tend to forget about the problem during oil bonanzas. Everyone is doing better, right? Why worry? Then the oil price inevitably falls, the party stops, the lights turn on and we see the naked truth that we are in a horrible state of disrepair.
Many say that the Venezuelan problem is economic (lack of diversification or investment in non-oil industries), political (once high polarization and weak rule of law), or even cultural (a tendency towards el guiso). But within these lies a deeper philosophical issue: for a society that claims to love liberty and our libertadores as much as we do, we don’t actually understand what it takes to create a liberal society.
This is hardly a Venezuela-specific issue, but we are a unique case in that so much of our self-perception is based on the idea of a people who achieved freedom from the yoke of Spanish tyranny, only to then continue to liberate other countries in South America, making Simón Bolívar the most famous person in the history of the continent.
What room is there to become “more liberal” once all citizens are recognized by the law and there is universal suffrage?
To understand what it means to be a liberal society, perhaps it would be best to understand what it means to be a more liberal society. When the classical liberal revolutions of the 18th and 19th centuries took place, it was the divine right of kings that fell. The power was taken from an individual and shared amongst parliaments, which were at the time controlled almost exclusively by rich landowners (including our own first few republics). Still, this was unquestionably a redistribution of power from the individual to the few. It took a long time, but eventually this distribution of power from the one to the few became a distribution of power from the few to the many. Nowadays, democratic societies are expected to allow every single citizen to vote, but this is a reality that is younger than the oldest person alive today. When English supercentenarian Ethel Caterham in the UK was born in 1909, her mother would not have been allowed to vote.
Liberal societies today hardly even question the idea that all people should be equal in respect to the law and that we ought to have a voice in the decisions of our country through voting. So what room is there to become “more liberal” once all citizens are recognized by the law and there is universal suffrage?

deduped_items.title: How Powerful Should Venezuela’s Next President Be?
deduped_items.summary: Venezuela needs to dismantle the presidency chavismo built without creating a government too weak to rebuild the country
deduped_items.body_text:
How Powerful Should Venezuela’s Next President Be?
Venezuela needs to dismantle the presidency chavismo built without creating a government too weak to rebuild the country
Photo: Acting President Ramón J. Velásquez (1993–1994) and his cabinet on the last day of his term. Dr. Velásquez, both during his brief tenure and previously at the helm of a special commission, was a leading proponent of decentralization in the late 20th-century. | Source: Archivo Fotografía Urbana.
The next democratically elected president of Venezuela will inherit an office that is simultaneously too powerful and not powerful enough.
Too powerful because decades of centralization have placed extraordinary political, fiscal and administrative authority in Miraflores. Not powerful enough because whoever inherits it will also confront a damaged bureaucracy, weak public services, deteriorated infrastructure and institutions that may still be controlled by political adversaries.
That combination will make concentration tempting.
A new government will have an enormous reconstruction mandate and voters impatient for results. Every institutional restraint will risk looking like another obstacle left behind by chavismo. Decentralization can wait until the State is stabilized. Congressional procedures can wait because the crisis is urgent. Extraordinary executive authorities can be justified because ordinary government is too slow.
Many of those arguments will contain some truth.
That is what makes them dangerous.
Chávez inherited Venezuela’s presidentialist political culture and radicalized it.
If Venezuela wants this transition to be the last one it needs, the country cannot simply transfer the powers accumulated in the presidency to someone more democratic. But neither can it respond to authoritarianism by constructing an executive incapable of governing.
The question is not whether Venezuela needs a strong president or a weak one. It needs to decide what the president should actually be strong enough to do.
Miraflores was powerful before Chávez
Chavismo radically expanded executive power, but it did not invent Venezuelan presidentialism.
Long before Hugo Chávez, the presidency occupied an unusually commanding position over the political system. Oil reinforced that arrangement. Whoever controlled the national government controlled the principal source of public revenue, and the ability to distribute that revenue made Caracas not merely the political center of Venezuela but the financial center on which much of the rest of the government depended.
The result was a particular understanding of political effectiveness. Presidents were expected to not merely administer the executive branch but to solve national problems, distribute resources, arbitrate conflicts and impose direction on the State.
Chávez inherited that culture and radicalized it.
Carlos Rangel would have recognized something familiar in the phenomenon. His critique of Latin American political culture repeatedly returned to the attraction of the providential leader: the politician whose extraordinary personal mandate supposedly allows him to rise above institutions that appear slow, compromised or incapable of producing the transformation the country requires.
A new democracy has to be built for the political society Venezuela actually has.
Chavismo gave that tradition a twenty-first-century vocabulary. The leader possessed a direct relationship with the people. Institutions that resisted him therefore did not represent legitimate constraints on democratic power; they interfered with the popular mandate.
That logic did not begin with Chávez, and removing chavismo will not automatically remove it.
This is one reason institutional design matters more than hoping Venezuela will simply develop a different political culture. deduped_items.summary: Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi, regional, and international technology enterprises showcased cutting-edge solutions in artificial intelligence, network synchronization, and enterprise digital transformation during their participation in the Iraq International Information and […] The post ITEX 2026: Iraqi AI and tech startups expand appeared first on Iraqi News.
deduped_items.body_text:
ITEX 2026: Iraqi AI and tech startups expand
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi, regional, and international technology enterprises showcased cutting-edge solutions in artificial intelligence, network synchronization, and enterprise digital transformation during their participation in the Iraq International Information and Communications Technology Exhibition in Baghdad.
The participating companies expressed strong ambition to expand operations and capture growing commercial opportunities in Iraq’s rapidly developing technological sector.
Hassan Abdul-Baqi Khalaf, founder of domestic startup Al-Burhan for AI Image and Video Recognition, told the Iraqi News Agency (INA) that the venture originated from registered patents specializing in automated media verification and tamper protection against digital forgery and deepfakes.
Khalaf—a computer science student at the American University of Iraq – Baghdad (AUIB) collaborating with a doctoral partner in mathematics and physics—highlighted that their platform processes requests for more than 3,000 daily active users across private corporate clients and the public.
Delivering up to 95 percent accuracy in identifying manipulated content, the company is leveraging its inaugural exhibition presence to pursue operational partnerships with federal entities, specifically the Ministry of Interior, to detect fabricated media and enhance sovereign cyber verification tools.
International infrastructure providers also underscored their entry into the domestic market. Engineer Ahmed Mustafa of Canada’s Al-Mamas, an IT and network engineering specialist, revealed that the firm is seeking to establish an operational foothold in Iraq following successful deployments in the UAE, Qatar, and Egypt.
Al-Mamas holds exclusive distribution rights across the Middle East and North Africa for precision German-manufactured timing and synchronization hardware, which is critical for maintaining ultra-low-latency architectures across telecommunications networks, industrial automation, data center facilities, and distributed artificial intelligence systems.
Highlighting regional corporate expansion, Samer Al-Yasin, sales director for Qatar-headquartered conglomerate Mannai Corporation, affirmed that Iraq represents a fertile and attractive destination for long-term tech investment.
Marking its second exhibition appearance in Baghdad, Mannai—which employs over 15,000 personnel across the Gulf—formally established its Baghdad branch three months ago and is actively preparing to launch regional offices in Erbil and Basra.
Al-Yasin emphasized that the group is deploying enterprise digital transformation, cloud integration, and systems architecture tailored for federal ministries, banking institutions, and healthcare providers, aiming to transfer its regional technical expertise to drive national modernization and support sovereign institutional revenues.

deduped_items.title: How do I empathise with my Lebanese friend?, By Osmund Agbo

Eine Drohne mit Sprengstoff an einer ukrainischen Frachtmaschine in Leipzig, Explosionen in Munitionsfabriken und Sabotage auf See. Russland intensiviert seine hybride Kriegsführung mitten in Europa und testet gezielt die roten Linien der NATO. Doch was passiert, wenn ein solcher Anschlag auf deutschem Boden tatsächlich gelingt und den Bündnisfall auslöst? Darüber spricht Gordon Repinski in dieser Folge mit Carlo Masala, Professor für Internationale Politik, Universität der Bundeswehr München.
Das Ziel des Kremls ist es, Panik zu schüren und die westliche Unterstützung für die Ukraine zu brechen. Im Gespräch analysiert Carlo, warum Putin gerade jetzt risikofreudiger wird und weshalb Friedrich Merz in der deutschen Debatte als entscheidender Schutzwall für weitere Hilfen gilt. Ein Wegbrechen dieser Unterstützung hätte fatale finanzielle und militärische Folgen für den gesamten Kontinent.
Gleichzeitig wächst der Druck auf Kiew massiv. Die Episode beleuchtet, wie eine mögliche Rückkehr von Trump ins Weiße Haus die Ukraine zu schmerzhaften Deals zwingen könnte und warum das europäische Superwahljahr 2027 Moskau eine beispiellose Chance bietet, die politische Landschaft endgültig zu seinen Gunsten zu drehen.

deduped_items.title: Dozens of men failed to stop an alleged gang rape at Cornell – here’s the misperception that keeps bystanders from intervening and how to short-circuit it

deduped_items.body_text:
As an undergrad student decades ago, I attended a dorm presentation describing the importance of giving and receiving sexual consent. The workshop leaders explained that if your partner said “no” or “stop” but you proceeded to have sex anyway, it was considered rape.
A high-profile athlete on campus raised his hand and said, in utter disbelief, “That can’t be right. By that definition, everyone I’ve ever had sex with I’ve raped.”
I was horrified by his comment, but most students laughed. He clearly saw nothing wrong with the view he’d expressed, presumably believing it was widely shared.
I immediately thought of this experience when I heard about the alleged sexual assault committed by seven fraternity members at Cornell University. As a social psychologist, and the author of a book examining why so-called good people stay silent in the face of problematic behavior, what I find most tragic about the events at Cornell is that reportedly over 50 men on a group chat learned about the assault as it was happening. Yet there’s been no public report that any of them tried to stop the assault, help the victim or contact campus or local police departments.
This type of inaction is very common. In about one-third of sexual assaults, at least one other person is present who potentially could intervene but in most instances chooses not to. Why?
Misperceiving that you’re the only one
Data suggests a minority of men actually commit sexual assault. Researchers estimate about 6.5% of male college students in the United States and Canada have committed rape. Yet many men who find sexual violence offensive mistakenly believe that other men do not.
Undergraduate men in one study reported their beliefs about common rape myths, such as “If a girl doesn’t physically fight back, you can’t really say it was rape,” and “If a girl goes to a room alone with a guy at a party, it is her own fault if she is raped.” Researchers then asked participants how they thought both their close friends and average male college students would answer these same questions.
The results provided clear evidence that college men have skewed views of what those around them are thinking. Most students saw their classmates and friends as more supportive of rape myths than they themselves were.
Unfortunately, believing that other men generally accept sexual violence – even when this belief is wrong – inhibits their willingness to intervene to stop such behavior when they encounter it. In fact, men’s beliefs about their peers’ attitudes are a stronger predictor of their willingness to intervene than their own stated attitudes about sexual aggression.
What’s behind these mistaken beliefs
Men who underestimate their peers’ discomfort with sexually aggressive behavior often fear the consequences of calling out problematic views or intervening in the face of inappropriate behavior. The most common reason male college students give for failing to intervene in situations involving sexual violence is a fear of being laughed at or ridiculed – in particular, a desire not to appear weak to other men.
Men who actually commit assault also tend to overestimate support for such behavior. Not surprisingly, men who report having committed sexual assault believe that other men are more accepting of such behavior and have engaged in such behavior themselves.
This assumed support leads them to feel comfortable describing problematic behavior, which leads other men to believe that sexual violence is more common, and more accepted, than it actually is.
Resetting a social norm
Given the consistent evidence that men wrongly believe that most men are more comfortable with sexual violence than they themselves are, the challenge is not to change the social norm. It’s getting people to see what it actually already is.
Correcting such misperceptions can go a long way toward reducing sexual violence. First-year male college students who participate in a 90-minute sexual assault prevention program – focused

Speaking to Israel’s Channel 14, Ben Gvir said that, if appointed defence minister, he would work to dismantle the Palestinian Authority an
deduped_items.body_text:
'The entire land is ours': Ben Gvir escalates calls for annexation of occupied West Bank
Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir claimed that the entire occupied West Bank “belongs to Israel” and has vowed to dismantle the Palestinian Authority and pursue the displacement of Palestinians if he becomes defence minister, Israeli media have reported.
Speaking to Israel’s Channel 14, Ben Gvir said that, if appointed defence minister, he would work to dismantle the Palestinian Authority and push for Palestinians to leave the occupied West Bank and Gaza.
The minister said that 60 percent of Palestinians want to “emigrate”.
“I will dedicate time to this, and I will manage the process continuously. Every week, I will hold a discussion involving all relevant parties,” he said. “There is no difference between Areas A, B and C. The entire land is ours."
Under the territorial framework established in the Oslo agreement between Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organisation in 1995, Areas A and B were placed under varying degrees of Palestinian jurisdiction, while Israel retained control over Area C.

deduped_items.body_text:
Gaza death toll rises after seven Palestinians killed in 24 hours
Gaza's death toll has reached 74,229 after seven more Palestinians were killed by Israel in the last 24 hours, the enclave's health ministry reports.
The ministry said that seven Palestinians have been killed and 20 others wounded in Israeli attacks in the last 24 hours. The figure includes two people who succumbed to injuries from previous attacks and one whose body was retrieved from rubble.
According to the ministry, some 1,445 Palestinians have been killed, 5,052 wounded and 835 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble since the so-called "ceasefire" came into effect in October 2024.
On Thursday, thousands gathered for a mass funeral for over 100 bodies belonging to victims trapped beneath the debris of a residential tower, which was flattened by Israeli strikes at the beginning of the genocide in October 2023.

Speaking to Israel’s Channel 14, Ben Gvir said that, if appointed defence minister, he would work to dismantle the Palestinian Authority an
deduped_items.body_text:
'The entire land is ours': Ben Gvir escalates calls for annexation of occupied West Bank
Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir claimed that the entire occupied West Bank “belongs to Israel” and has vowed to dismantle the Palestinian Authority and pursue the displacement of Palestinians if he becomes defence minister, Israeli media have reported.
Speaking to Israel’s Channel 14, Ben Gvir said that, if appointed defence minister, he would work to dismantle the Palestinian Authority and push for Palestinians to leave the occupied West Bank and Gaza.
The minister said that 60 percent of Palestinians want to “emigrate”.
“I will dedicate time to this, and I will manage the process continuously. Every week, I will hold a discussion involving all relevant parties,” he said. “There is no difference between Areas A, B and C. The entire land is ours."
Under the territorial framework established in the Oslo agreement between Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organisation in 1995, Areas A and B were placed under varying degrees of Palestinian jurisdiction, while Israel retained control over Area C.

deduped_items.body_text:
Capacity Substitution: How Tunisia’s Problems Became Someone Else’s Priorities
In the summer of 2023, a young man from Gafsa tried to cross the Mediterranean on a small boat. He did not make it. His story is one of thousands — and it is increasingly understood by Tunisian institutions through the language of border management. It is also a story about who defines what a problem is.
In June 2023, the European Commission announced a package for Tunisia: up to €900 million in proposed macro-financial assistance, €150 million in budget support, and €100 million for border management, search and rescue, anti-smuggling, and returns. In July, the EU and Tunisia signed a Memorandum of Understanding formalising the partnership. By September, a further €105 million was allocated to migration-related programmes. By December, the €150 million budget-support programme was operational.
The sequence is documented. What it produces institutionally is less visible. This article examines a mechanism I call capacity substitution. Capacity building strengthens a state’s ability to solve its own problems. Capacity substitution makes a state more efficient at solving problems defined by someone else. The distinction is simple. Its consequences are not.
Consider Tunisia’s migration apparatus. The EU–Tunisia Memorandum links European support to border management, anti-smuggling operations, search and rescue, and returns. These are legitimate European objectives. They are also objectives that European institutions can define, fund, monitor, and measure. European support has equipped units, funded training, and strengthened interception capacity.
What it has not done — and was not designed to do — is strengthen Tunisia’s capacity to address the economic conditions that generate migration. Youth unemployment stood at 35.4 percent in 2026. Graduate unemployment was 26.6 percent. Regional inequality remains entrenched.
The argument is not that European funding caused these figures. It is that external funding concentrates institutional development on a specific set of functions. Those functions become better equipped, better staffed, and more internationally connected. The functions that would address the structural conditions producing migration are not developed through an equivalent institutional investment. This is what capacity substitution describes.
A young unemployed person in Gafsa is unlikely to attempt to cross the Mediterranean simply because Tunisia lacks another surveillance system. The deeper driver is the narrowing of his economic and social horizon. If institutional capacity is concentrated on managing his departure, while the capacities that would address the conditions producing it are not developed through an equivalent investment, then the state becomes more effective at managing the symptom. It remains structurally less equipped to govern the cause. It does not require coercion. It does not require a conspiracy. It only requires that the external priority be better resourced than the domestic one.
Migration is not the only domain where this mechanism operates. European energy cooperation with Tunisia is another. EU funding for renewable energy, electricity interconnection, and green hydrogen is increasingly organised around projects that also serve European energy security: cross-Mediterranean interconnection such as the ELMED project, export capacity, and the decarbonisation of European supply chains.
Domestic energy challenges subsidy reform, grid reliability, and energy poverty are not absent from the relationship. But they are not the organising priority around which much of the external financing is structured. The result is a similar pattern: institutional capacity is strengthened in functions that serve externally defined priorities, while capacities addressing domestic structural conditions do not necessarily receive an equivalent institutional investment.
What migration and energy share is not a conspiracy. It is a logic. Ex

What Washington Agreed to Last Month
Somaliland’s president spent two weeks in Washington this month offering almost everything he has. Access to the port at Berbera. Access to the territory’s minerals. Military access, which he called a matter for negotiation and declined to rule out. He only asked for one thing in return. Recognition. He went home without it. The same month, the United States secured expanded security rights in Greenland and agreed in writing that sovereignty stays with Denmark.
What Somaliland Offered
Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi, known as Irro, arrived on September 5 for his first visit to the United States since winning Somaliland’s presidency in November 2024. On the 14th, he gave the keynote address at the Hudson Institute, at an event titled Somaliland as a Strategic Partner in the Horn of Africa.
His pitch was the seaport. Irro described Berbera as a modern deep water facility that United States Africa Command had already assessed and in which the Emirati operator DP World has invested $442 million. More than twelve percent of global maritime trade passes through the Bab el-Mandeb strait every day. He argued that Somaliland has protected its coastline from militants and pirates for three decades without any recognition at all.
Two days later he went further. In an interview with Semafor he said Somaliland was not giving anything away for free. He offered American investors the port and the minerals. On military access he said it was a matter for negotiation, and he would not rule out a future base agreement. Ten days later he added more. In an interview with the Council on Foreign Relations he suggested renaming Berbera International Airport after President Trump, having earlier floated a Trump Tower in Hargeisa.
What They Got
Nothing, so far. Irro himself said there is no American promise on recognition. A source told Politico there is no change in American policy towards Somaliland.
On September 16, China warned Irro that crossing its line on Taiwan would bring serious consequences, and publicly affirmed that Somaliland remains part of Somalia. That handed Mogadishu an endorsement from a permanent member of the Security Council in the middle of a rival’s tour.
The Hudson appearance also drew criticism at home. Clips circulated of Irro hesitating on questions about minerals and regional security. The event’s moderator, Joshua Meservey of the Hudson Institute, said afterwards that Irro had made the right argument, while also observing that Somaliland has not consistently made the case for the reason recognition is necessary.
What Happened For Greenland
On the evening of September 18, President Trump announced an agreement with Denmark and Greenland giving the United States permanent control over security in Greenland. He described it as an agreement with no end, at no cost. The three governments signed it in New York on September 22, and the White House released the text the same day.
Copenhagen and Nuuk described something narrower. Greenland’s prime minister, Jens-Frederik Nielsen, said the agreement recognises the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Kingdom and the right of Greenlanders to self-determination. A State Department official told CBS News it gives permanent access and overflight rights, allows more bases and bars non-NATO members from building their own.
None of this is new ground. American forces have been in Greenland since 1941, and a 1951 defence agreement gave the United States the right to operate bases there, with Danish sovereignty expressly preserved. Reading the text signed this month, ABC News reported that it does not appear to add materially to that access. What Washington secured was a broader scope and a bar on rival powers. The access itself it already had.

deduped_items.body_text:
African Newsrooms Can No Longer Delay Creating the Conditions for Women to Stay
When one Black South African journalist decided to leave the profession after only four years, she did not walk away because she had stopped believing in journalism: ‘I mourned because I knew I could have done so much in that space.’
Her experience is documented in a 2025 Reuters Institute fellowship paper by South African journalist Bongekile Macupe. After difficult experiences in the newsroom, including during her pregnancy, the journalist eventually decided to leave. Yet her words suggest that what disappeared with her departure was not her passion for journalism, but the possibility of what she might have contributed had the conditions allowed her to stay.
That sense of loss is part of what the Kigali Declaration on the Elimination of Gender Violence in and through Media in Africa by 2034 is trying to prevent.
Led by African Women in Media (AWiM), the Declaration calls for action across the media ecosystem; from media organisations and professional associations to journalists, journalism educators, funders, digital platforms and regulators, to address gender violence both within media institutions and through the content they produce.
Its ambition builds on a problem that has been documented for years: for many women journalists across Africa, entering a newsroom is only the first step. Staying, progressing and practising journalism without discrimination, harassment or violence can prove to be another challenge altogether.
Entering journalism is not enough
In 2020, AWiM and Fojo Media Institute published Barriers to Women Journalists in Sub-Saharan Africa based on questionnaire responses from 125 women journalists across 17 African countries, alongside interviews and focus groups. Significantly, the research did not look only at women’s ability to enter journalism. It examined barriers to entering, progressing and staying in the profession.
The women who participated had entered journalism with strong ambitions. Passion, societal good and the desire to tell overlooked stories emerged prominently among their motivations.
One Kenyan journalist explained: ‘I loved the career and still do because I wanted to inform and highlight some issues affecting people in remote communities.’
Another participant described journalism as a way of telling ‘untold stories’ capable of influencing policy and improving people’s lives. Yet the professional environments encountered by women did not always nurture those ambitions.
The AWiM study identified job stagnation and salary disparities, gendered allocation of assignments, sexual harassment, bullying, sexism and racial discrimination, family responsibilities and unequal access to leadership among the barriers affecting women’s careers.
The research also documented how gendered expectations around family life could affect retention. Women spoke about the difficulty of reconciling journalism with childcare and family responsibilities, particularly when combined with poor pay and limited opportunities for progression.
The contrast is striking: women described entering journalism because they wanted to tell stories, serve communities and create change, while the structures of the profession could eventually make remaining within it difficult.
The question, therefore, is not simply whether women can become journalists. It is whether the conditions exist for them to remain journalists.
When leaving becomes an option
Macupe’s 2025 Reuters Institute paper brings that question into sharper focus. She interviewed ten Black African women with newsroom experience ranging from one year to more than 30 years in South Africa. One of the observations that troubled her most was generational: younger journalists described experiences echoing those of women who had entered the profession decades earlier.

deduped_items.summary: نناقش في الأسبوع الاقتصادي تخصيص الحكومة الفرنسية لـ64 مليار يورو لقطاع التعليم في موازنة العام المقبل، فيما تشهد البلاد احتجاجات عنيفة لطلاب المدارس الثانوية ، ما تفاصيل موازنة قطاع التعليم العام المقبل؟ وإلى أي مدى تلبي مطالب المحتجين؟ كما نتطرق إلى إرسال الرئيس الفرنسي جنودا ورادارات لحماية موقع ينبع النفطي السعودي، ما أسباب هذا الدعم؟ وما أهمية ينبع في تصدير النفط السعودي عبر البحر الأحمر؟ ونسلط الضوء على تحذير البنك الدولي من نقص الـمياه في تونس. فكيف ستتأثر الزراعة والاقتصاد التونسي؟

deduped_items.title: Directo a... Washington y el futuro de Christa Pike tras sobrevivir a inyecciones letales
deduped_items.summary: El futuro de Christa Pike sigue en discusión. deduped_items.title: Pope appoints Cardinal Gambetti as new Archbishop of Chieti-Vasto
deduped_items.summary: Pope Leo XIV has chosen the 60-year-old Cardinal from Bologna, a Conventual Franciscan, as the new shepherd of the archdiocese in Abruzzo, after accepting the resignation of Archbishop Bruno Forte, 77. Since February 2021, Gambetti has served as Vicar General of His Holiness for Vatican City, Archpriest of St. Peter’s Papal Basilica in the Vatican, and President of the Fabric of Saint Peter. Previously, from 2013 to 2020, he was Custos of the Sacred Convent of St. Francis in Assisi. Read all
deduped_items.body_text:
Pope appoints Cardinal Gambetti as new Archbishop of Chieti-Vasto
By Vatican News
Pope Leo XIV on Saturday appointed Cardinal Mauro Gambetti, 60, a Conventual Franciscan, as the new Archbishop of Chieti-Vasto, transferring him from his positions as Vicar General of His Holiness for Vatican City, Archpriest of St. Peterâs Papal Basilica in the Vatican, and President of the Fabric of Saint Peter.
He succeeds Archbishop Bruno Forte, 77, who submitted his resignation from the pastoral governance of the archdiocese due to the age limit.
Created a Cardinal by Pope Francis in November 2020, Gambetti was called on February 20, 2021, to take up his positions at the Vatican. Previously, from 2013 to 2020, he served as Custos of the Sacred Convent of St. Francis in Assisi.
Born on October 27, 1965, in Castel San Pietro Terme in Bologna, after obtaining a degree in mechanical engineering from the University of Bologna, Mauro Gambetti began his journey with the Order of Friars Minor Conventual in September 1992, making his final profession of vows in September 1998.
After obtaining a Bachelorâs degree in Theology from the Theological Institute of Assisi in Perugia, he earned a Licentiate in Theological Anthropology from the Central Italy Theological Faculty in Florence.
He was ordained a priest on January 8, 2000, in Longiano at the Convent of the Most Holy Crucifix. There, he served as director of youth and vocational ministry for Emilia-Romagna and, from 2005 to 2009, also served as guardian friar, responsible for and animator of the religious community.
In the spring of 2009, his fellow friars of the Bolognese Province of St. Anthony of Padua elected him Provincial Minister. Then, on February 22, 2013, the Orderâs Minister General called him to serve as General Custos of the General Custody of the Sacred Convent of St. Francis in Assisi for the four-year term from 2013 to 2017.
In 2017, he was reconfirmed as Custos of the Sacred Convent for the 2017â2021 term, a position he held until October 30, 2020, when he was assigned the titular see of Tisiduo with the personal title of Archbishop. He received episcopal consecration on November 22, 2020, at the Basilica of St. Francis in Assisi.
At the consistory of November 28, 2020, Pope Francis created and proclaimed him a Cardinal, assigning him the Deaconry of the Most Holy Name of Mary at the Trajan Forum.
Following his appointment, on February 29, 2021, as Vicar General of His Holiness for Vatican City, Archpriest of St. Peterâs Papal Basilica in the Vatican, and President of the Fabric of Saint Peter, Francis also appointed him in June 2023 as a judge of the Court of Cassation of the Vatican City State.
Cardinal Gambetti is a member of the Dicastery for Institutes of Consecrated Life and Societies of Apostolic Life.

Pope Leo XIV on Saturday appointed Cardinal Mauro Gambetti, 60, a Conventual Franciscan, as the new Archbishop of Chieti-Vasto, transferring him from his positions as Vicar General of His Holiness for Vatican City, Archpriest of St. Peterâs Papal Basilica in the Vatican, and President of the Fabric of Saint Peter.
He succeeds Archbishop Bruno Forte, 77, who submitted his resignation from the pastoral governance of the archdiocese due to the age limit.
Created a Cardinal by Pope Francis in November 2020, Gambetti was called on February 20, 2021, to take up his positions at the Vatican. Previously, from 2013 to 2020, he served as Custos of the Sacred Convent of St. Francis in Assisi.
Born on October 27, 1965, in Castel San Pietro Terme in Bologna, after obtaining a degree in mechanical engineering from the University of Bologna, Mauro Gambetti began his journey with the Order of Friars Minor Conventual in September 1992, making his final profession of vows in September 1998.
After obtaining a Bachelorâs degree in Theology from the Theological Institute of Assisi in Perugia, he earned a Licentiate in Theological Anthropology from the Central Italy Theological Faculty in Florence.
He was ordained a priest on January 8, 2000, in Longiano at the Convent of the Most Holy Crucifix. There, he served as director of youth and vocational ministry for Emilia-Romagna and, from 2005 to 2009, also served as guardian friar, responsible for and animator of the religious community.
In the spring of 2009, his fellow friars of the Bolognese Province of St. Anthony of Padua elected him Provincial Minister. Then, on February 22, 2013, the Orderâs Minister General called him to serve as General Custos of the General Custody of the Sacred Convent of St. Francis in Assisi for the four-year term from 2013 to 2017.
In 2017, he was reconfirmed as Custos of the Sacred Convent for the 2017â2021 term, a position he held until October 30, 2020, when he was assigned the titular see of Tisiduo with the personal title of Archbishop. He received episcopal consecration on November 22, 2020, at the Basilica of St. Francis in Assisi.
At the consistory of November 28, 2020, Pope Francis created and proclaimed him a Cardinal, assigning him the Deaconry of the Most Holy Name of Mary at the Trajan Forum.
Following his appointment, on February 29, 2021, as Vicar General of His Holiness for Vatican City, Archpriest of St. Peterâs Papal Basilica in the Vatican, and President of the Fabric of Saint Peter, Francis also appointed him in June 2023 as a judge of the Court of Cassation of the Vatican City State.
Cardinal Gambetti is a member of the Dicastery for Institutes of Consecrated Life and Societies of Apostolic Life.

deduped_items.summary: Pope Leo XIV has chosen the 60-year-old Cardinal from Bologna, a Conventual Franciscan, as the new shepherd of the archdiocese in Abruzzo, after accepting the resignation of Archbishop Bruno Forte, 77. Since February 2021, Gambetti has served as Vicar General of His Holiness for Vatican City, Archpriest of St. Peter’s Papal Basilica in the Vatican, and President of the Fabric of Saint Peter. Previously, from 2013 to 2020, he was Custos of the Sacred Convent of St. Francis in Assisi. Read all
deduped_items.body_text:
Pope appoints Cardinal Gambetti as new Archbishop of Chieti-Vasto
By Vatican News
Pope Leo XIV on Saturday appointed Cardinal Mauro Gambetti, 60, a Conventual Franciscan, as the new Archbishop of Chieti-Vasto, transferring him from his positions as Vicar General of His Holiness for Vatican City, Archpriest of St. Peterâs Papal Basilica in the Vatican, and President of the Fabric of Saint Peter.
He succeeds Archbishop Bruno Forte, 77, who submitted his resignation from the pastoral governance of the archdiocese due to the age limit.
Created a Cardinal by Pope Francis in November 2020, Gambetti was called on February 20, 2021, to take up his positions at the Vatican. Previously, from 2013 to 2020, he served as Custos of the Sacred Convent of St. Francis in Assisi.
Born on October 27, 1965, in Castel San Pietro Terme in Bologna, after obtaining a degree in mechanical engineering from the University of Bologna, Mauro Gambetti began his journey with the Order of Friars Minor Conventual in September 1992, making his final profession of vows in September 1998.
After obtaining a Bachelorâs degree in Theology from the Theological Institute of Assisi in Perugia, he earned a Licentiate in Theological Anthropology from the Central Italy Theological Faculty in Florence.
He was ordained a priest on January 8, 2000, in Longiano at the Convent of the Most Holy Crucifix. There, he served as director of youth and vocational ministry for Emilia-Romagna and, from 2005 to 2009, also served as guardian friar, responsible for and animator of the religious community.
In the spring of 2009, his fellow friars of the Bolognese Province of St. Anthony of Padua elected him Provincial Minister. Then, on February 22, 2013, the Orderâs Minister General called him to serve as General Custos of the General Custody of the Sacred Convent of St. Francis in Assisi for the four-year term from 2013 to 2017.
In 2017, he was reconfirmed as Custos of the Sacred Convent for the 2017â2021 term, a position he held until October 30, 2020, when he was assigned the titular see of Tisiduo with the personal title of Archbishop. He received episcopal consecration on November 22, 2020, at the Basilica of St. Francis in Assisi.
At the consistory of November 28, 2020, Pope Francis created and proclaimed him a Cardinal, assigning him the Deaconry of the Most Holy Name of Mary at the Trajan Forum.
Following his appointment, on February 29, 2021, as Vicar General of His Holiness for Vatican City, Archpriest of St. Peterâs Papal Basilica in the Vatican, and President of the Fabric of Saint Peter, Francis also appointed him in June 2023 as a judge of the Court of Cassation of the Vatican City State.
Cardinal Gambetti is a member of the Dicastery for Institutes of Consecrated Life and Societies of Apostolic Life.

Pope Leo XIV on Saturday appointed Cardinal Mauro Gambetti, 60, a Conventual Franciscan, as the new Archbishop of Chieti-Vasto, transferring him from his positions as Vicar General of His Holiness for Vatican City, Archpriest of St. Peterâs Papal Basilica in the Vatican, and President of the Fabric of Saint Peter.
He succeeds Archbishop Bruno Forte, 77, who submitted his resignation from the pastoral governance of the archdiocese due to the age limit.
Created a Cardinal by Pope Francis in November 2020, Gambetti was called on February 20, 2021, to take up his positions at the Vatican. Previously, from 2013 to 2020, he served as Custos of the Sacred Convent of St. Francis in Assisi.
Born on October 27, 1965, in Castel San Pietro Terme in Bologna, after obtaining a degree in mechanical engineering from the University of Bologna, Mauro Gambetti began his journey with the Order of Friars Minor Conventual in September 1992, making his final profession of vows in September 1998.
After obtaining a Bachelorâs degree in Theology from the Theological Institute of Assisi in Perugia, he earned a Licentiate in Theological Anthropology from the Central Italy Theological Faculty in Florence.
He was ordained a priest on January 8, 2000, in Longiano at the Convent of the Most Holy Crucifix. There, he served as director of youth and vocational ministry for Emilia-Romagna and, from 2005 to 2009, also served as guardian friar, responsible for and animator of the religious community.
In the spring of 2009, his fellow friars of the Bolognese Province of St. Anthony of Padua elected him Provincial Minister. Then, on February 22, 2013, the Orderâs Minister General called him to serve as General Custos of the General Custody of the Sacred Convent of St. Francis in Assisi for the four-year term from 2013 to 2017.
In 2017, he was reconfirmed as Custos of the Sacred Convent for the 2017â2021 term, a position he held until October 30, 2020, when he was assigned the titular see of Tisiduo with the personal title of Archbishop. He received episcopal consecration on November 22, 2020, at the Basilica of St. Francis in Assisi.
At the consistory of November 28, 2020, Pope Francis created and proclaimed him a Cardinal, assigning him the Deaconry of the Most Holy Name of Mary at the Trajan Forum.
Following his appointment, on February 29, 2021, as Vicar General of His Holiness for Vatican City, Archpriest of St. Peterâs Papal Basilica in the Vatican, and President of the Fabric of Saint Peter, Francis also appointed him in June 2023 as a judge of the Court of Cassation of the Vatican City State.
Cardinal Gambetti is a member of the Dicastery for Institutes of Consecrated Life and Societies of Apostolic Life.

deduped_items.body_text:
Pope appoints Cardinal Gambetti as new Archbishop of Chieti-Vasto
By Vatican News
Pope Leo XIV on Saturday appointed Cardinal Mauro Gambetti, 60, a Conventual Franciscan, as the new Archbishop of Chieti-Vasto, transferring him from his positions as Vicar General of His Holiness for Vatican City, Archpriest of St. Peterâs Papal Basilica in the Vatican, and President of the Fabric of Saint Peter.
He succeeds Archbishop Bruno Forte, 77, who submitted his resignation from the pastoral governance of the archdiocese due to the age limit.
Created a Cardinal by Pope Francis in November 2020, Gambetti was called on February 20, 2021, to take up his positions at the Vatican. Previously, from 2013 to 2020, he served as Custos of the Sacred Convent of St. Francis in Assisi.
Born on October 27, 1965, in Castel San Pietro Terme in Bologna, after obtaining a degree in mechanical engineering from the University of Bologna, Mauro Gambetti began his journey with the Order of Friars Minor Conventual in September 1992, making his final profession of vows in September 1998.
After obtaining a Bachelorâs degree in Theology from the Theological Institute of Assisi in Perugia, he earned a Licentiate in Theological Anthropology from the Central Italy Theological Faculty in Florence.
He was ordained a priest on January 8, 2000, in Longiano at the Convent of the Most Holy Crucifix. There, he served as director of youth and vocational ministry for Emilia-Romagna and, from 2005 to 2009, also served as guardian friar, responsible for and animator of the religious community.
In the spring of 2009, his fellow friars of the Bolognese Province of St. Anthony of Padua elected him Provincial Minister. Then, on February 22, 2013, the Orderâs Minister General called him to serve as General Custos of the General Custody of the Sacred Convent of St. Francis in Assisi for the four-year term from 2013 to 2017.
In 2017, he was reconfirmed as Custos of the Sacred Convent for the 2017â2021 term, a position he held until October 30, 2020, when he was assigned the titular see of Tisiduo with the personal title of Archbishop. He received episcopal consecration on November 22, 2020, at the Basilica of St. Francis in Assisi.
At the consistory of November 28, 2020, Pope Francis created and proclaimed him a Cardinal, assigning him the Deaconry of the Most Holy Name of Mary at the Trajan Forum.
Following his appointment, on February 29, 2021, as Vicar General of His Holiness for Vatican City, Archpriest of St. Peterâs Papal Basilica in the Vatican, and President of the Fabric of Saint Peter, Francis also appointed him in June 2023 as a judge of the Court of Cassation of the Vatican City State.
Cardinal Gambetti is a member of the Dicastery for Institutes of Consecrated Life and Societies of Apostolic Life.

deduped_items.summary: ALEXANDRIA, La. (RNS and Verite News) — Part of the Trump administration’s efforts to ramp up deportations, the facility — which will hold unaccompanied minors and families — is situated beside an airport that has become known as the country’s busiest hub for deportation flights.
